Text:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description

We formulate a MILP that jointly optimizes train rescheduling (arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting) and speed management (time-discretized speed profiles) for high-speed railway operations under a **partial segment blockage** disruption. A double-track line is considered where one direction (northbound) on a specific segment is blocked during a time window. Affected trains may be rerouted to the opposite track.

---

## 2. Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| A1 | The line is a **double-track** line with one track per direction. The disruption blocks the **northbound track** on segment $s^*$ during $[t_{\text{dis}}, t_{\text{end}}]$. |
| A2 | Time is **discretized** into intervals of duration $\Delta t$ (e.g., 30 s) for speed management. |
| A3 | **No overtaking** is permitted on any single segment (block-occupied system). |
| A4 | Energy consumption is approximated by a **piecewise-linear** function of the running time on each segment. |
| A5 | Only one rerouting option exists: use of the **opposite (southbound) track** on segment $s^*$. |
| A6 | The disruption is **partial** (one track blocked); the other track remains fully operational. |
| A7 | Minimum headway $h_{\min}$ applies between consecutive trains on the same track in the same direction. |
| A8 | A rerouted train on the opposite track must **not overlap in time** with trains in that direction (strict separation). |
| A9 | Each train traverses each segment in a **single contiguous** time window (no re-entry). |
| A10 | The planning horizon is $[0, T_{\max}]$ and all trains must complete their journey within it. |

---

## 3. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of all trains |
| $T^{\text{N}}$ | Set of northbound trains ($T^{\text{N}} \subset T$) |
| $T^{\text{S}}$ | Set of southbound trains ($T^{\text{S}} \subset T$) |
| $N = \{1,\dots,|N|\}$ | Set of stations ordered along the line |
| $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$ | Set of segments; segment $s$ connects station $n_s$ to $n_s+1$ |
| $s^*$ | The disrupted segment |
| $K = \{1,\dots,|K|\}$ | Set of time intervals; $|K| = T_{\max}/\Delta t$ |
| $K^{\text{dis}}$ | Set of interval indices overlapping the disruption window |
| $S_i$ | Set of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $P = \{1,\dots,P\}$ | Set of pieces in the piecewise-linear energy approximation |

---

## 4. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t^{\text{sched}}_{i,n}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $n$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ |
| $rt^{\min}_{i,s},\; rt^{\max}_{i,s}$ | Min/max running time for train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $v^{\max}_{s,k}$ | Speed limit on segment $s$ in interval $k$ |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration/deceleration ($m/s^2$) |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between same-direction trains on same track |
| $d_{\min}^{\text{dwell}}_{i,n}$ | Minimum dwell time for train $i$ at station $n$ |
| $t_{\text{dis}},\; t_{\text{end}}$ | Start/end of the disruption window |
| $C_{\text{reroute}}$ | Penalty cost for rerouting one train |
| $C_{\text{order}}$ | Penalty cost for one order change (overtaking) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective weights for delay, rerouting, energy, order changes |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (chosen as $T_{\max}$ for time, $v^{\max}_{\text{global}}$ for speed) |
| $\alpha_p,\;\beta_p$ | Slope and intercept of energy piece $p$ (linear function of $rt$) |
| $rt^{\min}_p,\; rt^{\max}_p$ | Running-time bounds for energy piece $p$ |
| $y^{\text{sched}}_{i,j,s}$ | Scheduled ordering: 1 if $i$ is before $j$ in the original timetable on segment $s$ |

---

## 5. Decision Variables

### 5.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,n}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $n$ |
| $d_{i,n}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $n$ |
| $rt_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $v_{i,s,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $s$ during interval $k$ |
| $e_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $z^+_{i},\; z^-_{i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Positive/negative deviation of train $i$'s terminal arrival from schedule |
| $u^{\text{acc}}_{i,s,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Auxiliary: speed increase (acceleration) |
| $u^{\text{dec}}_{i,s,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Auxiliary: speed decrease (deceleration) |
| $\lambda_{i,s,p}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Auxiliary: amount of running time in energy piece $p$ |

### 5.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is on segment $s$ during interval $k$ |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ before train $j$ (defined for $i<j$) |
| $r_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if northbound train $i$ is rerouted to the southbound track on $s^*$ |
| $o_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if the order of $i,j$ on segment $s$ differs from the scheduled order |
| $\theta_{i,s,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if the running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ falls in energy piece $p$ |
| $B_{i,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | For $i \in T^{\text{N}}, j \in T^{\text{S}}$: 1 if rerouted train $i$ clears segment $s^*$ before southbound train $j$ enters |

---

## 6. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in T} \left( z^+_i + z^-_i \right)
+ w_2 \sum_{i \in T^{\text{N}}} C_{\text{reroute}} \, r_i
+ w_3 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S_i} e_{i,s}
+ w_4 \sum_{\substack{i,j \in T \\ i < j}} \sum_{s \in S} o_{i,j,s} \, C_{\text{order}}
$$

**Terms:**
1. **Total delay**: absolute deviation of terminal arrival from schedule (linearized via $z^+, z^-$).
2. **Rerouting cost**: fixed penalty per rerouted train.
3. **Total energy**: sum of energy consumption over all train-segment pairs.
4. **Order changes**: penalty for each pair whose relative order changes from the timetable.

---

## 7. Constraints

### 7.1 Train Continuity and Timing

**(C1) Running time definition:**
$$
rt_{i,s} = a_{i,n_s+1} - d_{i,n_s} \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S_i
$$

**(C2) Running time bounds:**
$$
rt^{\min}_{i,s} \leq rt_{i,s} \leq rt^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S_i
$$

**(C3) Dwell time at stations:**
$$
d_{i,n} - a_{i,n} \geq d^{\text{dwell}}_{\min,i,n} \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; n \in N \setminus \{n_{\text{origin}}(i)\}
$$

**(C4) Horizon bounds:**
$$
0 \leq a_{i,n} \leq T_{\max}, \quad 0 \leq d_{i,n} \leq T_{\max} \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; n \in N
$$

**(C5) Link between traversal binary and times:**
If $x_{i,s,k} = 1$, the train must be in transit during interval $k$:
$$
d_{i,n_s} \leq k\,\Delta t + M(1 - x_{i,s,k}) \qquad \forall\, i, s, k
$$
$$
a_{i,n_s+1} \geq (k-1)\,\Delta t - M(1 - x_{i,s,k}) \qquad \forall\, i, s, k
$$

If $x_{i,s,k} = 0$, the train is not on the segment during interval $k$. This is enforced by the Big-M relaxation above; additionally:
$$
x_{i,s,k} \leq 1 - \frac{a_{i,n_s+1} - k\,\Delta t}{M} \qquad \text{(forces } x=0 \text{ if arrival before interval starts)}
$$
$$
x_{i,s,k} \leq 1 - \frac{(k-1)\,\Delta t - d_{i,n_s}}{M} \qquad \text{(forces } x=0 \text{ if departure after interval ends)}
$$

**(C6) Contiguity of traversal (A9):**
The set of intervals where $x_{i,s,k}=1$ must form a contiguous block. Enforced by:
$$
x_{i,s,k} - x_{i,s,k+1} \leq 1 - x_{i,s,k+2} + 1 \quad \text{(forbidden pattern } 1,0,1\text{)}
$$
A standard formulation:
$$
x_{i,s,k} \leq x_{i,s,k-1} + 1 - x_{i,s,k-2} \quad \text{is complex; we use:}
$$
$$
\sum_{k} x_{i,s,k} = \left\lceil \frac{rt_{i,s}}{\Delta t} \right\rceil
$$
Since the ceiling is non-linear, we relax to:
$$
\frac{rt_{i,s}}{\Delta t} - 1 \leq \sum_{k} x_{i,s,k} \leq \frac{rt_{i,s}}{\Delta t} + 1 \qquad \forall\, i, s
$$
And rely on the Big-M links (C5) to fix the exact window.

---

### 7.2 Speed Management

**(C7) Speed bounds:**
$$
0 \leq v_{i,s,k} \leq v^{\max}_{s,k} \qquad \forall\, i, s, k
$$

**(C8) Speed–traversal linkage:**
$$
v_{i,s,k} \leq v^{\max}_{s,k} \cdot x_{i,s,k} \qquad \forall\, i, s, k
$$

**(C9) Distance consistency (linking speed to segment length):**
The total distance covered equals the segment length:
$$
\sum_{k \in K} v_{i,s,k} \, \Delta t = L_s \qquad \forall\, i \in T,\; s \in S_i
$$
*(Since $v_{i,s,k}=0$ when $x_{i,s,k}=0$ by C8, this sum only counts active intervals.)*

**(C10) Acceleration/deceleration limits:**
For each train $i$, segment $s$, and $k = 1, \dots, |K|-1$:
$$
v_{i,s,k+1} - v_{i,s,k} = u^{\text{acc}}_{i,s,k} - u^{\text{dec}}_{i,s,k}
$$
$$
0 \leq u^{\text{acc}}_{i,s,k} \leq a_{\max} \, \Delta t \cdot x_{i,s,k} + a_{\max} \, \Delta t \cdot x_{i,s,k+1}
$$
$$
0 \leq u^{\text{dec}}_{i,s,k} \leq a_{\max} \, \Delta t \cdot x_{i,s,k} + a_{\max} \, \Delta t \cdot x_{i,s,k+1}
$$
*(If either interval is inactive, the speed change is unbounded/zero; the Big-M relaxation allows the transition.)*

A simpler and standard form:
$$
-a_{\max} \Delta t \leq v_{i,s,k+1} - v_{i,s,k} \leq a_{\max} \Delta t + M(1 - x_{i,s,k}) + M(1 - x_{i,s,k+1})
$$

---

### 7.3 Ordering and Headway Constraints

**(C11) Order completeness:**
For each pair $i < j$ and segment $s$ (where both trains traverse $s$):
$$
y_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$y_{i,j,s} = 1$ means $i$ traverses $s$ before $j$; $y_{i,j,s} = 0$ means $j$ before $i$.

**(C12) Headway enforcement via ordering (same direction, same track):**
For trains $i, j$ in the same direction on segment $s$:
$$
a_{i,n_s+1} + h_{\min} \leq a_{j,n_s+1} + M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall\, i < j, s
$$
$$
a_{j,n_s+1} + h_{\min} \leq a_{i,n_s+1} + M \, y_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall\, i < j, s
$$

**(C13) Order change detection:**
$$
o_{i,j,s} \geq y_{i,j,s} - y^{\text{sched}}_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall\, i < j, s
$$
$$
o_{i,j,s} \geq y^{\text{sched}}_{i,j,s} - y_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall\, i < j, s
$$
$$
0 \leq o_{i,j,s} \leq 1
$$

---

### 7.4 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

**(C14) Rerouting only for northbound trains on $s^*$:**
$$
r_i = 0 \qquad \forall\, i \in T^{\text{S}}
$$
$$
r_i \leq \sum_{k \in K^{\text{dis}}} x_{i,s^*,k} \qquad \forall\, i \in T^{\text{N}}
$$
*(If train $i$ does not traverse $s^*$ during the disruption window, it need not be rerouted.)*

**(C15) Northbound track blocked during disruption:**
For all northbound trains $i \in T^{\text{N}}$ and all intervals $k \in K^{\text{dis}}$:
$$
x_{i,s^*,k} \leq r_i \qquad \forall\, k \in K^{\text{dis}}
$$
**Interpretation:** If $r_i = 0$, the train cannot be on $s^*$ during the disruption window (northbound track is blocked). If $r_i = 1$, the train is permitted on $s^*$ but uses the **southbound track**.

**(C16) Rerouted train uses southbound track – conflict with southbound trains:**
For each pair $(i, j)$ with $i \in T^{\text{N}}, j \in T^{\text{S}}$ (both traversing $s^*$):

Define $B_{i,j} = 1$ if rerouted train $i$ exits $s^*$ before train $j$ enters.

Strict separation (no overlap on the southbound track):
$$
a_{i,n_{s^*}+1} + h_{\min} \leq d_{j,n_{s^*}} + M(1 - B_{i,j}) + M(1 - r_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in T^{\text{N}},\; j \in T^{\text{S}}
$$
$$
a_{j,n_{s^*}+1} + h_{\min} \leq d_{i,n_{s^*}} + M(1 - B_{i,j}) + M(1 - r_i) \qquad \forall\, i \in T^{\text{N}},\; j \in T^{\text{S}}
$$
*(The $M(1-r_i)$ term relaxes the constraint when train $i$ is NOT rerouted.)*

---

### 7.5 Conflict-Free Operation

**(C17) At most one train per track-segment per interval:**
For any two distinct trains $i \neq j$ on the same track and segment $s$, in interval $k$:

For northbound track (non-disrupted segments, or $s^*$ outside disruption window):
$$
x_{i,s,k}^{(N)} + x_{j,s,k}^{(N)} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, i,j \in T^{\text{N}},\; i \neq j,\; s,\; k
$$
where $x_{i,s,k}^{(N)} = x_{i,s,k}$ for non-$s^*$ segments, and for $s^*$ during $K^{\text{dis}}$, no northbound train uses the northbound track (C15).

For southbound track (including rerouted trains on $s^*$):
$$
x_{i,s,k}^{(S)} + x_{j,s,k}^{(S)} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, i,j \in T^{\text{S}} \cup \{r_i=1: i \in T^{\text{N}}\},\; s,\; k
$$
where $x_{i,s^*,k}^{(S)} = r_i \cdot x_{i,s^*,k}$ for $i \in T^{\text{N}}$ (rerouted), and $x_{i,s,k}^{(S)} = x_{i,s,k}$ for $i \in T^{\text{S}}$.

Linearized form for the southbound track on $s^*$:
$$
x_{i,s^*,k} + r_i \cdot x_{j,s^*,k} + r_j \cdot x_{i,s^*,k} \leq 1 + M\big(1 - r_i - r_j\big) \quad \text{(for mixed pairs)}
$$
More cleanly, for $i \in T^{\text{S}}, j \in T^{\text{N}}$:
$$
x_{i,s^*,k} + r_j \, x_{j,s^*,k} \leq 1 \qquad \forall\, i \in T^{\text{S}},\; j \in T^{\text{N}},\; k \in K^{\text{dis}}
$$
*(A southbound train and a rerouted northbound train cannot be on $s^*$ in the same interval.)*

---

### 7.6 Energy Model (Piecewise-Linear)

**(C18) Running time decomposition into pieces:**
$$
rt_{i,s} = \sum_{p=1}^{P} \lambda_{i,s,p} \qquad \forall\, i, s
$$
$$
0 \leq \lambda_{i,s,p} \leq (rt^{\max}_p - rt^{\min}_p) \, \theta_{i,s,p} \qquad \forall\, i, s, p
$$
$$
\sum_{p=1}^{P} \theta_{i,s,p} = 1 \qquad \forall\, i, s
$$
$$
\lambda_{i,s,p} \leq (rt^{\max}_p - rt^{\min}_p)\, \theta_{i,s,p-1} + (rt^{\max}_p - rt^{\min}_p)\, \theta_{i,s,p} \quad \text{(sequencing, simplified)}
$$
A standard convex PL formulation (since we minimize, only the $\geq$ constraint is needed):
$$
e_{i,s} \geq \sum_{p=1}^{P} \left( \alpha_p \, \lambda_{i,s,p} + \beta_p \, \theta_{i,s,p} \right) \qquad \forall\, i, s
$$
Since we minimize $e_{i,s}$, this tightens to equality at optimality.

**(C19) Energy non-negativity:**
$$
e_{i,s} \geq 0 \qquad \forall\, i, s
$$

---

### 7.7 Delay Linearization

**(C20) Absolute deviation at terminal station:**
Let $n^{\text{term}}(i)$ be the terminal station of train $i$:
$$
z^+_i \geq a_{i,n^{\text{term}}(i)} - t^{\text{sched}}_{i,n^{\text{term}}(i)}
$$
$$
z^-_i \geq t^{\text{sched}}_{i,n^{\text{term}}(i)} - a_{i,n^{\text{term}}(i)}
$$
$$
z^+_i \geq 0, \quad z^-_i \geq 0
$$

---

## 8. Model Summary

| Constraint Group | Key Constraints | Purpose |
|-----------------|----------------|---------|
| Timing & Continuity | C1–C6 | Link arrival/departure/running times; dwell; horizon |
| Speed Management | C7–C10 | Speed limits, distance consistency, accel/decel bounds |
| Ordering & Headway | C11–C13 | Enforce ordering, headway, detect order changes |
| Disruption & Rerouting | C14–C16 | Block northbound track; force rerouting; coordinate with SB trains |
| Conflict-Free | C17 | At most one train per track-segment-interval |
| Energy | C18–C19 | PL approximation of energy vs. running time |
| Delay | C20 | Linearize absolute deviation |

---

## 9. Complexity and Solution Notes

- **Variable count:** $O(|T||N| + |T||S||K| + |T|^2|S| + |T||S|P)$
- **Constraint count:** $O(|T||S||K| + |T|^2|S| + |T||S|P)$
- For large instances, the decomposition approach described in the paper (separating an IP for train interactions from individual train speed plans) is recommended, as the full MILP grows quadratically in the number of trains.

---

## 10. Remarks on Linearity

All constraints are linear. The key linearization techniques used are:
- **Big-M** for linking binary traversal variables to continuous time variables (C5, C10, C15, C16).
- **Piecewise-linear** approximation for the energy function (C18), avoiding the non-linear ratio $L_s / rt_{i,s}$.
- **Absolute value** linearization for delay (C20).
- The product $v_{i,s,k} \cdot x_{i,s,k}$ in C9 is handled implicitly: since $v_{i,s,k} \leq v^{\max} x_{i,s,k}$ (C8), when $x=0$, $v=0$, so the sum $\sum v \Delta t$ only counts active intervals, making C9 linear.

Text:
# Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

This document presents a complete, linear Mixed-Integer Linear Programming formulation for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem under partial segment blockage disruptions in high-speed railways. The model simultaneously optimizes train timetables (arrival/departure times, dwell times, running times), track assignments (rerouting), train orders, and speed profiles (via discrete speed levels affecting energy consumption) to minimize total operational cost.

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $K$ | Set of all trains, indexed by $k$. |
| $K_{dir1}$ | Set of trains traveling in Direction 1 (normally assigned to Track A). |
| $K_{dir2}$ | Set of trains traveling in Direction 2 (normally assigned to Track B). |
| $S = \{1, 2, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations in sequence, indexed by $j$. |
| $I = \{1, 2, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of segments, indexed by $i$ (segment $i$ connects station $i$ and $i+1$). |
| $i_d$ | Index of the disrupted segment (between station $i_d$ and $i_d+1$). |
| $P = \{1, 2, \dots, P_{max}\}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $p$. |
| $\Omega_A(i_d)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{k_1, k_2\} \subset K_{dir1}$ that may conflict on Track A at segment $i_d$. |
| $\Omega_B(i_d)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{k_1, k_2\} \subset (K_{dir1} \cup K_{dir2})$ that may conflict on Track B at segment $i_d$. |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $L_i$ | Length of segment $i$. |
| $v^p$ | Speed value for speed level $p \in P$, with $v^1 < v^2 < \dots < v^{P_{max}}$. |
| $E_{i,p}$ | Precomputed energy consumption for segment $i$ at speed level $p$. |
| $a^{sched}_{k,j}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $k$ at station $j$. |
| $d^{sched}_{k,j}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $k$ from station $j$. |
| $\tau^{min}_{k,j}$ | Minimum dwell time for train $k$ at station $j$. |
| $\tau^{max}_{k,j}$ | Maximum dwell time for train $k$ at station $j$. |
| $t^{min}_{k,i}$ | Minimum running time for train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $t^{max}_{k,i}$ | Maximum running time for train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $H^{min}_A$ | Minimum headway between trains on Track A. |
| $H^{min}_B$ | Minimum headway between trains on Track B. |
| $t_{dis\_start}$ | Start time of the disruption on segment $i_d$. |
| $t_{dis\_end}$ | End time of the disruption on segment $i_d$. |
| $T_{horizon}$ | Planning horizon (sufficiently large upper bound on all times). |
| $C_{delay}$ | Penalty weight per unit time of delay. |
| $C_{energy}$ | Penalty weight per unit of energy consumption. |
| $C_{cancel}$ | Penalty weight for cancelling a train. |
| $C_{reroute}$ | Penalty weight for rerouting a train to the opposite track. |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (Big-M), set to $T_{horizon}$. |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $a_{k,j} \ge 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $k$ at station $j$. |
| $d_{k,j} \ge 0$ | Actual departure time of train $k$ from station $j$. |
| $r_{k,i} \ge 0$ | Running time of train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $w_{k,j} \ge 0$ | Dwell time of train $k$ at station $j$. |
| $\delta^a_{k,j} \ge 0$ | Arrival delay of train $k$ at station $j$ (auxiliary). |
| $\delta^d_{k,j} \ge 0$ | Departure delay of train $k$ from station $j$ (auxiliary). |
| $E_{k,i} \ge 0$ | Energy consumption of train $k$ on segment $i$. |

### Binary Variables

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $c_k$ | 1 if train $k$ is cancelled, 0 otherwise. |
| $x_{k,i_d}^A$ | 1 if train $k \in K_{dir1}$ uses Track A on segment $i_d$, 0 otherwise. |
| $x_{k,i_d}^B$ | 1 if train $k \in K_{dir1}$ uses Track B on segment $i_d$, 0 otherwise. |
| $u_k$ | Disjunction variable for disruption timing: 1 if train $k$ uses Track A after the disruption ends, 0 if before it starts. |
| $s_{k,i,p}$ | 1 if train $k$ uses speed level $p$ on segment $i$, 0 otherwise. |
| $y^A_{k_1,k_2}$ | 1 if train $k_1$ precedes train $k_2$ on Track A at segment $i_d$, 0 otherwise. |
| $y^B_{k_1,k_2}$ | 1 if train $k_1$ precedes train $k_2$ on Track B at segment $i_d$, 0 otherwise. |

### Auxiliary Definition

For headway constraints on Track B at segment $i_d$, define the Track B usage indicator:
$$
b_k = \begin{cases} 
1 - c_k & \text{if } k \in K_{dir2} \\
x_{k,i_d}^B & \text{if } k \in K_{dir1}
\end{cases}
$$

---

## 4. Assumptions

1. **Single Disrupted Segment**: Only segment $i_d$ on Track A is partially blocked during $[t_{dis\_start}, t_{dis\_end}]$. Track B remains fully operational.
2. **Fixed Track Assignment Outside Disruption**: For all segments $i \neq i_d$, trains in $K_{dir1}$ use Track A and trains in $K_{dir2}$ use Track B. Rerouting is only possible on segment $i_d$.
3. **Discrete Speed Levels**: Trains operate at one of $P_{max}$ pre-defined discrete speed levels per segment. Running time and energy are linear functions of the selected speed level.
4. **Precomputed Energy**: Energy consumption $E_{i,p}$ is a constant for each segment-speed level pair, precomputed from train dynamics.
5. **Conflict Pairs**: Headway constraints are enforced only between trains that are consecutive in the original schedule or that could potentially conflict (defined by sets $\Omega_A(i_d)$ and $\Omega_B(i_d)$).
6. **No Overtaking on Non-Disrupted Segments**: Train order is fixed on all segments except $i_d$, where reordering is allowed via the $y$ variables.
7. **All Stations Are Stopping Stations**: Every train stops at every station.
8. **Planning Horizon**: All operations must be completed within $T_{horizon}$.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total operational cost comprising delay penalties, energy consumption, cancellation penalties, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\min \quad Z = C_{delay} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{j \in S} \left( \delta^a_{k,j} + \delta^d_{k,j} \right) + C_{energy} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{i \in I} E_{k,i} + C_{cancel} \sum_{k \in K} c_k + C_{reroute} \sum_{k \in K_{dir1}} x_{k,i_d}^B
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Cancellation Logic

If a train is cancelled, its times are forced to zero; otherwise, they are bounded by the planning horizon.

$$
a_{k,j} \le T_{horizon} \cdot (1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{1}
$$

$$
d_{k,j} \le T_{horizon} \cdot (1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{2}
$$

$$
a_{k,j} \ge 0, \quad d_{k,j} \ge 0 \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{3}
$$

### 6.2 Time Continuity

$$
d_{k,j} = a_{k,j} + w_{k,j} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \setminus \{N\} \tag{4}
$$

$$
a_{k,j+1} = d_{k,j} + r_{k,j} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \setminus \{N\} \tag{5}
$$

### 6.3 Dwell Time Bounds

$$
\tau^{min}_{k,j} \cdot (1 - c_k) \le w_{k,j} \le \tau^{max}_{k,j} \cdot (1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \setminus \{N\} \tag{6}
$$

### 6.4 Speed Level Selection

Each non-cancelled train selects exactly one speed level per segment.

$$
\sum_{p \in P} s_{k,i,p} = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k \in K, \forall i \in I \tag{7}
$$

### 6.5 Running Time from Speed Level

$$
r_{k,i} = \sum_{p \in P} \left( \frac{L_i}{v^p} \right) s_{k,i,p} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall i \in I \tag{8}
$$

### 6.6 Energy Consumption from Speed Level

$$
E_{k,i} = \sum_{p \in P} E_{i,p} \cdot s_{k,i,p} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall i \in I \tag{9}
$$

### 6.7 Running Time Bounds (Consistency)

$$
t^{min}_{k,i} \cdot (1 - c_k) \le r_{k,i} \le t^{max}_{k,i} \cdot (1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in K, \forall i \in I \tag{10}
$$

### 6.8 Delay Linearization

$$
\delta^a_{k,j} \ge a_{k,j} - a^{sched}_{k,j} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{11}
$$

$$
\delta^d_{k,j} \ge d_{k,j} - d^{sched}_{k,j} \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{12}
$$

$$
\delta^a_{k,j} \ge 0, \quad \delta^d_{k,j} \ge 0 \quad \forall k \in K, \forall j \in S \tag{13}
$$

### 6.9 Track Assignment on Disrupted Segment $i_d$

For trains in $K_{dir1}$, exactly one track must be selected if the train is operating.

$$
x_{k,i_d}^A + x_{k,i_d}^B = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k \in K_{dir1} \tag{14}
$$

### 6.10 Disruption Window Constraints (Track A)

If a train in $K_{dir1}$ uses Track A on segment $i_d$, it must either complete the segment before the disruption starts or begin the segment after the disruption ends.

$$
a_{k,i_d+1} \le t_{dis\_start} + M(1 - x_{k,i_d}^A) + M \cdot u_k \quad \forall k \in K_{dir1} \tag{15}
$$

$$
d_{k,i_d} \ge t_{dis\_end} - M(1 - x_{k,i_d}^A) - M(1 - u_k) \quad \forall k \in K_{dir1} \tag{16}
$$

**Verification**:
- If $x_{k,i_d}^A = 0$: Both constraints become inactive (Big-M terms dominate).
- If $x_{k,i_d}^A = 1$ and $u_k = 0$: Constraint (15) gives $a_{k,i_d+1} \le t_{dis\_start}$; constraint (16) is inactive.
- If $x_{k,i_d}^A = 1$ and $u_k = 1$: Constraint (15) is inactive; constraint (16) gives $d_{k,i_d} \ge t_{dis\_end}$.

### 6.11 Headway Constraints on Track A at Segment $i_d$

For each pair $\{k_1, k_2\} \in \Omega_A(i_d)$:

**Ordering Logic**:
$$
y^A_{k_1,k_2} + y^A_{k_2,k_1} \le 1 \tag{17}
$$

$$
y^A_{k_1,k_2} + y^A_{k_2,k_1} \ge x_{k_1,i_d}^A + x_{k_2,i_d}^A - 1 \tag{18}
$$

**Headway Enforcement**:
$$
d_{k_1,i_d} + H^{min}_A \le d_{k_2,i_d} + M(1 - y^A_{k_1,k_2}) + M(1 - x_{k_1,i_d}^A) + M(1 - x_{k_2,i_d}^A) \tag{19}
$$

$$
d_{k_2,i_d} + H^{min}_A \le d_{k_1,i_d} + M(1 - y^A_{k_2,k_1}) + M(1 - x_{k_1,i_d}^A) + M(1 - x_{k_2,i_d}^A) \tag{20}
$$

**Verification**: If both trains are on Track A ($x_{k_1}=x_{k_2}=1$), constraint (18) forces exactly one of $y^A_{k_1,k_2}$ or $y^A_{k_2,k_1}$ to be 1. The corresponding headway constraint is active; the other is relaxed by $M$. If either train is not on Track A, the $M(1-x)$ terms relax both headway constraints.

### 6.12 Headway Constraints on Track B at Segment $i_d$

For each pair $\{k_1, k_2\} \in \Omega_B(i_d)$:

**Ordering Logic**:
$$
y^B_{k_1,k_2} + y^B_{k_2,k_1} \le 1 \tag{21}
$$

$$
y^B_{k_1,k_2} + y^B_{k_2,k_1} \ge b_{k_1} + b_{k_2} - 1 \tag{22}
$$

**Headway Enforcement**:
$$
d_{k_1,i_d} + H^{min}_B \le d_{k_2,i_d} + M(1 - y^B_{k_1,k_2}) + M(1 - b_{k_1}) + M(1 - b_{k_2}) \tag{23}
$$

$$
d_{k_2,i_d} + H^{min}_B \le d_{k_1,i_d} + M(1 - y^B_{k_2,k_1}) + M(1 - b_{k_1}) + M(1 - b_{k_2}) \tag{24}
$$

**Verification**: If both trains are on Track B ($b_{k_1}=b_{k_2}=1$), constraint (22) forces exactly one ordering. The corresponding headway constraint is active. If either train is not on Track B, the $M(1-b)$ terms relax both headway constraints.

### 6.13 Headway Constraints on Non-Disrupted Segments

For all segments $i \in I \setminus \{i_d\}$, train order is fixed (no reordering). Let $\pi_A(i)$ denote the fixed order of $K_{dir1}$ trains on Track A for segment $i$, and $\pi_B(i)$ denote the fixed order of $K_{dir2}$ trains on Track B for segment $i$.

**Track A**:
$$
d_{k_1,i} + H^{min}_A \le d_{k_2,i} \quad \forall i \in I \setminus \{i_d\}, \forall (k_1, k_2) \text{ consecutive in } \pi_A(i) \tag{25}
$$

**Track B**:
$$
d_{k_1,i} + H^{min}_B \le d_{k_2,i} \quad \forall i \in I \setminus \{i_d\}, \forall (k_1, k_2) \text{ consecutive in } \pi_B(i) \tag{26}
$$

### 6.14 Variable Domains

$$
c_k, x_{k,i_d}^A, x_{k,i_d}^B, u_k, s_{k,i,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall k, i, p \tag{27}
$$

$$
y^A_{k_1,k_2}, y^B_{k_1,k_2} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \{k_1,k_2\} \in \Omega_A(i_d) \cup \Omega_B(i_d) \tag{28}
$$

$$
a_{k,j}, d_{k,j}, r_{k,i}, w_{k,j}, \delta^a_{k,j}, \delta^d_{k,j}, E_{k,i} \ge 0 \quad \forall k, j, i \tag{29}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Aspect | Treatment |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Rescheduling** | Arrival/departure times, dwell times, and running times are decision variables bounded by operational limits. |
| **Rerouting** | Binary variables $x_{k,i_d}^A, x_{k,i_d}^B$ allow $K_{dir1}$ trains to choose Track A or B on the disrupted segment. |
| **Disruption Logic** | Disjunctive constraints (15)-(16) ensure trains on Track A avoid the disruption window. |
| **Speed Management** | Discrete speed levels $P$ with linear running time and energy functions (8)-(9). |
| **Conflict Resolution** | Big-M headway constraints with ordering binaries on both tracks at the disrupted segment (17)-(24). |
| **Cancellation** | Binary $c_k$ with Big-M bounds zeroing out all times for cancelled trains (1)-(3). |
| **Objective** | Weighted sum of delay, energy, cancellation, and rerouting costs. |

The model is a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) with $O(|K| \cdot |S| + |K| \cdot |I| \cdot P_{max} + |\Omega_A| + |\Omega_B|)$ variables and constraints, solvable by standard MILP solvers (CPLEX, Gurobi, SCIP) for moderate instance sizes. For large-scale instances, the decomposition-based solution approach described in the paper can be applied.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages – Complete MILP Model

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

This Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model addresses the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** for a high-speed railway corridor experiencing a partial segment blockage. The model simultaneously optimizes train timetables (departure/arrival times, ordering, rerouting) and speed profiles (running times, energy consumption) to minimize total operational cost while ensuring a conflict-free schedule.

**Assumptions:**
1.  **Network:** A single linear corridor with $N$ stations indexed $i = 1, \dots, N$ from West to East. Segment $s$ connects station $s$ and $s+1$.
2.  **Directions:**
    *   **Direction A (Set $\mathcal{D}$):** Trains travel West $\to$ East ($i \to i+1$). Primarily use Track 1.
    *   **Direction B (Set $\mathcal{U}$):** Trains travel East $\to$ West ($i \to i-1$). Primarily use Track 2.
3.  **Disruption:** Track 1 is blocked for Direction A on segment $s_{dis} = (d, d+1)$ during the time interval $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.
4.  **Rerouting:** Direction A trains affected by the blockage may be rerouted to Track 2. This creates shared-track conflicts with Direction B trains.
5.  **Speed/Energy:** Energy consumption is modeled as a linear function of running time. Faster running (shorter time) increases energy consumption. The relationship is approximated by a single linear segment connecting the minimum energy point (max time) and maximum energy point (min time).
6.  **Headways:** Minimum separation times are enforced between trains on the same track. Cross-direction clearance is enforced on shared Track 2.
7.  **Cancellation:** Trains may be cancelled at a significant penalty. Cancelled trains do not occupy track resources.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\mathcal{N} = \{1, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations. |
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of segments. Segment $i$ connects station $i$ and $i+1$. |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of all trains, $\mathcal{K} = \mathcal{D} \cup \mathcal{U}$. |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains in Direction A (West $\to$ East). |
| $\mathcal{U} \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ | Set of trains in Direction B (East $\to$ West). |
| $P_{\mathcal{D}}$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{k, l\}$ of distinct trains from $\mathcal{D}$. |
| $P_{\mathcal{U}}$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{k, l\}$ of distinct trains from $\mathcal{U}$. |
| $P_{cross}$ | Set of pairs $(k, l)$ where $k \in \mathcal{D}, l \in \mathcal{U}$. |
| $I_k$ | Set of segments traversed by train $k$. |
| $d$ | Index of the disrupted segment. |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Start and end time of the disruption on segment $d$. |
| $o_k, dest_k$ | Origin and destination station of train $k$. |
| $arr^{sch}_{k, dest_k}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $k$ at its destination. |
| $T^{min}_{k,i}, T^{max}_{k,i}$ | Minimum and maximum running time for train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $E^{min}_{k,i}, E^{max}_{k,i}$ | Minimum and maximum energy consumption for train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $\gamma_{k,i}$ | Energy-speed coupling coefficient ($>0$). |
| $dwell^{min}_{k,i}, dwell^{max}_{k,i}$ | Minimum and maximum dwell time at station $i$ for train $k$. |
| $h_{same}$ | Minimum same-direction headway on the same track. |
| $h_{cross}$ | Minimum cross-direction clearance time on shared Track 2. |
| $w_{cancel}, w_{delay}, w_{energy}, w_{reorder}$ | Penalty weights for cancellation, delay, energy, and reordering. |
| $sch_{k,l}$ | Binary parameter: $1$ if train $k$ is scheduled before train $l$ on the disrupted segment in the original timetable, $0$ otherwise. |
| $T_{end}$ | Maximum time horizon. |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (Big-M). |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Binary Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $c_k$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k$ is cancelled, $0$ otherwise. $\forall k \in \mathcal{K}$. |
| $r_k$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k \in \mathcal{D}$ is rerouted to Track 2 for segment $d$, $0$ otherwise. Undefined/irrelevant for $k \in \mathcal{U}$. |
| $z^e_k$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k \in \mathcal{D}$ completes segment $d$ before $t_{start}$, $0$ otherwise. |
| $z^l_k$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k \in \mathcal{D}$ starts segment $d$ after $t_{end}$, $0$ otherwise. |
| $x_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k$ precedes train $l$ on Track 1 for segment $d$. $\forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}}$. |
| $x^2_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k$ precedes train $l$ on Track 2 (rerouted) for segment $d$. $\forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}}$. |
| $x^U_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if train $k$ precedes train $l$ on Track 2 for segment $d$. $\forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{U}}$. |
| $y_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | $1$ if rerouted train $k \in \mathcal{D}$ clears Track 2 before train $l \in \mathcal{U}$ enters. $\forall (k, l) \in P_{cross}$. |
| $q_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | Auxiliary: $1$ if both trains $k, l \in \mathcal{D}$ are active ($c_k=0, c_l=0$). |
| $p_{k,l}$ | $\{0, 1\}$ | Auxiliary: $1$ if $k$ is reordered relative to schedule AND both $k, l$ are active. |

### 4.2 Continuous Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $dep_{k,i}$ | $[0, T_{end}]$ | Departure time of train $k$ from station $i$. |
| $arr_{k,i}$ | $[0, T_{end}]$ | Arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$. |
| $run_{k,i}$ | $[T^{min}_{k,i}, T^{max}_{k,i}]$ | Running time of train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $en_{k,i}$ | $[0, E^{max}_{k,i}]$ | Energy consumption of train $k$ on segment $i$. |
| $dev^+_k$ | $[0, T_{end}]$ | Positive deviation (lateness) of train $k$ at destination. |
| $dev^-_k$ | $[0, T_{end}]$ | Negative deviation (earliness) of train $k$ at destination. |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost of cancellations, passenger delays, energy consumption, and ordering reversals:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{w_{cancel} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} c_k}_{\text{Cancellation}} + \underbrace{w_{delay} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} dev^+_k}_{\text{Delay}} + \underbrace{w_{energy} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i \in I_k} en_{k,i}}_{\text{Energy}} + \underbrace{w_{reorder} \sum_{\{k,l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}}} sch_{k,l} \cdot p_{k,l}}_{\text{Reordering}}
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Flow and Timing Constraints

**Direction A Trains ($k \in \mathcal{D}$):**
$$
arr_{k,i+1} = dep_{k,i} + run_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{1}
$$
$$
dep_{k,i} \geq arr_{k,i} + dwell^{min}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D}, \forall i \in \text{Intermediate}(k) \tag{2}
$$
$$
dep_{k,i} \leq arr_{k,i} + dwell^{max}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D}, \forall i \in \text{Intermediate}(k) \tag{3}
$$

**Direction B Trains ($k \in \mathcal{U}$):**
$$
arr_{k,i-1} = dep_{k,i} + run_{k,i-1} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{U}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{4}
$$
$$
dep_{k,i} \geq arr_{k,i} + dwell^{min}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{U}, \forall i \in \text{Intermediate}(k) \tag{5}
$$
$$
dep_{k,i} \leq arr_{k,i} + dwell^{max}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{U}, \forall i \in \text{Intermediate}(k) \tag{6}
$$

**Running Time Bounds:**
$$
T^{min}_{k,i} \leq run_{k,i} \leq T^{max}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{7}
$$

**Time Horizon Bounds:**
$$
0 \leq arr_{k,i} \leq T_{end}, \quad 0 \leq dep_{k,i} \leq T_{end} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \tag{8}
$$

### 6.2 Disruption and Rerouting Logic

**Rerouting Logic (Linking $z$ to $r$):**
If a Direction A train is not rerouted ($r_k=0$), it must pass the disrupted segment either entirely before the blockage starts or entirely after it ends.
$$
z^e_k + z^l_k \geq 1 - r_k \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D} \tag{9}
$$

**Definition of "Early" ($z^e_k = 1$):**
Train $k$ must arrive at station $d+1$ before $t_{start}$.
$$
arr_{k,d+1} \leq t_{start} + M(1 - z^e_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D} \tag{10}
$$
$$
arr_{k,d+1} \geq t_{start} - M z^e_k \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D} \tag{11}
$$

**Definition of "Late" ($z^l_k = 1$):**
Train $k$ must depart from station $d$ after $t_{end}$.
$$
dep_{k,d} \geq t_{end} - M(1 - z^l_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D} \tag{12}
$$
$$
dep_{k,d} \leq t_{end} + M z^l_k \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{D} \tag{13}
$$

### 6.3 Energy Consumption Model

Energy is positively correlated with speed (inversely with running time). The linear approximation bounds the energy from below, ensuring the solver selects the minimum feasible energy for a given running time.
$$
en_{k,i} \geq E^{min}_{k,i} + \gamma_{k,i} (T^{max}_{k,i} - run_{k,i}) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{14}
$$
$$
en_{k,i} \leq E^{max}_{k,i} \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{15}
$$
$$
en_{k,i} \geq 0 \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{16}
$$

### 6.4 Headway and Conflict Constraints

**A. Same-Direction on Track 1 (Direction A, Non-Rerouted)**
Active only if $r_k=0, r_l=0, c_k=0, c_l=0$.
$$
x_{k,l} + x_{l,k} = 1 \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{17}
$$
$$
dep_{l,d} \geq dep_{k,d} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x_{k,l}) + r_k + r_l + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{18}
$$
$$
dep_{k,d} \geq dep_{l,d} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x_{l,k}) + r_k + r_l + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{19}
$$

**B. Same-Direction on Track 2 (Rerouted Direction A)**
Active only if $r_k=1, r_l=1, c_k=0, c_l=0$.
$$
x^2_{k,l} + x^2_{l,k} = 1 \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{20}
$$
$$
dep_{l,d} \geq dep_{k,d} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x^2_{k,l}) + (1 - r_k) + (1 - r_l) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{21}
$$
$$
dep_{k,d} \geq dep_{l,d} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x^2_{l,k}) + (1 - r_k) + (1 - r_l) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{22}
$$

**C. Same-Direction on Track 2 (Direction B)**
Active if $c_k=0, c_l=0$.
$$
x^U_{k,l} + x^U_{l,k} = 1 \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{U}} \tag{23}
$$
$$
dep_{l,d+1} \geq dep_{k,d+1} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x^U_{k,l}) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{U}} \tag{24}
$$
$$
dep_{k,d+1} \geq dep_{l,d+1} + h_{same} - M \left( (1 - x^U_{l,k}) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{U}} \tag{25}
$$

**D. Cross-Direction on Track 2 (Rerouted A vs. B)**
Active if $r_k=1, c_k=0, c_l=0$.
$$
y_{k,l} + y_{l,k} = r_k \quad \forall (k, l) \in P_{cross} \tag{26}
$$
$$
dep_{l,d+1} \geq arr_{k,d+1} + h_{cross} - M \left( (1 - y_{k,l}) + (1 - r_k) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall (k, l) \in P_{cross} \tag{27}
$$
$$
dep_{k,d} \geq arr_{l,d} + h_{cross} - M \left( (1 - y_{l,k}) + (1 - r_k) + c_k + c_l \right) \quad \forall (k, l) \in P_{cross} \tag{28}
$$

### 6.5 Cancellation Logic

If a train is cancelled, its time and energy variables are forced to zero to prevent false conflicts.
$$
dep_{k,i} \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \tag{29}
$$
$$
arr_{k,i} \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \tag{30}
$$
$$
run_{k,i} \leq T^{max}_{k,i}(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{31}
$$
$$
en_{k,i} \leq E^{max}_{k,i}(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K}, \forall i \in I_k \tag{32}
$$
$$
dev^+_k \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{33}
$$
$$
dev^-_k \leq M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{34}
$$

**Delay Deviation Logic:**
$$
dev^+_k + dev^-_k \geq arr_{k,dest_k} - arr^{sch}_{k,dest_k} - M c_k \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{35}
$$
$$
dev^+_k + dev^-_k \geq arr^{sch}_{k,dest_k} - arr_{k,dest_k} - M c_k \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{36}
$$
$$
dev^+_k \geq 0, \quad dev^-_k \geq 0 \quad \forall k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{37}
$$

### 6.6 Reorder Penalty Linearization

**Step 1: Auxiliary $q_{k,l}$ (Both Active)**
$$
q_{k,l} \leq 1 - c_k \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{38}
$$
$$
q_{k,l} \leq 1 - c_l \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{39}
$$
$$
q_{k,l} \geq 1 - c_k - c_l \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{40}
$$
$$
q_{k,l} \geq 0 \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{41}
$$

**Step 2: Auxiliary $p_{k,l}$ (Reordered AND Both Active)**
Linearizes $p_{k,l} = (1 - x_{k,l}) \cdot q_{k,l}$.
$$
p_{k,l} \leq 1 - x_{k,l} \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{42}
$$
$$
p_{k,l} \leq q_{k,l} \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{43}
$$
$$
p_{k,l} \geq q_{k,l} - x_{k,l} \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{44}
$$
$$
p_{k,l} \geq 0 \quad \forall \{k, l\} \in P_{\mathcal{D}} \tag{45}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

*   **Variables:** Binary ($c, r, z^e, z^l, x, x^2, x^U, y, q, p$) and Continuous ($dep, arr, run, en, dev^+, dev^-$).
*   **Objective:** Minimize weighted sum of cancellation penalties, arrival delays, energy consumption, and schedule reordering penalties.
*   **Constraints:**
    *   **Flow/Timing:** Links departure, arrival, and running times (1-8).
    *   **Disruption:** Enforces rerouting or timing avoidance of the blocked segment (9-13).
    *   **Energy:** Linearized energy-speed trade-off (14-16).
    *   **Conflicts:** Same-direction and cross-direction headways on shared infrastructure (17-28).
    *   **Cancellation:** Zeroing of variables for cancelled trains and handling of delay deviations (29-37).
    *   **Linearization:** Auxiliary binaries for non-linear reorder penalty terms (38-45).

This model is a fully linear MILP suitable for solution by standard optimization solvers.

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

This document presents a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model for Conflict Detection and Resolution (CDR) in railway networks utilizing Distance-to-Go (DTG) signalling systems (specifically ETCS Level 2 with Trackside Train Detection). The model is an enhancement of the RECIFE-MILP framework, incorporating speed-dependent separation distances and braking curve supervision.

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem Statement:**
Given a railway network, a reference timetable, and a set of delayed trains/events, determine a new feasible timetable (rescheduling) that resolves all track conflicts while minimizing the total weighted delay of all trains. The model must account for DTG signalling constraints, where train separation is not fixed by block length but is determined by the train's speed and braking distance.

**Key Assumptions:**
1.  **Network Structure:** The network is modeled as a directed graph $G=(N, A)$, where $N$ is the set of nodes (track sections, platforms, switches) and $A$ is the set of arcs (connections).
2.  **Discretization of Speed Profiles:** Although DTG allows continuous speed profiles, for MILP tractability, we assume a finite set of discrete speed profile options $\Omega$ available for each train on each arc. This is a standard assumption in enhanced RECIFE models to linearize speed-dependent constraints.
3.  **Braking Distance Function:** The braking distance $d_{brake}(v_{start}, v_{end})$ is a known, non-linear function of initial speed $v_{start}$ and target speed $v_{end}$. To maintain linearity, we pre-calculate the minimum required separation distance $S_{min}(p, q)$ for every pair of speed profile options $p \in \Omega_i$ and $q \in \Omega_j$ for trains $i$ and $j$ on conflicting arcs.
4.  **Conflict Definition:** A conflict occurs if two trains occupy the same track resource (block/section) at overlapping times, violating the minimum separation distance required by DTG rules.
5.  **Ordering:** The relative order of trains on any arc is fixed (no overtaking) or determined by binary variables. For simplicity in this formulation, we assume the relative order is fixed based on the reference timetable, but the model structure allows for reordering via binary variables if extended. *Note: Standard RECIFE fixes order; this model assumes fixed order to focus on the DTG separation enhancement, but includes binary variables for platform usage if applicable.*
6.  **Objective:** Minimize the sum of weighted delays for all trains at their final destinations.
7.  **Time Horizon:** The planning horizon is $T$.

## 2. Sets and Indices

*   $I$: Set of trains.
*   $J$: Set of nodes (locations/blocks/sections).
*   $A$: Set of arcs (track segments between nodes).
*   $K_i$: Set of nodes visited by train $i$ in chronological order.
*   $\Omega_i$: Set of feasible speed profile options for train $i$.
*   $P$: Set of platforms (subset of nodes $J$).
*   $S_{conflict}$: Set of pairs of trains $(i, j)$ that potentially conflict on shared resources.
*   $t$: Time index (discrete time steps, e.g., seconds or minutes).

## 3. Parameters

*   $T$: Planning horizon.
*   $w_i$: Weight for train $i$ (priority factor).
*   $t_{ref, i, k}$: Reference arrival time of train $i$ at node $k$.
*   $t_{dep, i, k}$: Reference departure time of train $i$ from node $k$.
*   $d_{min}(p, q)$: Minimum separation distance required between a train using speed profile $p$ and a following train using speed profile $q$ on a specific arc. This value is derived from braking curves: $d_{min} = d_{brake}(v_p) + \text{safety\_margin}$.
*   $v_{arc, p}$: Average speed or characteristic speed for speed profile $p$ on a given arc.
*   $L_{arc}$: Length of the arc.
*   $M$: Large constant (Big-M) for linearization.
*   $\tau_{i, k}$: Minimum dwell time for train $i$ at node $k$ (0 for non-platforms).

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables
*   $x_{i, k} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Arrival time of train $i$ at node $k$.
*   $y_{i, k} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Departure time of train $i$ from node $k$.
*   $z_{i, k} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Delay of train $i$ at node $k$ relative to the reference timetable.
    *   $z_{i, k} \ge x_{i, k} - t_{ref, i, k}$

### Binary Variables
*   $u_{i, k} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $i$ selects speed profile option $k \in \Omega_i$ for its movement. *Note: For simplicity, we assume one speed profile choice per train segment or per train. Let's refine: Let $u_{i, a, p} \in \{0, 1\}$ be 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on arc $a$.*
    *   To keep the model compact, let's assume the speed profile choice determines the travel time and the separation requirement. Let $u_{i, p} \in \{0, 1\}$ denote that train $i$ adopts speed profile $p$ globally (or per segment if indexed). Let's use $u_{i, a, p}$ for precision.
*   $o_{i, j, a} \in \{0, 1\}$: Ordering variable. Equals 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on arc $a$. (Assuming fixed order in this specific linearization for clarity, but included for completeness if reordering is allowed. If order is fixed, $o_{i,j,a}$ is a parameter). *Assumption: Order is fixed as per reference timetable to reduce complexity, focusing on the DTG separation logic.*
*   $s_{i, j, a} \in \{0, 1\}$: Conflict indicator variable. Equals 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ conflict on arc $a$. (Optional, often implied by constraints).

*Refined Variable Set for DTG Specifics:*
To handle the speed-dependent separation, we need to link the time difference to the speed choices.

Let:
*   $x_{i, k}$: Arrival time of train $i$ at node $k$.
*   $y_{i, k}$: Departure time of train $i$ from node $k$.
*   $u_{i, a, p} \in \{0, 1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on arc $a$.
*   $d_{i, k}$: Delay of train $i$ at node $k$.

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted delay of all trains at their final destinations (or sum of delays at all nodes, weighted by importance).

$$
\text{Minimize } Z = \sum_{i \in I} w_i \cdot d_{i, |K_i|}
$$

Where $|K_i|$ is the last node for train $i$. Alternatively, sum over all nodes:
$$
\text{Minimize } Z = \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K_i} w_{i,k} \cdot d_{i, k}
$$

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1. Delay Definition
For each train $i$ and node $k$:
$$
d_{i, k} \ge x_{i, k} - t_{ref, i, k}
$$
$$
d_{i, k} \ge 0
$$

### 6.2. Flow and Timing Constraints
For each train $i$ and consecutive nodes $k, k+1$ in $K_i$ (connected by arc $a$):

1.  **Departure after Arrival:**
    $$
    y_{i, k} \ge x_{i, k} + \tau_{i, k}
    $$

2.  **Travel Time Linkage (Speed Profile Selection):**
    The travel time from $k$ to $k+1$ depends on the selected speed profile $p$.
    Let $tt_{i, a, p}$ be the pre-calculated travel time for train $i$ on arc $a$ using speed profile $p$.
    
    $$
    x_{i, k+1} \ge y_{i, k} + \sum_{p \in \Omega_i} tt_{i, a, p} \cdot u_{i, a, p}
    $$

3.  **Speed Profile Uniqueness:**
    Exactly one speed profile is selected per train per arc:
    $$
    \sum_{p \in \Omega_i} u_{i, a, p} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I, a \in A_i
    $$

### 6.3. DTG Separation Constraints (The Core Enhancement)

This is the critical part distinguishing DTG from fixed-block. In fixed-block, the separation is constant (block length). In DTG, the separation depends on the speed of the leading train and the braking capability of the following train.

Consider two trains $i$ (leading) and $j$ (following) on the same arc $a$.
Let $x_{i, k}$ and $x_{j, k}$ be the arrival times at the start of the arc (or entry point).
Let $y_{i, k}$ and $y_{j, k}$ be the departure times from the start of the arc.

The constraint ensures that train $j$ does not enter the arc until train $i$ has cleared the "braking zone" required for safe separation.

**Linearized Separation Constraint:**
The minimum time headway $\Delta t_{min}$ between the departure of train $i$ and the departure of train $j$ is not constant; it depends on the speed profiles $p$ chosen by $i$ and $q$ chosen by $j$.

Let $H_{p, q}$ be the minimum time headway required between train $i$ (profile $p$) and train $j$ (profile $q$) on arc $a$.
$H_{p, q}$ is calculated as:
$$
H_{p, q} = \frac{d_{min}(p, q)}{v_{avg, p}} + \text{reaction\_time}
$$
*(Note: $d_{min}$ is the distance-based separation, converted to time headway based on the speed of the leading train or a conservative average speed. In a rigorous model, this is often handled via spatial constraints, but for a linear time-based MILP, we use time headways derived from the braking curves.)*

To linearize the dependency on $u_{i, a, p}$ and $u_{j, a, q}$, we use the Big-M method or a disjunctive formulation. Since the order is fixed ($i$ before $j$), we can write:

$$
y_{j, k} \ge y_{i, k} + \sum_{p \in \Omega_i} \sum_{q \in \Omega_j} H_{p, q} \cdot u_{i, a, p} \cdot u_{j, a, q}
$$

**Linearization of the Product Term:**
The term $u_{i, a, p} \cdot u_{j, a, q}$ is non-linear. We introduce auxiliary binary variables $w_{i, j, a, p, q} \in \{0, 1\}$ such that:
$$
w_{i, j, a, p, q} = 1 \iff u_{i, a, p} = 1 \text{ AND } u_{j, a, q} = 1
$$

Constraints for $w$:
1.  $w_{i, j, a, p, q} \le u_{i, a, p}$
2.  $w_{i, j, a, p, q} \le u_{j, a, q}$
3.  $w_{i, j, a, p, q} \ge u_{i, a, p} + u_{j, a, q} - 1$
4.  $w_{i, j, a, p, q} \ge 0$

Now, the separation constraint becomes linear:
$$
y_{j, k} \ge y_{i, k} + \sum_{p \in \Omega_i} \sum_{q \in \Omega_j} H_{p, q} \cdot w_{i, j, a, p, q}
$$

**Note on Spatial vs. Temporal:**
The above constraint is a *time-based* approximation of the spatial DTG constraint. A more accurate spatial constraint would involve the position $pos(t)$. However, for a MILP based on arrival/departure times, the time-headway approach using pre-calculated $H_{p,q}$ is the standard linearization technique for DTG in CDR models (as suggested by the "speed profile options" enhancement mentioned in the prompt).

### 6.4. Platform Capacity Constraints (If applicable)
If multiple trains can be at the same platform but must not overlap in time:
For any two trains $i, j$ at platform $k$:
$$
y_{i, k} \le x_{j, k} \quad \text{OR} \quad y_{j, k} \le x_{i, k}
$$
This is typically handled with binary ordering variables if platform order is not fixed. If order is fixed:
$$
y_{i, k} \le x_{j, k}
$$

### 6.5. Boundary Conditions
*   $x_{i, k} \ge 0$
*   $y_{i, k} \le T$
*   $x_{i, k} \le T$

## 7. Summary of the Model Structure

1.  **Variables:**
    *   Continuous: Arrival times $x$, Departure times $y$, Delays $d$.
    *   Binary: Speed profile selection $u$, Interaction indicators $w$.

2.  **Objective:**
    *   Minimize $\sum w_i d_{i, final}$.

3.  **Constraints:**
    *   **Timing:** Departure $\ge$ Arrival + Dwell.
    *   **Travel Time:** Next Arrival $\ge$ Current Departure + Travel Time(selected profile).
    *   **Profile Selection:** Sum of profile binaries = 1.
    *   **DTG Separation:** Following Train Departure $\ge$ Leading Train Departure + Headway(selected profiles).
    *   **Linearization:** Auxiliary variables $w$ to handle the product of speed profile binaries in the headway calculation.

## 8. Discussion of DTG Specifics in this Model

*   **Speed-Dependent Separation:** The parameter $H_{p, q}$ captures the physics of DTG. If train $i$ travels fast ($p$ is high speed), its braking distance is long. If train $j$ approaches, the required separation $d_{min}$ increases. This increases $H_{p, q}$.
*   **Brake Indication Points:** By linking the separation to the speed profile, the model implicitly ensures that the "brake indication point" for train $j$ is located far enough back from train $i$'s position to allow a safe stop. In a fixed-block model, this separation would be constant (block length), regardless of speed.
*   **Linearity:** The model remains linear because the non-linear physics (braking curves) are pre-processed into the parameters $tt_{i, a, p}$ and $H_{p, q}$. The optimization only decides *which* discrete profile to use and *when* to arrive/depart.

## 9. Assumptions Marked

*   **A1:** Speed profiles are discrete options $\Omega_i$. (Reasonable for MILP, approximates continuous control).
*   **A2:** Train order is fixed. (Simplifies the model; reordering can be added with additional binary variables and Big-M constraints).
*   **A3:** Time-headway approximation for spatial separation. (Standard in time-based CDR models; a spatial model would require continuous position variables, making it non-linear or much larger).
*   **A4:** Homogeneous track characteristics per arc. (Braking parameters $H_{p,q}$ are constant per arc).

(2023a) to include **flexible train composition** and **rolling stock circulation** alongside time-vary passenger demands, the following Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is formulated.

### 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem Statement:**
The objective is to formulate a real-time train rescheduling model for a single urban rail line. The model determines the optimal departure and arrival times, train compositions (number of cars), and rolling stock circulation (which physical train unit runs which service) to minimize total operational costs and passenger waiting times, subject to infrastructure and operational constraints.

**Assumptions:**
1.  **Line Structure:** The line consists of $N$ stations indexed by $i = 1, \dots, N$.
2.  **Time Horizon:** The scheduling horizon is divided into $T$ discrete time intervals (or steps) indexed by $t = 1, \dots, T$. The length of each interval is $\Delta t$.
3.  **Trains and Services:**
    *   There is a set of potential train services $K$, indexed by $k$.
    *   There is a set of physical rolling stock units (trains) $U$, indexed by $u$.
    *   **Flexible Composition:** A train can operate with a variable number of cars, $c_{k,t} \in \{1, 2, \dots, C_{max}\}$, where $C_{max}$ is the maximum number of cars.
4.  **Passenger Demands:**
    *   Passenger demand is time-varying and sectional.
    *   $D_{i,j,t}$ is the number of passengers wishing to travel from station $i$ to station $j$ during time interval $t$.
    *   Passengers wait at station $i$ until a train arrives that has sufficient capacity for their journey (or they board if capacity allows).
5.  **Capacity:** The capacity of a train with $c$ cars is $Cap(c) = c \times Cap_{unit}$, where $Cap_{unit}$ is the capacity of a single car.
6.  **Operational Constraints:**
    *   Minimum headway between consecutive trains at any station.
    *   Minimum/Maximum running time and dwell time.
    *   Rolling stock continuity: A physical train unit $u$ must follow a continuous path (it cannot teleport between non-adjacent services).
7.  **Linearity:** To maintain linearity, running times are assumed to be fixed or linearly dependent on the number of stops (stop-skipping is excluded for simplicity in this base model, focusing on composition and circulation as per the "flexible train composition" contribution). *Note: The input mentions "stop-skipping" in literature review but the specific contribution focuses on composition and circulation. We assume fixed stopping patterns for all trains to ensure linearity, or that running time is a constant $R_{k}$ for service $k$.*

### 2. Decision Variables

**Binary Variables:**
*   $x_{k,u,t} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if physical train unit $u$ is assigned to service $k$ during time interval $t$ (or if service $k$ is operated by unit $u$). *Assumption: Since composition can change, we link unit $u$ to service $k$.*
*   $y_{k,t} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if service $k$ is operated (active) in time interval $t$.
*   $z_{i,k,t} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if service $k$ stops at station $i$ in time interval $t$. *(Assumption: Fixed stopping pattern implies $z_{i,k}$ is constant, but we include it for generality if stop-skipping were allowed. For strict linearity with fixed patterns, $z_{i,k}$ is a parameter. We assume fixed patterns here to simplify, so $z_{i,k}$ is a parameter.)* -> **Correction:** The prompt asks for a model based on the input. The input highlights "flexible train composition" and "rolling stock circulation". It does not explicitly highlight "flexible stopping patterns" as the *new* contribution in the specific paper described, but rather extends Liu et al. (2023a). Liu et al. (2023a) likely had fixed stops. We will assume **fixed stopping patterns** ($z_{i,k}$ is a parameter) to ensure the model remains a standard MILP without complex stop-skipping logic, focusing on the requested composition and circulation.

**Integer Variables:**
*   $c_{k,t} \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: The number of cars used for service $k$ in time interval $t$.
    *   Constraint: $1 \le c_{k,t} \le C_{max}$.

**Continuous Variables:**
*   $A_{i,k,t}$: Arrival time of service $k$ at station $i$ in interval $t$.
*   $D_{i,k,t}$: Departure time of service $k$ from station $i$ in interval $t$.
*   $W_{i,t}$: Number of passengers waiting at station $i$ at the end of time interval $t$.
*   $B_{i,k,t}$: Number of passengers boarding service $k$ at station $i$ in interval $t$.
*   $Al_{i,k,t}$: Number of passengers alighting from service $k$ at station $i$ in interval $t$.

### 3. Objective Function

The objective is to minimize the sum of operational costs (energy/proportional to train length) and passenger waiting costs.

$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{t \in T} \left( C_{op} \cdot c_{k,t} \cdot y_{k,t} \right) + \sum_{i \in N} \sum_{t \in T} \left( C_{wait} \cdot W_{i,t} \right)
$$

Where:
*   $C_{op}$: Operational cost per car per time interval (proxy for energy/maintenance).
*   $C_{wait}$: Cost weight per passenger waiting unit.
*   $y_{k,t}$: Ensures we only pay for active services.

### 4. Constraints

#### 4.1. Train Operation and Timing Constraints

**1. Service Activity Link:**
A service is active only if it is assigned a train unit.
$$
y_{k,t} = \sum_{u \in U} x_{k,u,t} \quad \forall k, t
$$
*(Note: Assuming 1-to-1 mapping between active service and unit in a given interval for simplicity, or $\sum x \le 1$ and $y \ge x$. Let's use $y_{k,t} \ge x_{k,u,t}$ and $y_{k,t} \le \sum x_{k,u,t}$)*.

**2. Departure and Arrival Times:**
Departure time at station $i$ is arrival time plus dwell time.
$$
D_{i,k,t} = A_{i,k,t} + \delta_{i,k} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$
Where $\delta_{i,k}$ is the fixed dwell time for service $k$ at station $i$.

**3. Running Time:**
Arrival time at station $i+1$ is departure time at station $i$ plus running time.
$$
A_{i+1,k,t} = D_{i,k,t} + R_{i,i+1,k} \quad \forall i < N, k, t
$$
Where $R_{i,i+1,k}$ is the fixed running time between station $i$ and $i+1$ for service $k$.

**4. Headway Constraints:**
Minimum time gap between consecutive trains at any station. Let $k'$ be the train immediately preceding $k$ in the timetable order at station $i$.
$$
D_{i,k,t} - D_{i,k',t} \ge H_{min} \quad \forall i, k, k'
$$
*(Simplification for MILP: If train order is fixed, this is linear. If order is variable, big-M constraints are needed. We assume fixed train order for the base model.)*

**5. Time Bounds:**
$$
T_{start} \le A_{i,k,t} \le T_{end} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

#### 4.2. Rolling Stock Circulation Constraints

**1. Unit Assignment:**
Each active service must be assigned exactly one physical unit.
$$
\sum_{u \in U} x_{k,u,t} = y_{k,t} \quad \forall k, t
$$

**2. Unit Continuity (Circulation):**
A physical unit $u$ cannot perform two services simultaneously.
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{k,u,t} \le 1 \quad \forall u, t
$$

**3. Turnaround/Connection:**
If unit $u$ finishes service $k_1$ at station $i$ and starts service $k_2$ at station $j$, the time gap must allow for turnaround.
$$
D_{i,k_1,t} + T_{turn} \le A_{j,k_2,t'} \quad \text{if } x_{k_1,u,t}=1 \text{ and } x_{k_2,u,t'}=1
$$
*Linearized Form (Big-M):*
$$
A_{j,k_2,t'} - D_{i,k_1,t} \ge T_{turn} - M(2 - x_{k_1,u,t} - x_{k_2,u,t'}) \quad \forall k_1, k_2, u, t, t'
$$

#### 4.3. Passenger Flow and Capacity Constraints

**1. Passenger Balance at Station $i$:**
The number of waiting passengers at the end of interval $t$ is the previous waiting passengers plus new demand minus those who boarded.
$$
W_{i,t} = W_{i,t-1} + D^{demand}_{i,t} - \sum_{k \in K} B_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i, t
$$
*Assumption:* $D^{demand}_{i,t}$ is the total demand arriving at station $i$ in interval $t$ (aggregated over all destinations).

**2. Boarding Capacity Limit:**
Passengers can only board if there is available capacity.
$$
B_{i,k,t} \le Cap(c_{k,t}) - Load_{i,k,t} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$
*Note:* $Load_{i,k,t}$ is the number of passengers already on train $k$ upon arriving at station $i$.
$$
Load_{i,k,t} = \sum_{j < i} (B_{j,k,t} - Al_{j,k,t}) \quad \text{(Simplified)}
$$
To keep it linear and simple, we assume passengers board in order of destination or use a simplified capacity check:
$$
\sum_{j \in Dest(i)} B_{i,j,k,t} \le Cap(c_{k,t}) \quad \forall i, k, t
$$
*(Refined Linear Capacity Constraint):*
Let $P_{k,t}$ be the total load on train $k$ at the start of interval $t$ (after previous stations).
$$
\sum_{i \in N} B_{i,k,t} \le Cap(c_{k,t}) \quad \forall k, t
$$
*This is an approximation. A more rigorous flow conservation:*
$$
\sum_{j \in Dest(i)} B_{i,j,k,t} \le Cap(c_{k,t}) - \sum_{h < i} \sum_{j \in Dest(h)} (B_{h,j,k,t} - Al_{h,j,k,t})
$$

**3. Alighting:**
Passengers alight at their destination.
$$
Al_{i,k,t} = \sum_{j < i} B_{j,i,k,t} \quad \forall i, k, t
$$

**4. Non-negativity:**
$$
W_{i,t} \ge 0, \quad B_{i,k,t} \ge 0, \quad c_{k,t} \ge 1
$$

### 5. Summary of the MILP Model

**Sets:**
*   $N$: Set of stations $\{1, \dots, N\}$
*   $K$: Set of train services $\{1, \dots, K\}$
*   $U$: Set of rolling stock units $\{1, \dots, U\}$
*   $T$: Set of time intervals $\{1, \dots, T\}$
*   $Dest(i)$: Set of destinations for passengers boarding at station $i$.

**Parameters:**
*   $C_{op}$: Cost per car per interval.
*   $C_{wait}$: Cost per passenger waiting.
*   $Cap_{unit}$: Capacity of one car.
*   $C_{max}$: Max cars per train.
*   $\delta_{i,k}$: Dwell time for service $k$ at station $i$.
*   $R_{i,i+1,k}$: Running time for service $k$ from $i$ to $i+1$.
*   $H_{min}$: Minimum headway.
*   $T_{turn}$: Minimum turnaround time.
*   $D^{demand}_{i,t}$: Passenger demand arriving at station $i$ in interval $t$.
*   $M$: Large constant for Big-M formulation.

**Variables:**
*   $y_{k,t} \in \{0,1\}$: Service $k$ active in $t$.
*   $x_{k,u,t} \in \{0,1\}$: Unit $u$ assigned to service $k$ in $t$.
*   $c_{k,t} \in \mathbb{Z}^+$: Number of cars for service $k$ in $t$.
*   $A_{i,k,t}, D_{i,k,t} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Arrival/Departure times.
*   $W_{i,t} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Waiting passengers at station $i$ in $t$.
*   $B_{i,j,k,t} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Passengers boarding at $i$ for dest $j$ on train $k$ in $t$.
*   $Al_{i,k,t} \in \mathbb{R}^+$: Passengers alighting at $i$ on train $k$ in $t$.

**Objective:**
$$
\min \sum_{k,t} C_{op} c_{k,t} y_{k,t} + \sum_{i,t} C_{wait} W_{i,t}
$$

**Constraints:**
1.  **Timing:**
    *   $D_{i,k,t} = A_{i,k,t} + \delta_{i,k}$
    *   $A_{i+1,k,t} = D_{i,k,t} + R_{i,i+1,k}$
    *   $D_{i,k,t} - D_{i,k_{prev},t} \ge H_{min}$ (for fixed order)
2.  **Circulation:**
    *   $\sum_{u} x_{k,u,t} = y_{k,t}$
    *   $\sum_{k} x_{k,u,t} \le 1$
    *   $A_{j,k_2,t'} - D_{i,k_1,t} \ge T_{turn} - M(2 - x_{k_1,u,t} - x_{k_2,u,t'})$
3.  **Passenger Flow:**
    *   $W_{i,t} = W_{i,t-1} + D^{demand}_{i,t} - \sum_{k} \sum_{j \in Dest(i)} B_{i,j,k,t}$
    *   $\sum_{j \in Dest(i)} B_{i,j,k,t} \le Cap_{unit} \cdot c_{k,t} - Load_{i,k,t}$
    *   $Al_{i,k,t} = \sum_{j < i} B_{j,i,k,t}$
    *   $W_{i,t} \ge 0, B \ge 0, c_{k,t} \ge 1$

This model captures the interplay between **operational decisions** (composition $c_{k,t}$, circulation $x_{k,u,t}$) and **service outcomes** (waiting time $W_{i,t}$), addressing the specific contributions mentioned in the input text.

# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Context and Assumptions

A **linear high-speed railway line** with bidirectional tracks (eastbound track and westbound track) is considered. A **single disruption** blocks the eastbound track on a specific segment $k^*$ during a known time window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$. Affected trains may **reroute** to the (operational) westbound track on that segment, which introduces **bidirectional conflicts** that must be resolved. The model **jointly** optimizes:

1. **Timetable**: arrival and departure times at stations, train ordering, rerouting decisions.
2. **Speed profiles**: inter-station running times (a linear proxy for speed profiles), from which **energy consumption** is derived.

**Key assumptions (stated explicitly):**

*   **(A1)** Stations are indexed $j \in \mathcal{J} = \{1, \dots, J\}$ in physical order; segments $k \in \mathcal{K} = \{1, \dots, J-1\}$ connect stations $k$ and $k+1$.
*   **(A2)** Each train $i \in \mathcal{I}$ has known origin $o_i$, destination $d_i$, scheduled arrival $t^{sched}_{ij}$ and departure $t^{sched}_{ij,dep}$ times at every visited station.
*   **(A3)** The disruption blocks the **eastbound track** on segment $k^*$ during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$; the westbound track remains operational.
*   **(A4)** Rerouting is only permitted on segment $k^*$ (local rerouting within the disruption area); elsewhere, trains use their default-direction track. *(This is a simplification; a full model could allow rerouting over multiple adjacent segments.)*
*   **(A5)** **Energy model** (linearization assumption): energy on segment $k$ is a decreasing linear function of running time, $E_{ik} = \alpha_k - \beta_k \cdot t_{ik}$ with $\beta_k > 0$ (faster travel ⇒ more energy). This is a linear approximation of the true (convex, nonlinear) energy-vs-time curve. *(Marked as a simplifying assumption.)*
*   **(A6)** Speed, acceleration, and deceleration limits are **encoded via pre-computed** minimum/maximum inter-station running times $t^{min}_{ik}, t^{max}_{ik}$ (so the model stays linear and avoids explicit kinematic nonlinearities).
*   **(A7)** Trains do not pass each other on the same track; ordering is modeled with binary variables and a Big-$M$ formulation.
*   **(A8)** All parameters are known and deterministic.
*   **(A9)** A fixed maximum delay at origin $\Delta_{max}$ anchors each train's departure; no train is allowed to depart later than its original departure plus $\Delta_{max}$.
*   **(A10)** The minimum headway $HW^{min}$ between consecutive same-direction trains and the minimum separation $HW^{opp}$ between opposing trains on a shared segment are constant safety parameters.

---

## 2. Index Sets and Parameters

### 2.1 Index Sets

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{I} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | Set of all trains |
| $\mathcal{I}^E$ | Eastbound trains (default direction $+1$) |
| $\mathcal{I}^W$ | Westbound trains (default direction $-1$) |
| $\mathcal{I}^{aff} \subseteq \mathcal{I}^E$ | Trains that traverse segment $k^*$ eastbound (affected by disruption) |
| $\mathcal{J} = \{1,\dots,J\}$ | Set of stations |
| $\mathcal{J}_i$ | Ordered set of stations visited by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{K} = \{1,\dots,J-1\}$ | Set of segments |
| $\mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{P}^{same}_k$ | Pairs $(i,j)$ sharing segment $k$ in the **same** direction |
| $\mathcal{P}^{opp}$ | Pairs $(i,j)$ of **opposing** trains that may conflict on a shared segment |

### 2.2 Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $o_i, d_i$ | Origin / destination station of train $i$ |
| $t^{sched}_{ij},\; t^{sched}_{ij,dep}$ | Scheduled arrival / departure of train $i$ at station $j$ |
| $t^{orig}_i$ | Original departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $t^{dest}_i$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at its destination |
| $\Delta_{max}$ | Maximum allowed departure delay at origin |
| $DW_j$ | Minimum dwell time at station $j$ |
| $t^{min}_{ik},\; t^{max}_{ik}$ | Min / max running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ (encodes speed & kinematics) |
| $HW^{min}$ | Minimum headway between same-direction trains on a segment |
| $HW^{opp}$ | Minimum separation for opposing trains on a shared segment |
| $T_{start},\; T_{end}$ | Disruption window on segment $k^*$ |
| $k^*$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $\alpha_k,\; \beta_k\;(\beta_k>0)$ | Energy-model coefficients on segment $k$ |
| $w^d_i$ | Delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., passenger count or priority) |
| $w^E$ | Weight on total energy in the objective |
| $M$ | Big-$M$ constant (a large upper bound on time) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{ij}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $j$, $j\in\mathcal{J}_i$ |
| $d_{ij}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $j$, $j\in\mathcal{J}_i$ |
| $t_{ik}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Inter-station running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $E_{ik}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $delay_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Destination delay of train $i$ (linearization of $(a_{i,d_i}-t^{dest}_i)^+$) |

### 3.2 Binary variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on a shared same-direction segment ($(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}^{same}_k$) |
| $u_{ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if train $i$ clears a shared segment before opposing train $j$ ($(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}^{opp}$) |
| $r_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if affected train $i\in\mathcal{I}^{aff}$ **reroutes** to the westbound track on segment $k^*$ |
| $s_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $=1$ if non-rerouted train $i$ traverses $k^*$ **before** the disruption, $=0$ if **after** |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of **total passenger delay** and **total energy consumption**:

$$
\boxed{\;\min \; Z \;=\; \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}} w^d_i \cdot delay_i \;+\; w^E \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}_i} E_{ik}\;}
$$

The trade-off is intrinsic: a train that **decelerates** (larger $t_{ik}$) reduces energy $E_{ik}=\alpha_k-\beta_k t_{ik}$ but may increase $delay_i$; a train that **accelerates** (smaller $t_{ik}$) cuts delay but raises energy. The optimizer balances the two via $w^d_i$ and $w^E$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### C1. Energy–running-time linkage (speed management)

$$
E_{ik} = \alpha_k - \beta_k \cdot t_{ik} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; k\in\mathcal{K}_i
$$
$$
E_{ik} \geq 0 \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; k\in\mathcal{K}_i
$$

### C2. Delay definition (linearization)

$$
delay_i \geq a_{i,d_i} - t^{dest}_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}
$$
$$
delay_i \geq 0 \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}
$$
*(Since $delay_i$ is minimized, it takes the value $\max(0,\,a_{i,d_i}-t^{dest}_i)$.)*

### C3. Timetable consistency (flow & dwell)

**Dwell time:**
$$
d_{ij} \geq a_{ij} + DW_j \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; j\in\mathcal{J}_i \setminus \{o_i\}
$$

**Inter-station linkage (arrival at next station = departure + running time):**
$$
a_{i,j+1} = d_{ij} + t_{ij} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; j\in\mathcal{J}_i,\; j+1\in\mathcal{J}_i
$$

**Running-time bounds (speed / acceleration / deceleration limits, A6):**
$$
t^{min}_{ik} \leq t_{ik} \leq t^{max}_{ik} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I},\; k\in\mathcal{K}_i
$$

**Origin anchoring (A9):**
$$
t^{orig}_i \;\leq\; a_{i,o_i} \;\leq\; t^{orig}_i + \Delta_{max} \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}
$$

### C4. Same-direction ordering & headways

For every pair $(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}^{same}_k$, $i\neq j$, on a shared segment $k$:
$$
d_{ik} + HW^{min} \;\leq\; d_{jk} + M(1 - x_{ij})
$$
$$
d_{jk} + HW^{min} \;\leq\; d_{ik} + M \cdot x_{ij}
$$
$$
x_{ij} + x_{ji} = 1
$$
*(Exactly one of the two trains precedes the other, and the trailing train departs the segment at least $HW^{min}$ after the leading one.)*

### C5. Opposing-train (bidirectional) conflicts

For every conflicting pair $(i,j)\in\mathcal{P}^{opp}$ sharing a segment $k$:
$$
d_{ik} \;\leq\; a_{jk} - HW^{opp} + M(1 - u_{ij})
$$
$$
d_{jk} \;\leq\; a_{ik} - HW^{opp} + M \cdot u_{ij}
$$
$$
u_{ij} \in \{0,1\}
$$
*(The first train must fully clear the segment a minimum separation $HW^{opp}$ before the opposing train enters. On segment $k^*$, a rerouted eastbound train and a westbound train are both on the westbound track and are treated as an opposing/conflicting pair, so these constraints apply.)*

### C6. Rerouting and disruption constraint (core of the model)

The disrupted eastbound track on $k^*$ is unusable during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$. For each affected train $i\in\mathcal{I}^{aff}$, either **reroute** ($r_i=1$) or **time the traversal** to avoid the window.

**Coupling reroute with timing indicator:**
$$
s_i \;\leq\; 1 - r_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}^{aff}
$$

**Disjunctive timing (before/after the disruption), linearized:**
$$
a_{i,k^*+1} \;\leq\; T_{start} + M(1 - s_i) \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}^{aff}
$$
$$
d_{i,k^*} \;\geq\; T_{end} - M\, s_i \qquad \forall i\in\mathcal{I}^{aff}
$$

**Logic check:**
* If $r_i = 1$ (rerouted): $s_i$ may be 0 or 1; both timing constraints are effectively relaxed, so the train uses the open westbound track at any time (its conflicts are handled by C5).
* If $r_i = 0$ (not rerouted): $s_i \in \{0,1\}$ must be chosen.
    * $s_i = 1 \Rightarrow a_{i,k^*+1}\le T_{start}$ and $d_{i,k^*}\ge T_{end}-M$ (relaxed) ⇒ train traverses **before** the disruption.
    * $s_i = 0 \Rightarrow a_{i,k^*+1}\le T_{start}+M$ (relaxed) and $d_{i,k^*}\ge T_{end}$ ⇒ train traverses **after** the disruption clears.

### C7. Rerouting eligibility

Rerouting variables are defined only for affected trains; all other trains keep their default track:
$$
r_i = 0 \qquad \forall i \notin \mathcal{I}^{aff}
$$
(For non-affected trains, $s_i$ is not defined/needed.)

### C8. Variable domains

$$
a_{ij},\, d_{ij},\, t_{ik},\, E_{ik},\, delay_i \;\geq\; 0
$$
$$
x_{ij},\, u_{ij},\, r_i,\, s_i \;\in\; \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Element | Content |
|---------|---------|
| **Type** | Mixed-Integer Linear Program (fully linear) |
| **Continuous vars** | $a_{ij}, d_{ij}, t_{ik}, E_{ik}, delay_i$ |
| **Binary vars** | $x_{ij}$ (ordering), $u_{ij}$ (opposing), $r_i$ (reroute), $s_i$ (disruption timing) |
| **Objective** | Minimize $\sum w^d_i\, delay_i + w^E \sum E_{ik}$ (delay + energy) |
| **Key constraints** | Energy↔running-time (C1); delay linearization (C2); dwell & linkage (C3); same-direction headways (C4); opposing-train separation (C5); reroute/disruption disjunction (C6); eligibility (C7) |

**Why this model is valid and complete:**
* **Linearity:** every term is linear in the decision variables (the $(\cdot)^+$ in delay and the energy curve are both linearized; kinematics are pre-compressed into $t^{min/max}$ bounds).
* **Conflict-free:** C4 enforces headways among same-direction trains and C5 enforces separation among opposing trains, including rerouted trains that share the westbound track — guaranteeing a conflict-free timetable.
* **Integrated:** timetable variables ($a,d$) and speed variables ($t$, hence $E$) are **coupled** through C1 and C3, so the rescheduling and speed-management decisions are made simultaneously rather than sequentially.
* **Disruption-aware:** C6 couples the rerouting decision $r_i$ with the "before/after window" timing $s_i$, so the model can either divert a train to the open track or hold it to pass before/after the blockage.

**Known simplifications (for future extension):** single-segment rerouting (A4); single linear energy segment (A5); constant headways (A10); deterministic parameters (A8). These can be relaxed to multi-segment rerouting, piecewise-linear energy (SOS2), train-pair-specific headways, and stochastic/robust scenarios respectively, without changing the overall MILP structure.

The model can be solved directly with a standard MILP solver (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP, CBC); for large instances, the decomposition and adaptive iterative approach described in the source paper (splitting into an ordering IP plus per-train speed plans) can be applied to the same formulation.
