# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description

A bidirectional high-speed railway line with stations connected by segments. A partial blockage occurs on one track of a specific segment during a known time window, forcing trains in the blocked direction to reroute to the opposite track. The model simultaneously optimizes:
- **Retiming:** Arrival and departure times at stations
- **Reordering:** Train order on shared segments
- **Rerouting:** Track assignment for affected trains
- **Speed Management:** Segment running times (which determine energy consumption)

The objective minimizes total weighted passenger delay, total energy consumption, and rerouting penalties.

---

## 2. Assumptions

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| A1 | Trains are modeled as point masses; train length is absorbed into the minimum headway parameter. |
| A2 | Energy consumption on each segment is a **linear decreasing** function of running time (shorter running time → higher energy). This is a standard linearization of the nonlinear speed–energy relationship. |
| A3 | Acceleration and deceleration limits are constant, and the feasible running-time interval $[t^{\min}, t^{\max}]$ for each segment is **pre-computed** from track geometry, speed limits, and train dynamics. |
| A4 | Station dwelling times are bounded by known minimum and maximum values. |
| A5 | There is a **single disruption zone**: one physical segment $k^*$ where one track (direction $D^+$) is blocked during a fixed time window $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$. |
| A6 | No train cancellations are considered in this model (an extension can add binary cancellation variables). |
| A7 | The line has exactly two physical tracks (one per direction) per segment. |
| A8 | The disruption window is known in advance (deterministic setting). |

---

## 3. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{S} = \{1, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line |
| $\mathcal{E} = \{(i, j)\}$ | Set of **directed** segments (arcs). For each physical segment between $i$ and $i+1$, there are two arcs: $(i, i+1)$ (direction $+$) and $(i+1, i)$ (direction $-$) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of **physical** segments (undirected). $k^* \in \mathcal{K}$ is the disrupted segment |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^+$ | Subset of trains traveling in direction $+$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^-$ | Subset of trains traveling in direction $-$ |
| $P_t \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Ordered sequence of stations visited by train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{E}_t \subseteq \mathcal{E}$ | Set of directed arcs traversed by train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{W} = [T_{\text{start}},\, T_{\text{end}}]$ | Disruption time window |

---

## 4. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $t^{\text{sch}}_{t,i}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $w^{\text{del}}_{t,i}$ | Weight (cost per unit time) for delay of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $c^{\text{reroute}}$ | Fixed cost penalty for rerouting a train through the disruption zone |
| $t^{\min}_{t,(i,j)}$ | Minimum feasible running time of train $t$ on arc $(i,j)$ (from max speed and acceleration limits) |
| $t^{\max}_{t,(i,j)}$ | Maximum feasible running time of train $t$ on arc $(i,j)$ (from min speed and deceleration limits) |
| $\tau^{\min}_{t,i}$ | Minimum dwelling time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $\tau^{\max}_{t,i}$ | Maximum dwelling time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $\Delta t^{\min}_{(i,j)}$ | Minimum headway (time separation) between consecutive trains on arc $(i,j)$ |
| $\alpha_{t,(i,j)}$ | Slope of the linearized energy function for train $t$ on arc $(i,j)$, with $\alpha < 0$ |
| $\beta_{t,(i,j)}$ | Intercept of the linearized energy function for train $t$ on arc $(i,j)$ |
| $E^{\min}_{t,(i,j)}$ | Minimum energy consumption (achieved at $t^{\max}$) |
| $E^{\max}_{t,(i,j)}$ | Maximum energy consumption (achieved at $t^{\min}$) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) for linearization |

---

## 5. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{t,i}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $d_{t,i}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $i$ |
| $r_{t,(i,j)}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $t$ on directed arc $(i,j)$ |
| $e_{t,(i,j)}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on directed arc $(i,j)$ |
| $\text{delay}_{t,i}$ | $\geq 0$ | Positive delay of train $t$ at station $i$ (deviation from schedule) |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,k^*}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ **reroutes** (uses the opposite track) on disrupted physical segment $k^*$; 0 otherwise. Defined only for $t \in \mathcal{T}^+$ (trains in the blocked direction) |
| $y_{t,u,(i,j)}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ **precedes** train $u$ on directed arc $(i,j)$; 0 otherwise. Defined for all pairs $t \neq u$ sharing arc $(i,j)$ in the **same direction** |
| $y^{\text{bi}}_{t,u,k^*}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ (direction $+$, rerouted) **passes before** train $u$ (direction $-$) on physical segment $k^*$; 0 otherwise. Defined for pairs $(t, u)$ where $t \in \mathcal{T}^+$, $u \in \mathcal{T}^-$, both traversing $k^*$ |
| $z_{t,1}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Auxiliary: 1 if train $t$ **exits** the disrupted segment before $T_{\text{start}}$ |
| $z_{t,2}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Auxiliary: 1 if train $t$ **enters** the disrupted segment after $T_{\text{end}}$ |

---

## 6. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{
\min \; Z \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{i \in P_t} w^{\text{del}}_{t,i} \;\cdot\; \text{delay}_{t,i}}_{\text{Total weighted delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{(i,j) \in \mathcal{E}_t} e_{t,(i,j)}}_{\text{Total energy consumption}} \;+\; \underbrace{c^{\text{reroute}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^+} x_{t,k^*}}_{\text{Total rerouting penalty}}
}
$$

**Interpretation:**
- The first term penalizes late arrivals relative to the original schedule.
- The second term encourages energy-efficient speed profiles (longer running times where delay allows).
- The third term discourages unnecessary rerouting (operational complexity, signaling costs).

---

## 7. Constraints

### (C1) Station Dwelling Time

For every train $t$ and station $i \in P_t$:

$$
d_{t,i} \;\geq\; a_{t,i} + \tau^{\min}_{t,i}
$$

$$
d_{t,i} \;\leq\; a_{t,i} + \tau^{\max}_{t,i}
$$

### (C2) Running Time Linkage (Flow Conservation)

For every train $t$ and consecutive stations $i, j$ in $P_t$ (where $(i,j) \in \mathcal{E}_t$):

$$
a_{t,j} \;=\; d_{t,i} + r_{t,(i,j)}
$$

### (C3) Running Time Bounds (Speed Profile Feasibility)

For every train $t$ and arc $(i,j) \in \mathcal{E}_t$:

$$
t^{\min}_{t,(i,j)} \;\leq\; r_{t,(i,j)} \;\leq\; t^{\max}_{t,(i,j)}
$$

*These bounds encode the physical limits imposed by maximum/minimum speed, constant acceleration $a_{\text{acc}}$, and constant deceleration $a_{\text{dec}}$. They are pre-computed as:*

$$
t^{\min}_{t,(i,j)} = \frac{v_{\max}}{a_{\text{acc}}} + \frac{v_{\max}}{a_{\text{dec}}} + \frac{L_{(i,j)} - \frac{v_{\max}^2}{2a_{\text{acc}}} - \frac{v_{\max}^2}{2a_{\text{dec}}}}{v_{\max}}
$$

$$
t^{\max}_{t,(i,j)} = \frac{L_{(i,j)}}{v_{\min}}
$$

*(Assuming the segment is long enough to reach $v_{\max}$; otherwise, the trapezoidal/parabolic profile formula applies.)*

### (C4) Linearized Energy Consumption

For every train $t$ and arc $(i,j) \in \mathcal{E}_t$:

$$
e_{t,(i,j)} \;=\; \alpha_{t,(i,j)} \;\cdot\; r_{t,(i,j)} \;+\; \beta_{t,(i,j)}
$$

with the additional bounds:

$$
E^{\min}_{t,(i,j)} \;\leq\; e_{t,(i,j)} \;\leq\; E^{\max}_{t,(i,j)}
$$

*Since $\alpha_{t,(i,j)} < 0$, shorter running times (higher speeds) yield higher energy. The optimizer trades off delay (wants shorter $r$) against energy (wants longer $r$).*

### (C5) Delay Definition

For every train $t$ and station $i \in P_t$:

$$
\text{delay}_{t,i} \;\geq\; a_{t,i} - t^{\text{sch}}_{t,i}
$$

$$
\text{delay}_{t,i} \;\geq\; 0
$$

*(Since the objective minimizes $\text{delay}_{t,i}$, it will take the value $\max(0,\; a_{t,i} - t^{\text{sch}}_{t,i})$.)*

### (C6) Disruption / Rerouting Logic

Let the disrupted physical segment $k^*$ connect stations $p$ and $p+1$. The blocked direction is $D^+$, so the directed arc is $(p, p+1)$. For every train $t \in \mathcal{T}^+$ traversing segment $k^*$:

**Logic:** If train $t$ does **not** reroute ($x_{t,k^*} = 0$), it must be **entirely before** or **entirely after** the disruption window on the normal track.

Introduce auxiliary binaries $z_{t,1}, z_{t,2} \in \{0,1\}$:

$$
\text{If } z_{t,1} = 1: \quad a_{t,p+1} \;\leq\; T_{\text{start}} \quad \text{(train exits before disruption starts)}
$$

$$
\text{If } z_{t,2} = 1: \quad d_{t,p} \;\geq\; T_{\text{end}} \quad \text{(train enters after disruption ends)}
$$

**Linearization:**

$$
a_{t,p+1} \;\leq\; T_{\text{start}} + M\,(1 - z_{t,1})
$$

$$
a_{t,p+1} \;\geq\; T_{\text{start}} - M\, z_{t,1}
$$

$$
d_{t,p} \;\geq\; T_{\text{end}} - M\,(1 - z_{t,2})
$$

$$
d_{t,p} \;\leq\; T_{\text{end}} + M\, z_{t,2}
$$

**Rerouting enforcement:**

$$
x_{t,k^*} \;\geq\; 1 - z_{t,1} - z_{t,2}
$$

*Interpretation:* If neither $z_{t,1}=1$ nor $z_{t,2}=1$ (i.e., the train's traversal overlaps the disruption window), then $x_{t,k^*}$ must equal 1 (forced reroute). If the train is entirely before or after the window, $x_{t,k^*}$ can be 0 (no reroute needed). The objective's rerouting penalty will drive $x_{t,k^*}=0$ whenever feasible.

### (C7) Same-Direction Ordering and Headway

For every pair of trains $t, u \in \mathcal{T}^+$ (or both in $\mathcal{T}^-$) sharing directed arc $(i,j)$, $t \neq u$:

**Ordering completeness:**

$$
y_{t,u,(i,j)} + y_{u,t,(i,j)} \;=\; 1
$$

**Headway constraints (Big-M):**

If $t$ precedes $u$ ($y_{t,u,(i,j)} = 1$):
$$
a_{u,j} \;\geq\; a_{t,j} + \Delta t^{\min}_{(i,j)}
$$

If $u$ precedes $t$ ($y_{u,t,(i,j)} = 1$):
$$
a_{t,j} \;\geq\; a_{u,j} + \Delta t^{\min}_{(i,j)}
$$

**Combined linear form:**

$$
a_{u,j} \;\geq\; a_{t,j} + \Delta t^{\min}_{(i,j)} - M\,(1 - y_{t,u,(i,j)})
$$

$$
a_{t,j} \;\geq\; a_{u,j} + \Delta t^{\min}_{(i,j)} - M\, y_{t,u,(i,j)}
$$

### (C8) Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (Rerouted vs. Normal Trains)

This is the **critical** constraint set for partial blockage. When a train $t \in \mathcal{T}^+$ reroutes ($x_{t,k^*}=1$), it occupies the **opposite** physical track (the $D^-$ track) on segment $k^*$. It now shares this track with trains $u \in \mathcal{T}^-$ traveling in direction $-$.

For every pair $(t, u)$ where $t \in \mathcal{T}^+$, $u \in \mathcal{T}^-$, both traversing physical segment $k^*$:

**Ordering variable:** $y^{\text{bi}}_{t,u,k^*} \in \{0,1\}$, where 1 means $t$ passes through $k^*$ before $u$.

**Separation constraints (active only when $t$ is rerouted):**

$$
a_{t,p+1} \;\leq\; d_{u,p+1} + M\,(1 - y^{\text{bi}}_{t,u,k^*}) + M\,(1 - x_{t,k^*})
$$

$$
a_{u,p} \;\leq\; d_{t,p} + M\, y^{\text{bi}}_{t,u,k^*} + M\,(1 - x_{t,k^*})
$$

*Interpretation:*
- If $x_{t,k^*} = 0$ (no reroute): the term $M(1 - x_{t,k^*}) = M$ makes both constraints vacuous. Train $t$ is on the blocked track, train $u$ is on the opposite track — no conflict.
- If $x_{t,k^*} = 1$ (rerouted): the Big-M term vanishes, and the constraints enforce that either $t$ exits $k^*$ before $u$ enters ($y^{\text{bi}}=1$), or $u$ exits before $t$ enters ($y^{\text{bi}}=0$). This ensures **no simultaneous occupancy** of the shared physical track.

### (C9) Non-Negativity and Domain Constraints

$$
a_{t,i},\; d_{t,i},\; r_{t,(i,j)},\; e_{t,(i,j)},\; \text{delay}_{t,i} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \forall\, t, i, (i,j)
$$

$$
x_{t,k^*},\; y_{t,u,(i,j)},\; y^{\text{bi}}_{t,u,k^*},\; z_{t,1},\; z_{t,2} \;\in\; \{0, 1\}
$$

---

## 8. Model Summary

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| **Objective** | Trade-off between punctuality (delay), energy efficiency, and operational simplicity (rerouting count) |
| **C1–C2** | Ensure temporal consistency: departure ≥ arrival + dwell; arrival at next station = departure + running time |
| **C3** | Enforce physical speed/acceleration limits via pre-computed running-time bounds |
| **C4** | Link running time to energy via a linear (decreasing) function, enabling the speed–energy trade-off |
| **C5** | Define delay as the positive deviation from the original schedule |
| **C6** | Force rerouting when a train's traversal overlaps the disruption window on the blocked track |
| **C7** | Guarantee same-direction train separation (headway) via ordering variables |
| **C8** | Guarantee bidirectional train separation on the shared physical track when rerouting occurs |
| **C9** | Standard domain and non-negativity restrictions |

---

## 9. Key Linearization Techniques

1. **Energy model:** The nonlinear relationship between speed (or running time) and energy is approximated by a single linear segment $e = \alpha r + \beta$ with $\alpha < 0$. For higher accuracy, a piecewise-linear approximation with multiple segments and SOS2 or binary variables can be used.

2. **Disruption logic (C6):** The "if-then" condition (if the train overlaps the window, it must reroute) is linearized using auxiliary binaries $z_{t,1}, z_{t,2}$ and the constraint $x_{t,k^*} \geq 1 - z_{t,1} - z_{t,2}$.

3. **Conditional conflict (C8):** The bidirectional separation constraint is "switched on" only when $x_{t,k^*}=1$ via the Big-M term $M(1 - x_{t,k^*})$. This avoids adding the constraint for all pairs unconditionally, reducing model size.

4. **Delay (C5):** The $\max(0, \cdot)$ function is linearized by introducing a non-negative variable bounded below by the deviation, relying on the minimization objective to set it to the exact value.

---

## 10. Complexity Notes

- The number of binary ordering variables $y_{t,u,(i,j)}$ is $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2 \cdot |\mathcal{E}|)$ in the worst case, making this a large-scale MILP.
- The paper's proposed decomposition approach (splitting into a master IP for train interactions and sub-problems for individual train speed plans) is designed to address this combinatorial complexity.
- The Big-M constants $M$ should be set as tightly as possible (e.g., $M = T_{\text{end}} - T_{\text{start}} + \max r_{t,(i,j)}$) to improve solver performance.

Text:
Based on the provided text, specifically focusing on the "Contributions of the paper" and the description of the multi-stage framework, here is a complete Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model.

The model focuses on the **Global Optimum Model** described in Section 3.3, which extends the sub-optimal model to consider delay propagation. This model solves the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP) by simultaneously determining **rerouting**, **reordering**, and **rescheduling**.

### 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem:**
Given a set of trains with initial timetables, a railway network with potential conflicts, and a specific time horizon, determine the optimal route, order, and schedule for all trains to minimize total delay, while respecting infrastructure capacity and safety constraints.

**Assumptions (Marked as reasonable assumptions based on standard rtRTMP literature and the text):**
1.  **Discrete Time Horizon:** The time horizon is discretized into steps of $\Delta t$ (e.g., 1 minute). Let $T$ be the total number of time steps.
2.  **Fixed Travel Times:** The travel time between any two consecutive resources (blocks/stations) is fixed and known, independent of speed variations (standard in many MILP formulations for tractability, or assumed constant for the specific route selected).
3.  **Resource Types:** The network consists of **Blocks** (track sections) and **Stations** (platforms). We assume a unified resource set $\mathcal{R}$ for simplicity, where each resource has a capacity of 1 (only one train can occupy it at a time).
4.  **Route Pre-computation:** As suggested by the text ("solve the route selection problem first... providing a smaller subset"), we assume a set of feasible alternative routes $\mathcal{A}_t$ is pre-computed for each train $t$. The model selects one route from this set.
5.  **No Overtaking in Blocks:** Trains cannot overtake each other within a block section. Overtaking is only possible at stations (if multiple platforms are available, modeled as separate resources).
6.  **Delay Definition:** Delay is defined as the difference between the actual departure/arrival time and the nominal (planned) time.
7.  **Safety Margins:** The "safety-relevant overlaps" mentioned in the text are incorporated as fixed time lags (buffer times) required between consecutive trains using the same resource.

### 2. Sets and Indices

*   $\mathcal{T}$: Set of trains.
*   $\mathcal{R}$: Set of resources (blocks and station platforms).
*   $\mathcal{A}_t$: Set of feasible alternative routes for train $t$.
*   $k \in \{1, \dots, K_t\}$: Index for the sequence of resources in a route.
*   $a \in \mathcal{A}_t$: Index for a specific alternative route for train $t$.
*   $i, j \in \mathcal{R}$: Indices for resources.
*   $\tau \in \{1, \dots, T\}$: Discrete time steps.

### 3. Parameters

*   $N_{t,a}$: Number of resources in route $a$ for train $t$.
*   $r_{t,a,k}$: The specific resource ID occupied by train $t$ in step $k$ of route $a$.
*   $\theta_{t,a,k}$: The nominal arrival time (in time steps) of train $t$ at resource $r_{t,a,k}$ if no delays occur and route $a$ is chosen.
*   $\Delta t_{t,a,k}$: The nominal travel time (in time steps) from resource $k-1$ to $k$ for train $t$ on route $a$.
*   $L_{i,j}$: The minimum time lag (safety margin) required between the end of occupancy of resource $i$ by one train and the start of occupancy of resource $j$ by another train (if they are consecutive in the network). *Assumption: If resources are independent, $L=0$.*
*   $M$: A large constant (Big-M) for linearization.
*   $w_t$: Weighting factor for train $t$ (e.g., based on priority or cost of delay). Default $w_t = 1$.

### 4. Decision Variables

**Binary Variables:**
*   $x_{t,a} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ selects route $a$, 0 otherwise.
*   $y_{t,i,\tau} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ occupies resource $i$ at time step $\tau$, 0 otherwise.
*   $z_{t,t',i} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ is scheduled *before* train $t'$ on resource $i$ (ordering variable). If $t=t'$, this is undefined/0.

**Continuous/Integer Variables:**
*   $d_{t,i} \geq 0$: The delay (in time steps) of train $t$ at resource $i$.
*   $S_{t,i} \geq 0$: The start time (in time steps) of train $t$ at resource $i$.
*   $E_{t,i} \geq 0$: The end time (in time steps) of train $t$ at resource $i$.

*(Note: To keep the model strictly linear and compact as per modern formulations like Pellegrini et al., we often use arrival/departure times directly. Let's refine the variables to be more standard for MILP efficiency.)*

**Refined Decision Variables:**
*   $x_{t,a} \in \{0, 1\}$: Route selection.
*   $u_{t,i} \in \{0, 1\}$: Equals 1 if train $t$ uses resource $i$ (derived from route selection, but kept explicit for clarity or calculated). *Actually, it is better to link $x$ directly to resource usage.*
*   Let's use **Start Time** variables $S_{t,i}$ (integer) for the start of occupation of resource $i$ by train $t$.
*   $o_{t,t',i} \in \{0, 1\}$: Ordering variable. $o_{t,t',i}=1$ if train $t$ starts on resource $i$ before train $t'$.

### 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted delay of all trains. The delay is calculated as the difference between the actual start time at the first resource (or final resource) and the nominal start time. To simplify, we define delay at the final destination or sum delays at all resources. A common approach is minimizing the sum of arrival delays at the final station.

$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} w_t \cdot D_t
$$

Where $D_t$ is the delay of train $t$. To make this linear, we define $D_t$ as the start time of the last resource minus the nominal start time of the last resource.
Let $i_{last,t,a}$ be the last resource in route $a$ for train $t$.
Since the route is a decision, we need to linearize the delay calculation.
Alternatively, a simpler and robust objective is to minimize the sum of start times relative to nominal times for all resources, or specifically the final arrival.

Let's define the objective as minimizing the sum of weighted delays at the **final resource** of each train.
Let $R_{final, t, a}$ be the last resource in route $a$ for train $t$.
Let $\Theta_{t, final, a}$ be the nominal arrival time at $R_{final, t, a}$ for route $a$.

$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} w_t \cdot x_{t,a} \cdot (S_{t, R_{final, t, a}} - \Theta_{t, final, a})
$$

*Correction:* This is non-linear because of $x \cdot S$.
Better approach: Introduce a delay variable $D_t$.
$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} w_t D_t
$$
Subject to:
$$
D_t \geq S_{t, i} - \Theta_{t, i, a} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall a \in \mathcal{A}_t, \forall i \in \text{Resources in route } a
$$
*Assumption:* We minimize the maximum delay per train or sum of delays. Let's assume **sum of delays at all resources** for a comprehensive penalty, or just the final delay. Let's stick to **Final Delay** for simplicity, but link it correctly.

Actually, the most standard linear formulation for "minimize total delay" in these MILPs is:
$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{R}} w_t \cdot \max(0, S_{t,i} - \Theta_{t,i})
$$
Linearized as:
$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{R}} w_t \cdot D_{t,i}
$$
Subject to:
$$
D_{t,i} \geq S_{t,i} - \Theta_{t,i, a} \cdot x_{t,a} \quad \text{(This is still tricky if } \Theta \text{ depends on } a)
$$

**Simplification for the Model:**
Let's assume the nominal time $\Theta_{t,i}$ is defined for the *nominal route* only. If a train reroutes, the nominal time for the new resources might be 0 or undefined.
*Standard Approach:* Define delay only for the resources on the *selected* route.
Let's use the formulation where we minimize the start time of the train at its final destination.

**Final Objective Function:**
$$
\min \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} w_t \cdot D_t
$$

### 6. Constraints

#### A. Route Selection Constraints
Each train must select exactly one route.
$$
\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} x_{t,a} = 1 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

#### B. Resource Usage Linking
A train occupies a resource $i$ only if it selects a route $a$ that contains resource $i$.
Let $\delta_{t,a,i} = 1$ if resource $i$ is in route $a$ for train $t$, else 0.
$$
S_{t,i} \geq 0
$$
$$
S_{t,i} \leq M \cdot \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} \delta_{t,a,i} x_{t,a} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
$$
*(If the train doesn't use resource $i$, $S_{t,i}$ is forced to 0.)*

#### C. Precedence Constraints (Travel Time)
For each train $t$ and each pair of consecutive resources $(i, j)$ in a route $a$, if $i$ is followed by $j$ in route $a$, the start time at $j$ must be at least the start time at $i$ plus the travel time.
Let $Next_{t,a,i}$ be the resource following $i$ in route $a$.
Let $Travel_{t,a,i}$ be the travel time from $i$ to $Next_{t,a,i}$.

$$
S_{t, Next_{t,a,i}} \geq S_{t,i} + Travel_{t,a,i} - M(1 - x_{t,a}) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall a \in \mathcal{A}_t, \forall i \in \text{Resources in } a \text{ (except last)}
$$

#### D. Capacity and Ordering Constraints (The Core of rtRTMP)
For any two distinct trains $t, t'$ and any resource $i$, they cannot occupy the resource simultaneously. We use the ordering variable $o_{t,t',i}$.

1.  **Ordering Logic:**
    $$
    o_{t,t',i} + o_{t',t,i} \leq 1 \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    *(Note: If both trains do not use resource $i$, this constraint is trivial. To tighten, we can add $o_{t,t',i} \leq \sum_{a} \delta_{t,a,i} x_{t,a}$ and similar for $t'$.)*

2.  **Separation Constraint (Big-M):**
    If train $t$ is ordered before train $t'$ on resource $i$ ($o_{t,t',i}=1$), then $t$ must finish before $t'$ starts (plus safety margin).
    Let $Dur_{t,i}$ be the duration of train $t$ on resource $i$.
    Let $Lag_{i}$ be the safety margin (headway) required on resource $i$.

    $$
    S_{t',i} \geq S_{t,i} + Dur_{t,i} + Lag_{i} - M(1 - o_{t,t',i}) \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    S_{t,i} \geq S_{t',i} + Dur_{t',i} + Lag_{i} - M(1 - o_{t',t,i}) \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$

    *Refinement:* The duration $Dur_{t,i}$ might depend on the route if the speed profile changes, but usually, dwell time at a station or passage time through a block is fixed per resource. We assume $Dur_{t,i}$ is a known parameter for train $t$ on resource $i$.

#### E. Delay Propagation and Definition
To capture the "delay propagation" mentioned in the text (Section 3.3), the start time $S_{t,i}$ naturally propagates through the precedence constraints (C). The delay variable $D_t$ must be linked to the actual start times.

Let's define $D_t$ as the delay at the final resource.
Let $i_{end, t, a}$ be the last resource in route $a$ for train $t$.
Let $\Theta_{t, end, a}$ be the nominal arrival time at that resource for route $a$.

We need a linear constraint linking $D_t$ to $S_{t, i_{end}}$ and $x_{t,a}$.
Since $x_{t,a}$ is binary, we can use the following:
$$
D_t \geq S_{t, i_{end, t, a}} - \Theta_{t, end, a} - M(1 - x_{t,a}) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall a \in \mathcal{A}_t
$$
$$
D_t \geq 0 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

*Note:* This ensures that if route $a$ is selected ($x_{t,a}=1$), $D_t$ is at least the actual delay for that route. Since we minimize $D_t$, it will take the exact value of the delay for the selected route.

#### F. Time Horizon Bounds
$$
0 \leq S_{t,i} \leq T \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
$$

### 7. Complete Model Summary

**Minimize:**
$$
\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} w_t D_t
$$

**Subject to:**

1.  **Route Selection:**
    $$
    \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} x_{t,a} = 1 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
    $$

2.  **Resource Usage Activation:**
    $$
    S_{t,i} \leq M \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} \delta_{t,a,i} x_{t,a} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$

3.  **Precedence (Travel Time):**
    $$
    S_{t, j} \geq S_{t, i} + Travel_{t,a,i} - M(1 - x_{t,a}) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall a \in \mathcal{A}_t, \forall (i,j) \in \text{Consecutive pairs in route } a
    $$

4.  **Ordering Logic:**
    $$
    o_{t,t',i} + o_{t',t,i} \leq 1 \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    o_{t,t',i} \leq \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_t} \delta_{t,a,i} x_{t,a} \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    o_{t,t',i} \leq \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}_{t'}} \delta_{t',a,i} x_{t',a} \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$

5.  **Capacity (Separation):**
    $$
    S_{t',i} \geq S_{t,i} + Dur_{t,i} + Lag_{i} - M(1 - o_{t,t',i}) \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    S_{t,i} \geq S_{t',i} + Dur_{t',i} + Lag_{i} - M(1 - o_{t',t,i}) \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, \forall i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$

6.  **Delay Calculation:**
    $$
    D_t \geq S_{t, i_{end, t, a}} - \Theta_{t, end, a} - M(1 - x_{t,a}) \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, \forall a \in \mathcal{A}_t
    $$
    $$
    D_t \geq 0 \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
    $$

7.  **Variable Domains:**
    $$
    x_{t,a} \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, a \in \mathcal{A}_t
    $$
    $$
    o_{t,t',i} \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall t \neq t' \in \mathcal{T}, i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    S_{t,i} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}, i \in \mathcal{R}
    $$
    $$
    D_t \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \quad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}
    $$

### 8. Explanation of Linearity and Completeness

*   **Linearity:** All constraints are linear. The Big-M method is used to handle the logical implications of route selection and ordering. The objective function is linear in terms of $D_t$.
*   **Rerouting:** Handled by $x_{t,a}$.
*   **Reordering:** Handled by $o_{t,t',i}$.
*   **Rescheduling:** Handled by $S_{t,i}$ (start times).
*   **Delay Propagation:** Handled by the precedence constraints (3), which force the start time of the next resource to depend on the previous one. If a train is delayed at resource $i$ (due to conflict), $S_{t,i}$ increases, which forces $S_{t,j}$ (next resource) to increase, thus propagating the delay.
*   **Global Optimum:** By solving this single MILP, the model considers all interactions between route, order, and schedule simultaneously, ensuring the global optimum for the defined problem scope, as described in the "Global Optimum Model" section of the text.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) – MILP Formulation

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $B$ | Set of track segments (blocks), indexed by $b$ |
| $TS$ | Set of train–station pairs $(t,s)$ where train $t$ visits station $s$ |
| $TB$ | Set of train–block pairs $(t,b)$ where train $t$ traverses block $b$ |
| $K$ | Set of piece indices $k = 1, \ldots, K_{\text{pieces}}$ for the energy piecewise-linear approximation |
| $TBK$ | Set of $(t,b,k)$ triples for the incremental energy variables |
| $SD$ | Set of same-direction conflict pairs $(t_1, t_2, b)$ where trains $t_1$ and $t_2$ traverse block $b$ in the same direction, $t_1 < t_2$ |
| $OP$ | Set of opposite-direction conflict pairs $(t_1, t_2, b)$ arising from rerouting on the disrupted block |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $a^{pl}_t(s)$ | Planned arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $d^{pl}_t(s)$ | Planned departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $rt^{\min}_{t,b}$ | Minimum feasible running time of train $t$ on block $b$ |
| $rt^{\max}_{t,b}$ | Maximum feasible running time of train $t$ on block $b$ |
| $\delta^{\min}_t(s)$ | Minimum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $b_d$ | Disrupted block index |
| $d_d$ | Disrupted direction on block $b_d$ |
| $T_{\text{start}}$ | Disruption start time |
| $T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption end time |
| $H_{\min}$ | Minimum headway between two consecutive trains on the same block in the same direction |
| $H_{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum separation between two opposite-direction trains sharing the same physical track |
| $T_{\max}$ | Planning horizon upper bound on all times |
| $M$ | Big-M constant, $M = T_{\max}$ |
| $E^{\min}_{t,b}$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on block $b$ at $rt^{\max}_{t,b}$ (minimum energy) |
| $\text{slope}_{t,b,k}$ | Slope of piece $k$ in the piecewise-linear energy function for train $t$ on block $b$ |
| $\Delta_{t,b,k}$ | Length of piece $k$: $(rt^{\max}_{t,b} - rt^{\min}_{t,b})/K_{\text{pieces}}$ |
| $w_{\text{delay}}$ | Weight for total passenger delay |
| $w_{\text{energy}}$ | Weight for total energy consumption |
| $w_{\text{route}}$ | Weight for rerouting penalty |
| $\mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}$ | Set of trains affected by the disruption (trains whose path includes $b_d$ in direction $d_d$ and whose scheduled traversal overlaps $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$) |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_t(s)$ | Continuous, $[0,\, T_{\max}]$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$, for $(t,s) \in TS$ |
| $d_t(s)$ | Continuous, $[0,\, T_{\max}]$ | Departure time of train $t$ from station $s$, for $(t,s) \in TS$ |
| $rt_{t,b}$ | Continuous, $[rt^{\min}_{t,b},\, rt^{\max}_{t,b}]$ | Running time of train $t$ on block $b$, for $(t,b) \in TB$ |
| $R_t$ | Binary | $1$ if affected train $t$ is rerouted onto the opposite track on $b_d$, $0$ otherwise. Defined for $t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}$ |
| $x^{sd}_{t_1,t_2,b}$ | Binary | $1$ if train $t_1$ traverses block $b$ before train $t_2$ (same direction), for $(t_1,t_2,b) \in SD$ |
| $x^{op}_{t_1,t_2,b}$ | Binary | $1$ if rerouted train $t_1$ passes the shared track before opposite-direction train $t_2$, for $(t_1,t_2,b) \in OP$ |
| $E_{t,b}$ | Continuous, $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on block $b$, for $(t,b) \in TB$ |
| $\Delta_{t,b,k}$ | Continuous, $[0,\, \Delta_{t,b,k}]$ | Incremental running-time variable for piece $k$ of the energy function, for $(t,b,k) \in TBK$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S: (t,s) \in TS} \bigl| a_t(s) - a^{pl}_t(s) \bigr| \;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{(t,b) \in TB} E_{t,b} \;+\; w_{\text{route}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}} R_t
$$

The absolute value is linearized with auxiliary continuous variables $y_t(s) \geq 0$:
$$
y_t(s) \geq a_t(s) - a^{pl}_t(s), \qquad y_t(s) \geq a^{pl}_t(s) - a_t(s), \qquad \forall (t,s) \in TS
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Consistency

**(C1) Minimum dwell time**
$$
d_t(s) \geq a_t(s) + \delta^{\min}_t(s), \qquad \forall (t,s) \in TS
$$

**(C2) Linking departure, running time, and arrival**
For each $(t,b) \in TB$, let $s_i$ be the origin station and $s_{i+1}$ the destination station of block $b$ in train $t$'s route:
$$
a_t(s_{i+1}) = d_t(s_i) + rt_{t,b}, \qquad \forall (t,b) \in TB
$$

**(C3) Running time bounds**
$$
rt^{\min}_{t,b} \leq rt_{t,b} \leq rt^{\max}_{t,b}, \qquad \forall (t,b) \in TB
$$

### 5.2 Disruption and Rerouting

**(C4) Non-rerouted affected trains must wait until disruption ends**
For each $t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}$, let $s_i$ be the station immediately before the disrupted block $b_d$ in train $t$'s route:
$$
d_t(s_i) \geq T_{\text{end}} - M \cdot R_t, \qquad \forall t \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}
$$
*Interpretation:* If $R_t = 0$ (not rerouted), the train cannot depart for the disrupted segment before $T_{\text{end}}$. If $R_t = 1$ (rerouted onto the opposite track), this constraint is deactivated.

### 5.3 Conflict / Ordering Constraints

**(C5) Same-direction ordering on a shared block (two constraints per pair)**
For each $(t_1, t_2, b) \in SD$, let $s^{to}_{t_1}$ be the destination station of block $b$ for train $t_1$, and $s^{from}_{t_2}$ the origin station of block $b$ for train $t_2$:

$$
a_{t_1}(s^{to}_{t_1}) + H_{\min} \;\leq\; d_{t_2}(s^{from}_{t_2}) + M\bigl(1 - x^{sd}_{t_1,t_2,b}\bigr)
$$
$$
a_{t_2}(s^{to}_{t_2}) + H_{\min} \;\leq\; d_{t_1}(s^{from}_{t_1}) + M \cdot x^{sd}_{t_1,t_2,b}
$$

*Interpretation:* Exactly one of the two trains precedes the other on the block, with a minimum headway $H_{\min}$.

**(C6) Opposite-direction ordering on the shared track during rerouting (two constraints per pair)**
For each $(t_1, t_2, b_d) \in OP$, where $t_1 \in \mathcal{T}_{\text{aff}}$ is rerouted onto the track used by $t_2$:

$$
a_{t_1}(s^{to}_{t_1}) + H_{\text{opp}} \;\leq\; d_{t_2}(s^{from}_{t_2}) + M\bigl(1 - R_{t_1}\bigr) + M\bigl(1 - x^{op}_{t_1,t_2,b_d}\bigr)
$$
$$
a_{t_2}(s^{to}_{t_2}) + H_{\text{opp}} \;\leq\; d_{t_1}(s^{from}_{t_1}) + M\bigl(1 - R_{t_1}\bigr) + M \cdot x^{op}_{t_1,t_2,b_d}
$$

*Interpretation:* If $R_{t_1} = 0$ (train $t_1$ is not rerouted), the constraints are deactivated (big-M terms vanish). If $R_{t_1} = 1$, the two trains must be separated by at least $H_{\text{opp}}$ on the shared physical track, with exactly one passing before the other.

### 5.4 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Approximation)

Assume energy $E_{t,b}$ is a decreasing convex function of running time $rt_{t,b}$, approximated by $K_{\text{pieces}}$ linear pieces over $[rt^{\min}_{t,b},\, rt^{\max}_{t,b}]$.

**(C7) Energy definition**
$$
E_{t,b} = E^{\min}_{t,b} + \sum_{k \in K} \text{slope}_{t,b,k} \cdot \Delta_{t,b,k}, \qquad \forall (t,b) \in TB
$$
where $\text{slope}_{t,b,k} < 0$ (energy decreases as running time increases).

**(C8) Running time decomposition**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} \Delta_{t,b,k} = rt_{t,b} - rt^{\min}_{t,b}, \qquad \forall (t,b) \in TB
$$

**(C9) Piece-length bounds**
$$
0 \leq \Delta_{t,b,k} \leq \frac{rt^{\max}_{t,b} - rt^{\min}_{t,b}}{K_{\text{pieces}}}, \qquad \forall (t,b) \in TB,\; \forall k \in K
$$

### 5.5 Temporal Bounds

**(C10)**
$$
0 \leq a_t(s) \leq T_{\max}, \qquad 0 \leq d_t(s) \leq T_{\max}, \qquad \forall (t,s) \in TS
$$

---

## 6. Key Assumptions

1. **Continuous time** is used for arrival/departure/running-time variables (no explicit time discretization grid is imposed on the scheduling variables).
2. **No train cancellations** are considered in this formulation; all trains complete their full route.
3. **Rerouting** is limited to the single disrupted block $b_d$; affected trains either use the opposite track on $b_d$ or wait before $b_d$ until the disruption ends.
4. **Energy function** $E_{t,b} = f(rt_{t,b})$ is modeled as a piecewise-linear, convex, decreasing function of running time. The piece slopes $\text{slope}_{t,b,k}$ and breakpoints are given as parameters derived from train traction/braking data.
5. **Ordering binary variables** are defined for every pair of trains that share a block in the same direction, and for every pair where one train is affected by the disruption and the other travels in the opposite direction on the same physical track.
6. **Headways** $H_{\min}$ and $H_{\text{opp}}$ are fixed constants representing the minimum time separation required for safe operation.
7. **The disruption blocks only one direction** on block $b_d$; trains in the unblocked direction operate normally on their own track.
8. **The big-M value** is set to $T_{\max}$, the maximum planning horizon, which is a valid and tight enough bound for this formulation.

---

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Problem:** A high-speed railway line experiences a partial segment blockage on segment $k^*$ during time window $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$, blocking one direction of travel. Affected trains may be rerouted to the opposite track (shared with oncoming trains), creating bidirectional conflicts. The model simultaneously optimizes train timetables (arrival/departure times, ordering, rerouting) and speed profiles (piecewise-constant speeds) to minimize total delay, energy consumption, and operational penalties while ensuring conflict-free operation.

**Assumptions:**
- The railway line has $N$ stations and $N-1$ track segments, with one track per direction.
- The disruption blocks one direction on segment $k^*$ for a known time window $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.
- Trains in the affected direction may be rerouted to the opposite track on segment $k^*$.
- Speed profiles are piecewise-constant over $J$ fixed time sub-intervals of duration $\Delta t$ per segment.
- The running time on each segment is fixed at $T_{run} = J \cdot \Delta t$ (speed management optimizes energy for a given running time window).
- Energy consumption is dominated by resistance and kinetic energy changes, linearized via convex hull approximation.
- Train cancellations are permitted but heavily penalized.
- The model covers a finite time horizon from disruption onset to full recovery.
- All trains have identical mass $m$ and resistance coefficient $F_{res}$ (simplification; can be extended to train-specific parameters).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $S = \{1, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations |
| $K = \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of track segments (segment $k$ connects station $k$ to $k+1$) |
| $T = \{1, \dots, M\}$ | Set of trains |
| $T_{dir}$ | Subset of trains traveling in the direction affected by the disruption |
| $T_{opp}$ | Subset of trains traveling in the opposite (unaffected) direction |
| $J = \{1, \dots, J_{max}\}$ | Set of speed sub-intervals per segment |
| $k^*$ | Index of the disrupted segment |
| $P_{t,t',k}$ | Set of train pairs $(t,t')$ that may conflict on segment $k$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $A^{sched}_{t,s}, D^{sched}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival/departure time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $L_k$ | Length of segment $k$ |
| $\Delta t$ | Duration of each speed sub-interval (fixed) |
| $T_{run} = J_{max} \cdot \Delta t$ | Fixed running time per segment |
| $v_{min}, v_{max}$ | Minimum/maximum allowed speeds |
| $a_{max}, b_{max}$ | Maximum acceleration/deceleration rates |
| $dwell_{min,t,s}$ | Minimum dwell time for train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum headway between trains on the same track |
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Disruption time window on segment $k^*$ |
| $m$ | Train mass |
| $F_{res}$ | Resistance force coefficient |
| $M_{big}$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |
| $w_{delay}, w_{energy}, w_{cancel}, w_{reroute}$ | Objective function weights |
| $P_{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling a train |
| $v_{nom}$ | Nominal speed for linearization of $v^2$ |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $A_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $v_{t,k,j} \geq 0$ | Speed of train $t$ on segment $k$ during sub-interval $j$ |
| $q_{t,k,j} \geq 0$ | Auxiliary variable approximating $v_{t,k,j}^2$ |
| $E_{t,k} \geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $k$ |
| $delay^+_{t,s}, delay^-_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Positive/negative arrival time deviation |
| $dep\_delay^+_{t,s}, dep\_delay^-_{t,s} \geq 0$ | Positive/negative departure time deviation |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| $c_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled, 0 otherwise |
| $x_{t} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t \in T_{dir}$ is rerouted on segment $k^*$, 0 otherwise |
| $z_{t,t',k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $k$ (same direction) |
| $w_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if rerouted train $t$ precedes oncoming train $t'$ on segment $k^*$ |
| $late_t \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ traverses segment $k^*$ after $t_{end}$, 0 if before $t_{start}$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_{delay} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \left( delay^+_{t,s} + delay^-_{t,s} + dep\_delay^+_{t,s} + dep\_delay^-_{t,s} \right) + w_{energy} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} E_{t,k} + w_{cancel} \sum_{t \in T} P_{cancel} \cdot c_t + w_{reroute} \sum_{t \in T_{dir}} x_t
$$

**Interpretation:**
- **Delay term:** Total absolute deviation of arrival and departure times from the scheduled timetable.
- **Energy term:** Total energy consumption across all trains and segments.
- **Cancellation penalty:** Heavy penalty for each cancelled train.
- **Rerouting penalty:** Small penalty to discourage unnecessary rerouting.

---

## 6. Constraints

### A. Train Cancellation Logic

**(A1)** Deactivation of timing variables for cancelled trains:
$$
A_{t,s} \leq M_{big}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
D_{t,s} \leq M_{big}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$

**(A2)** Deactivation of speed variables for cancelled trains:
$$
v_{t,k,j} \leq v_{max}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J
$$

**(A3)** Zero delay for cancelled trains:
$$
delay^+_{t,s} + delay^-_{t,s} \leq M_{big}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
dep\_delay^+_{t,s} + dep\_delay^-_{t,s} \leq M_{big}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$

---

### B. Timing and Dwell Constraints

**(B1)** Departure after arrival with minimum dwell:
$$
D_{t,s} \geq A_{t,s} + dwell_{min,t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S \setminus \{N\}
$$

**(B2)** Running time linkage (fixed running time per segment):
$$
A_{t,k+1} = D_{t,k} + T_{run} \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$

---

### C. Delay Deviation Linearization

**(C1)** Arrival time deviation:
$$
A_{t,s} - A^{sched}_{t,s} \leq delay^+_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
A^{sched}_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \leq delay^-_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$

**(C2)** Departure time deviation:
$$
D_{t,s} - D^{sched}_{t,s} \leq dep\_delay^+_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$
$$
D^{sched}_{t,s} - D_{t,s} \leq dep\_delay^-_{t,s} \quad \forall t \in T, \; s \in S
$$

---

### D. Speed Profile Constraints

**(D1)** Distance constraint (speed profile must cover segment length):
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{J_{max}} v_{t,k,j} \cdot \Delta t = L_k (1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$

**(D2)** Speed limits:
$$
v_{min}(1 - c_t) \leq v_{t,k,j} \leq v_{max}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J
$$

**(D3)** Acceleration limit:
$$
v_{t,k,j+1} - v_{t,k,j} \leq a_{max} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J \setminus \{J_{max}\}
$$

**(D4)** Deceleration limit:
$$
v_{t,k,j} - v_{t,k,j+1} \leq b_{max} \cdot \Delta t \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J \setminus \{J_{max}\}
$$

**(D5)** Boundary speed conditions (train starts and ends each segment at minimum speed, e.g., at stations):
$$
v_{t,k,1} \leq v_{min} + M_{big} \cdot c_t \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$
$$
v_{t,k,J_{max}} \leq v_{min} + M_{big} \cdot c_t \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$

---

### E. Energy Consumption (Linearized)

The energy consumption on segment $k$ for train $t$ is:
$$
E_{t,k} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(v_{t,k,J_{max}}^2 - v_{t,k,1}^2\right) + F_{res} \cdot \Delta t \sum_{j=1}^{J_{max}} v_{t,k,j}
$$

To linearize the quadratic term $v^2$, we introduce auxiliary variables $q_{t,k,j}$ with convex hull constraints:

**(E1)** Lower bound (tangent at $v_{min}$):
$$
q_{t,k,j} \geq 2v_{min} \cdot v_{t,k,j} - v_{min}^2 \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J
$$

**(E2)** Upper bound (tangent at $v_{max}$):
$$
q_{t,k,j} \leq 2v_{max} \cdot v_{t,k,j} - v_{max}^2 \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K, \; j \in J
$$

**(E3)** Energy calculation:
$$
E_{t,k} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(q_{t,k,J_{max}} - q_{t,k,1}\right) + F_{res} \cdot \Delta t \sum_{j=1}^{J_{max}} v_{t,k,j} \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$

**(E4)** Energy non-negativity and deactivation:
$$
E_{t,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$
$$
E_{t,k} \leq M_{big}(1 - c_t) \quad \forall t \in T, \; k \in K
$$

---

### F. Headway and Ordering Constraints (Same Direction)

**(F1)** Ordering completeness for conflicting same-direction pairs:
$$
z_{t,t',k} + z_{t',t,k} = 1 \quad \forall (t,t') \in P_{t,t',k}, \; t \neq t', \; k \in K
$$

**(F2)** Headway enforcement (if $t$ precedes $t'$, then $t'$ enters segment $k$ after $t$ exits):
$$
D_{t',k} \geq A_{t,k+1} + h_{min} - M_{big}(1 - z_{t,t',k}) - M_{big}c_t - M_{big}c_{t'} \quad \forall (t,t') \in P_{t,t',k}, \; k \in K
$$
$$
D_{t,k} \geq A_{t',k+1} + h_{min} - M_{big}(1 - z_{t',t,k}) - M_{big}c_t - M_{big}c_{t'} \quad \forall (t,t') \in P_{t,t',k}, \; k \in K
$$

---

### G. Rerouting and Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (Disrupted Segment $k^*$)

**(G1)** Rerouting decision (only for affected-direction trains):
$$
x_t \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}
$$

**(G2)** Bidirectional ordering completeness (between rerouted trains and oncoming trains):
$$
w_{t,t'} + w_{t',t} = 1 \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}, \; t' \in T_{opp}
$$

**(G3)** Bidirectional headway enforcement on shared track:
If train $t \in T_{dir}$ is rerouted ($x_t = 1$), it shares the track with oncoming trains $t' \in T_{opp}$ on segment $k^*$. They must not overlap:

$$
A_{t,k^*+1} \leq D_{t',k^*} - h_{min} + M_{big}(1 - w_{t,t'}) + M_{big}(1 - x_t) + M_{big}c_t + M_{big}c_{t'} \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}, \; t' \in T_{opp}
$$
$$
A_{t',k^*+1} \leq D_{t,k^*} - h_{min} + M_{big} \cdot w_{t,t'} + M_{big}(1 - x_t) + M_{big}c_t + M_{big}c_{t'} \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}, \; t' \in T_{opp}
$$

**Interpretation:** If $x_t = 0$ (not rerouted), the $M_{big}(1-x_t)$ term deactivates the constraint (trains are on different tracks). If $x_t = 1$ (rerouted), the constraint enforces that either $t$ exits before $t'$ enters (if $w_{t,t'}=1$) or $t'$ exits before $t$ enters (if $w_{t,t'}=0$).

**(G4)** Same-direction ordering among rerouted trains on the shared track:
For pairs $t, t' \in T_{dir}$ both rerouted ($x_t = x_{t'} = 1$), they share the track and must maintain headway:
$$
D_{t',k^*} \geq A_{t,k^*+1} + h_{min} - M_{big}(1 - z_{t,t',k^*}) - M_{big}(1 - x_t) - M_{big}(1 - x_{t'}) \quad \forall t, t' \in T_{dir}, \; t \neq t'
$$
$$
D_{t,k^*} \geq A_{t',k^*+1} + h_{min} - M_{big}(1 - z_{t',t,k^*}) - M_{big}(1 - x_t) - M_{big}(1 - x_{t'}) \quad \forall t, t' \in T_{dir}, \; t \neq t'
$$

---

### H. Disruption Window Avoidance

**(H1)** Non-rerouted trains must avoid the disruption window on segment $k^*$:

If $x_t = 0$ (train $t$ is NOT rerouted), it must either:
- Complete traversal before $t_{start}$: $A_{t,k^*+1} \leq t_{start}$, or
- Begin traversal after $t_{end}$: $D_{t,k^*} \geq t_{end}$

This disjunction is modeled using binary $late_t$:

$$
A_{t,k^*+1} \leq t_{start} + M_{big} \cdot late_t + M_{big} \cdot x_t \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}
$$
$$
D_{t,k^*} \geq t_{end} - M_{big}(1 - late_t) - M_{big} \cdot x_t \quad \forall t \in T_{dir}
$$

**Interpretation:**
- If $x_t = 1$ (rerouted): Both $M_{big} \cdot x_t$ terms are large, making constraints inactive (train is on the opposite track, unaffected by the blockage).
- If $x_t = 0$ (not rerouted): 
  - If $late_t = 0$: $A_{t,k^*+1} \leq t_{start}$ (train finishes before disruption starts).
  - If $late_t = 1$: $D_{t,k^*} \geq t_{end}$ (train starts after disruption ends).

---

### I. Non-Negativity and Domain Constraints

$$
A_{t,s}, D_{t,s}, v_{t,k,j}, q_{t,k,j}, E_{t,k}, delay^+_{t,s}, delay^-_{t,s}, dep\_delay^+_{t,s}, dep\_delay^-_{t,s} \geq 0
$$
$$
c_t, x_t, z_{t,t',k}, w_{t,t'}, late_t \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Key Features |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Objective** | Multi-criteria: delay + energy + cancellation + rerouting penalties |
| **Retiming** | Arrival/departure times with dwell constraints and fixed running times |
| **Reordering** | Binary ordering variables with Big-M headway constraints |
| **Rerouting** | Binary decision to divert affected trains to opposite track |
| **Speed Management** | Piecewise-constant speed profiles with acceleration/deceleration limits |
| **Energy** | Linearized via convex hull approximation of $v^2$ |
| **Conflict Resolution** | Same-direction headways + bidirectional headways on shared track |
| **Disruption Handling** | Disjunctive constraint forcing non-rerouted trains to avoid blocked window |

**Model Size:** The model has $O(M \cdot N)$ timing variables, $O(M \cdot (N-1) \cdot J_{max})$ speed variables, $O(M^2 \cdot (N-1))$ ordering binaries (for conflicting pairs only), and $O(M)$ rerouting/cancellation binaries. The number of constraints is polynomial in the problem dimensions, making it solvable for moderate instance sizes using commercial MILP solvers.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage Disruptions

## Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $r$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $A$ | Set of track segments (arcs between consecutive stations), indexed by $a$ |
| $D \subseteq A$ | Set of disruption-affected segments |
| $K_{r,a}$ | Set of feasible speed profiles for train $r$ on segment $a$, indexed by $k$ |
| $P_r$ | Set of feasible paths (routes) for train $r$, indexed by $p$ |
| $S_r$ | Set of stations visited by train $r$ |
| $A_r$ | Set of segments traversed by train $r$ |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $t_0^r$ | Scheduled departure time of train $r$ from its origin |
| $t_1^r$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $r$ at its destination |
| $\bar{t}^{arr}_{r,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $r$ at station $s$ |
| $\bar{t}^{dep}_{r,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $r$ from station $s$ |
| $\tau^{\min}_{r,a,k}$ | Minimum running time for train $r$ on segment $a$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $\tau^{\max}_{r,a,k}$ | Maximum running time for train $r$ on segment $a$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $e_{r,a,k}$ | Energy consumption for train $r$ on segment $a$ with speed profile $k$ |
| $d^{\min}_{r,s}$ | Minimum dwell time for train $r$ at station $s$ |
| $d^{\max}_{r,s}$ | Maximum dwell time for train $r$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{\min}_a$ | Minimum headway between consecutive trains on segment $a$ |
| $h^{\max}_a$ | Maximum headway between consecutive trains on segment $a$ |
| $T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start},a}$ | Start time of disruption on segment $a$ |
| $T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end},a}$ | End time of disruption on segment $a$ |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4$ | Objective function weights |
| $\pi^{\text{cancel}}_r$ | Penalty for cancelling train $r$ |
| $\pi^{\text{reroute}}_{r,a}$ | Penalty for rerouting train $r$ on segment $a$ |
| $C^{\text{plat}}_s$ | Platform capacity at station $s$ |
| $C^{\text{track}}_a$ | Track capacity on segment $a$ |
| $s^{\text{prev}}_{r,s}$ | Previous station of $s$ for train $r$ |
| $a_{r,s}$ | Segment between $s^{\text{prev}}_{r,s}$ and $s$ for train $r$ |

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{r,a,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $r$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $a$, 0 otherwise |
| $y_{r,p}$ | Binary | 1 if train $r$ uses path $p$, 0 otherwise |
| $z_r$ | Binary | 1 if train $r$ is cancelled, 0 otherwise |
| $t^{arr}_{r,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $r$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{dep}_{r,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Departure time of train $r$ from station $s$ |
| $\tau_{r,a}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Running time of train $r$ on segment $a$ |
| $o_{r_1,r_2,a}$ | Binary | 1 if train $r_1$ precedes train $r_2$ on segment $a$, 0 otherwise |
| $\rho_{r,a}$ | Binary | 1 if train $r$ is rerouted (uses opposite track) on segment $a$, 0 otherwise |
| $c_{r_1,r_2,a}$ | Binary | 1 if train $r_1$ precedes train $r_2$ on bidirectional segment $a$, 0 otherwise |
| $\delta^{arr}_{r,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Absolute deviation of arrival time from schedule at station $s$ |
| $\delta^{dep}_{r,s}$ | Continuous $\geq 0$ | Absolute deviation of departure time from schedule at station $s$ |

## Objective Function

Minimize the total operational cost:

$$\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{r \in T} \sum_{s \in S_r} \left( \delta^{arr}_{r,s} + \delta^{dep}_{r,s} \right) + w_2 \sum_{r \in T} \sum_{a \in A_r} \sum_{k \in K_{r,a}} e_{r,a,k} \, x_{r,a,k} + w_3 \sum_{r \in T} \pi^{\text{cancel}}_r \, z_r + w_4 \sum_{r \in T} \sum_{a \in A_r} \pi^{\text{reroute}}_{r,a} \, \rho_{r,a}$$

where:
- The first term penalizes deviations from the scheduled timetable (retiming cost)
- The second term minimizes total energy consumption across all speed profiles
- The third term penalizes train cancellations
- The fourth term penalizes the use of rerouting strategies

## Constraints

### 1. Path Selection (each train uses exactly one path)

$$\sum_{p \in P_r} y_{r,p} = 1 \quad \forall \, r \in T$$

### 2. Speed Profile Selection (each train uses exactly one speed profile per segment)

$$\sum_{k \in K_{r,a}} x_{r,a,k} = 1 \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A_r$$

### 3. Running Time Bounds (linking speed profile to running time)

$$\tau^{\min}_{r,a,k} \, x_{r,a,k} \leq \tau_{r,a} \leq \tau^{\max}_{r,a,k} \, x_{r,a,k} + M(1 - x_{r,a,k}) \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A_r, \; k \in K_{r,a}$$

### 4. Arrival–Departure Time Propagation

$$t^{arr}_{r,s} = t^{dep}_{r,\, s^{\text{prev}}_{r,s}} + \tau_{r,\, a_{r,s}} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r \setminus \{s^{\text{origin}}_r\}$$

### 5. Dwell Time Bounds

$$d^{\min}_{r,s} \leq t^{dep}_{r,s} - t^{arr}_{r,s} \leq d^{\max}_{r,s} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r \setminus \{s^{\text{origin}}_r, s^{\text{dest}}_r\}$$

### 6. Origin Departure Time

$$t^{dep}_{r,\, s^{\text{origin}}_r} \geq t_0^r \quad \forall \, r \in T$$

### 7. Destination Arrival Time (relaxed if cancelled)

$$t^{arr}_{r,\, s^{\text{dest}}_r} \leq t_1^r + M \, z_r \quad \forall \, r \in T$$

### 8. Cancellation Consistency (zero out times if cancelled)

$$t^{arr}_{r,s} \leq M(1 - z_r) \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

$$t^{dep}_{r,s} \leq M(1 - z_r) \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

### 9. Disruption Constraints (trains must avoid disrupted segments during the disruption window unless rerouted)

For each disrupted segment $a \in D$, train $r \in T$, and path $p \in P_r$ that traverses segment $a$:

$$t^{dep}_{r,\, s^{\text{prev}}_{r,a}} + \tau_{r,a} \geq T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{end},a} - M(1 - \rho_{r,a}) - M(1 - y_{r,p}) \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in D, \; p \in P_r \text{ with } a \in p$$

$$t^{dep}_{r,\, s^{\text{prev}}_{r,a}} \leq T^{\text{dis}}_{\text{start},a} - M(1 - \rho_{r,a}) - M(1 - y_{r,p}) \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in D, \; p \in P_r \text{ with } a \in p$$

*Assumption:* The disruption constraint is linearized using big-M. A train may traverse a disrupted segment only if it either (i) arrives after the disruption ends, (ii) departs before the disruption starts, or (iii) is rerouted onto the opposite track.

### 10. Same-Direction Headway Constraints (ordering on shared segments)

For any two distinct trains $r_1, r_2 \in T$ that both traverse segment $a$ in the same direction:

$$t^{dep}_{r_2,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} - t^{arr}_{r_1,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} \geq h^{\min}_a - M(1 - o_{r_1,r_2,a}) \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2, \; a \in A$$

$$t^{dep}_{r_1,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} - t^{arr}_{r_2,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} \geq h^{\min}_a - M \, o_{r_1,r_2,a} \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2, \; a \in A$$

where $s^{\text{end}}_a$ is the terminal station of segment $a$.

### 11. Bidirectional Conflict Constraints (opposing trains on shared/rerouted segments)

For any two trains $r_1, r_2 \in T$ traversing segment $a$ in opposite directions (e.g., one on the original track and one rerouted onto the opposite track):

$$t^{arr}_{r_1,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} \geq t^{dep}_{r_2,\, s^{\text{start}}_a} + h^{\min}_a - M(1 - c_{r_1,r_2,a}) \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2, \; a \in A$$

$$t^{arr}_{r_2,\, s^{\text{end}}_a} \geq t^{dep}_{r_1,\, s^{\text{start}}_a} + h^{\min}_a - M \, c_{r_1,r_2,a} \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2, \; a \in A$$

where $s^{\text{start}}_a$ is the origin station of segment $a$.

### 12. Platform Capacity

$$\sum_{r \in T} \mathbb{1}\!\left[t^{arr}_{r,s} \leq t \leq t^{dep}_{r,s}\right] \leq C^{\text{plat}}_s \quad \forall \, s \in S, \; t \in \mathcal{T}$$

*Assumption:* This is a time-indexed capacity constraint over a discrete time horizon $\mathcal{T}$. In practice, it can be linearized using binary occupancy variables or approximated by peak-load constraints.

### 13. Track Capacity

$$\sum_{r \in T} \mathbb{1}\!\left[t^{dep}_{r,\, s^{\text{start}}_a} \leq t \leq t^{arr}_{r,\, s^{\text{end}}_a}\right] \leq C^{\text{track}}_a \quad \forall \, a \in A, \; t \in \mathcal{T}$$

*Assumption:* Similar time-indexed formulation as platform capacity.

### 14. Rerouting Consistency

For each train $r$ and segment $a$, let $P^{\text{opp}}_{r,a}$ be the set of paths for train $r$ that use the opposite track on segment $a$, and $P^{\text{orig}}_{r,a}$ be the set of paths using the original track:

$$\rho_{r,a} \leq \sum_{p \in P^{\text{opp}}_{r,a}} y_{r,p} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A$$

$$\rho_{r,a} \geq y_{r,p} - 1 \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A, \; p \in P^{\text{orig}}_{r,a}$$

### 15. Schedule Deviation Linearization

$$\delta^{arr}_{r,s} \geq t^{arr}_{r,s} - \bar{t}^{arr}_{r,s} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

$$\delta^{arr}_{r,s} \geq \bar{t}^{arr}_{r,s} - t^{arr}_{r,s} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

$$\delta^{dep}_{r,s} \geq t^{dep}_{r,s} - \bar{t}^{dep}_{r,s} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

$$\delta^{dep}_{r,s} \geq \bar{t}^{dep}_{r,s} - t^{dep}_{r,s} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

### 16. Variable Domains

$$x_{r,a,k} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A_r, \; k \in K_{r,a}$$

$$y_{r,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; p \in P_r$$

$$z_r \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r \in T$$

$$o_{r_1,r_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2 \in T, \; a \in A$$

$$\rho_{r,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; a \in A$$

$$c_{r_1,r_2,a} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall \, r_1 \neq r_2 \in T, \; a \in A$$

$$t^{arr}_{r,s} \geq 0, \; t^{dep}_{r,s} \geq 0, \; \tau_{r,a} \geq 0 \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r, \; a \in A_r$$

$$\delta^{arr}_{r,s} \geq 0, \; \delta^{dep}_{r,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall \, r \in T, \; s \in S_r$$

## Key Assumptions

1. **Discretized speed profiles:** The continuous speed management problem is approximated by a finite set of pre-computed speed profiles $K_{r,a}$ for each train-segment pair, each with associated minimum/maximum running times and energy consumption. This is a standard linearization technique.

2. **Big-M formulation:** The disruption avoidance, cancellation, and ordering constraints use big-M linearization. The value of $M$ must be chosen sufficiently large to not cut off feasible solutions but as small as possible for computational efficiency.

3. **Time-indexed capacity constraints:** Platform and track capacity constraints are formulated over a discrete time horizon $\mathcal{T}$. In practice, these can be replaced by peak-load approximations or handled via the decomposition approach described in the paper.

4. **Single cancellation variable per train:** A train is either fully operated or fully cancelled ($z_r$ is a single binary per train, not per station).

5. **Fixed segment topology:** The network topology (stations and segments) is fixed; rerouting only changes which track (original or opposite) a train uses on a given segment, not the sequence of stations.

6. **Speed profile feasibility:** The running time bounds $\tau^{\min}_{r,a,k}$ and $\tau^{\max}_{r,a,k}$ implicitly encode acceleration/deceleration limits and speed limits. The coupling between consecutive segments' speed profiles (ensuring feasible speed transitions) is assumed to be captured in the pre-computed profile set.

7. **Conflict-free operation:** The headway and bidirectional conflict constraints ensure that no two trains occupy the same track segment simultaneously in a conflicting manner, guaranteeing a conflict-free rescheduled timetable.

Text:
# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description

This Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model addresses the integrated optimization of train timetables and speed profiles in response to a partial segment blockage disruption in a high-speed railway network. The model simultaneously determines retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed profile selection to minimize total passenger delay, energy consumption, and rerouting penalties while ensuring a conflict-free operation.

## 2. Assumptions

1. **Network Topology**: The railway line is linear with $N$ stations indexed $1, \dots, N$ and $N-1$ segments. Segment $k$ connects station $k$ to station $k+1$.
2. **Dual Track Structure**: Each segment has two tracks. Track 1 is the primary track for trains in direction $I^+$ (station $1 \to N$). Track 2 is the primary track for trains in direction $I^-$ (station $N \to 1$).
3. **Disruption**: Track 1 in segment $K_d$ (between station $d$ and $d+1$) is blocked during the time window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$. Trains cannot traverse this segment on Track 1 during this window.
4. **Rerouting**: Affected trains may be rerouted to the opposite (unblocked) track in segment $K_d$. Rerouting incurs an operational penalty.
5. **Discrete Speed Plans**: For each segment $k$, a finite set of pre-computed feasible speed plans $P_k$ is available. Each plan $p$ has a fixed running time $RT_{k,p}$ and energy consumption $E_{k,p}$. All plans satisfy dynamic constraints (max speed, acceleration, deceleration).
6. **Fixed Dwell Times**: Dwell times at stations are fixed at their scheduled values.
7. **No Overtaking**: The relative order of trains in the same direction is preserved from the original schedule.
8. **Unaffected Trains**: Trains that do not traverse the disrupted segment $K_d$ maintain their scheduled times.
9. **Same Speed Plans for Both Tracks**: The set of available speed plans $P_k$ is identical regardless of which track is used in segment $k$.
10. **No Train Cancellations**: All trains must be operated.
11. **Big-M Formulation**: A sufficiently large constant $M$ is used to linearize disjunctive and conditional constraints.

## 3. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $S = \{1, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations, ordered along the line |
| $K = \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of track segments; segment $k$ connects station $k$ to $k+1$ |
| $I$ | Set of all trains |
| $I^+ \subset I$ | Trains traveling in direction $1 \to N$ |
| $I^- \subset I$ | Trains traveling in direction $N \to 1$ |
| $K_d$ | Index of the disrupted segment (between station $d$ and $d+1$) |
| $I_{K_d} \subset I$ | Trains that traverse segment $K_d$ |
| $I_{K_d}^+ = I^+ \cap I_{K_d}$ | Trains in $I^+$ that traverse $K_d$ |
| $I_{K_d}^- = I^- \cap I_{K_d}$ | Trains in $I^-$ that traverse $K_d$ |
| $P_k$ | Set of feasible speed plans for segment $k$ |
| $stations(i)$ | Ordered set of stations visited by train $i$ |
| $origin(i)$ | Origin station of train $i$ |
| $dest(i)$ | Destination station of train $i$ |
| $O_{i,s}$ | Set of trains $j$ in the same direction as $i$ such that $j$ is scheduled to depart station $s$ before $i$ |

## 4. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $t^{sch}_{arr,i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{sch}_{dep,i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $RT_{k,p}$ | Running time for segment $k$ under speed plan $p$ |
| $E_{k,p}$ | Energy consumption for segment $k$ under speed plan $p$ |
| $Dwell_{i,s}$ | Fixed dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h_{min}$ | Minimum headway between consecutive same-direction trains at a station |
| $g_{min}$ | Minimum separation time between opposing trains sharing the unblocked track in $K_d$ |
| $T_{start}, T_{end}$ | Start and end times of the disruption window for segment $K_d$ |
| $D_{max}$ | Maximum allowable delay for any train |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective function weights for delay, energy, and rerouting |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |

## 5. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $d_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at its destination |

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses speed plan $p$ on segment $k$, 0 otherwise |
| $r_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track in $K_d$, 0 otherwise (defined for $i \in I_{K_d}$) |
| $v_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Disjunction variable for blocked track constraint (defined for $i \in I_{K_d}$) |
| $c_{i,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i \in I_{K_d}^+$ precedes train $j \in I_{K_d}^-$ on Track 2, 0 otherwise |
| $w_{i,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if both train $i \in I_{K_d}^+$ and train $j \in I_{K_d}^-$ use Track 2 in $K_d$, 0 otherwise |

## 6. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay, total energy consumption, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\min \quad Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in I} d_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{p \in P_k} E_{k,p} \, x_{i,k,p} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I_{K_d}} r_i
$$

## 7. Constraints

### 7.1 Speed Plan Selection

Each train must select exactly one speed plan for each segment it traverses:

$$
\sum_{p \in P_k} x_{i,k,p} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I, \; \forall k \in K \text{ traversed by } i \tag{1}
$$

### 7.2 Running Time Linking

The time to traverse a segment equals the running time of the selected speed plan.

**For trains in $I^+$ (direction $1 \to N$):**

$$
a_{i,k+1} - dep_{i,k} = \sum_{p \in P_k} RT_{k,p} \, x_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i \in I^+, \; \forall k \in K \text{ traversed by } i \tag{2a}
$$

**For trains in $I^-$ (direction $N \to 1$):**

$$
a_{i,k} - dep_{i,k+1} = \sum_{p \in P_k} RT_{k,p} \, x_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i \in I^-, \; \forall k \in K \text{ traversed by } i \tag{2b}
$$

### 7.3 Fixed Dwell Time

Departure time is arrival time plus the fixed dwell time:

$$
dep_{i,s} = a_{i,s} + Dwell_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in I, \; \forall s \in stations(i) \tag{3}
$$

### 7.4 Delay Definition and Bounds

The delay is the positive part of the difference between actual and scheduled arrival at the destination, bounded above by $D_{max}$:

$$
d_i \geq a_{i,dest(i)} - t^{sch}_{arr,i,dest(i)} \quad \forall i \in I \tag{4a}
$$

$$
d_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in I \tag{4b}
$$

$$
d_i \leq D_{max} \quad \forall i \in I \tag{4c}
$$

### 7.5 Origin Departure Constraint

Trains cannot depart their origin earlier than scheduled:

$$
dep_{i,origin(i)} \geq t^{sch}_{dep,i,origin(i)} \quad \forall i \in I \tag{5}
$$

### 7.6 No Overtaking / Headway Constraints

For same-direction trains, the scheduled departure order is preserved with a minimum headway. For each station $s$ and each pair $(i,j)$ where $j \in O_{i,s}$ (train $j$ is scheduled to depart station $s$ before train $i$, same direction):

$$
dep_{i,s} \geq dep_{j,s} + h_{min} \quad \forall i \in I, \; \forall s \in stations(i), \; \forall j \in O_{i,s} \tag{6}
$$

### 7.7 Blocked Track Constraint for $I^+$ Trains

For trains $i \in I_{K_d}^+$, if $r_i = 0$ (train uses the blocked Track 1), it must either complete the segment before $T_{start}$ or start the segment after $T_{end}$. If $r_i = 1$ (train is rerouted to unblocked Track 2), these constraints are relaxed.

$$
a_{i,d+1} \leq T_{start} + M(1 - v_i) + M \cdot r_i \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+ \tag{7a}
$$

$$
dep_{i,d} \geq T_{end} - M \cdot v_i - M \cdot r_i \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+ \tag{7b}
$$

**Logic**: If $r_i = 1$, the terms $M \cdot r_i = M$ make both constraints non-binding. If $r_i = 0$, the constraints reduce to $a_{i,d+1} \leq T_{start} + M(1-v_i)$ and $dep_{i,d} \geq T_{end} - M \cdot v_i$, enforcing that the train either finishes before the disruption starts ($v_i = 0$) or starts after it ends ($v_i = 1$).

### 7.8 Blocked Track Constraint for $I^-$ Trains

For trains $j \in I_{K_d}^-$, if $r_j = 1$ (train is rerouted to the blocked Track 1), it must either complete the segment before $T_{start}$ or start the segment after $T_{end}$. If $r_j = 0$ (train uses unblocked Track 2), these constraints are relaxed.

$$
a_{j,d} \leq T_{start} + M(1 - v_j) + M(1 - r_j) \quad \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{8a}
$$

$$
dep_{j,d+1} \geq T_{end} - M \cdot v_j - M(1 - r_j) \quad \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{8b}
$$

**Logic**: If $r_j = 0$, the terms $M(1-r_j) = M$ make both constraints non-binding. If $r_j = 1$, the constraints enforce that the train either arrives at station $d$ before $T_{start}$ ($v_j = 0$) or departs from station $d+1$ after $T_{end}$ ($v_j = 1$).

### 7.9 Track 2 Shared Usage Indicator

The variable $w_{i,j}$ equals 1 if and only if train $i \in I_{K_d}^+$ uses Track 2 ($r_i = 1$) AND train $j \in I_{K_d}^-$ uses Track 2 ($r_j = 0$):

$$
w_{i,j} \leq r_i \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{9a}
$$

$$
w_{i,j} \leq 1 - r_j \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{9b}
$$

$$
w_{i,j} \geq r_i + (1 - r_j) - 1 \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{9c}
$$

### 7.10 Sequencing Variable Bound

The sequencing variable is only active when both trains share Track 2:

$$
c_{i,j} \leq w_{i,j} \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{10}
$$

### 7.11 Separation Constraint: Train $i$ Precedes Train $j$

If $c_{i,j} = 1$ and $w_{i,j} = 1$, train $i$ must clear segment $K_d$ (arrive at station $d+1$) at least $g_{min}$ time before train $j$ enters the segment (departs from station $d+1$):

$$
a_{i,d+1} + g_{min} \leq dep_{j,d+1} + M(1 - c_{i,j}) + M(1 - w_{i,j}) \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{11}
$$

### 7.12 Separation Constraint: Train $j$ Precedes Train $i$

If $c_{i,j} = 0$ and $w_{i,j} = 1$, train $j$ must clear segment $K_d$ (arrive at station $d$) at least $g_{min}$ time before train $i$ enters the segment (departs from station $d$):

$$
a_{j,d} + g_{min} \leq dep_{i,d} + M \cdot c_{i,j} + M(1 - w_{i,j}) \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{12}
$$

**Logic**: When $w_{i,j} = 1$, exactly one of $c_{i,j}$ or $(1-c_{i,j})$ is 1, activating exactly one separation constraint. When $w_{i,j} = 0$, the term $M(1-w_{i,j}) = M$ relaxes both constraints.

### 7.13 Unaffected Trains Fixed to Schedule

Trains that do not traverse the disrupted segment maintain their scheduled times:

$$
a_{i,s} = t^{sch}_{arr,i,s} \quad \forall i \in I \setminus I_{K_d}, \; \forall s \in stations(i) \tag{13a}
$$

$$
dep_{i,s} = t^{sch}_{dep,i,s} \quad \forall i \in I \setminus I_{K_d}, \; \forall s \in stations(i) \tag{13b}
$$

### 7.14 Variable Domains

$$
a_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad dep_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad d_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in I, \; \forall s \in stations(i) \tag{14a}
$$

$$
x_{i,k,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in I, \; \forall k \in K, \; \forall p \in P_k \tag{14b}
$$

$$
r_i \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d} \tag{14c}
$$

$$
v_i \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d} \tag{14d}
$$

$$
c_{i,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{14e}
$$

$$
w_{i,j} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in I_{K_d}^+, \; \forall j \in I_{K_d}^- \tag{14f}
$$

## 8. Model Summary

| Component | Constraints | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| Speed Plan Selection | (1) | Exactly one speed profile per segment |
| Running Time Linking | (2a), (2b) | Link timetable to speed profiles |
| Fixed Dwell | (3) | Enforce scheduled dwell times |
| Delay Definition | (4a)-(4c) | Define and bound train delays |
| Origin Departure | (5) | No early departure |
| No Overtaking / Headway | (6) | Preserve order, maintain minimum headway |
| Blocked Track ($I^+$) | (7a), (7b) | Prevent use of blocked track during disruption |
| Blocked Track ($I^-$) | (8a), (8b) | Prevent use of blocked track during disruption |
| Track 2 Indicator | (9a)-(9c) | Detect when opposing trains share Track 2 |
| Sequencing Bound | (10) | Activate sequencing only when needed |
| Separation ($i$ before $j$) | (11) | Physical separation on shared track |
| Separation ($j$ before $i$) | (12) | Physical separation on shared track |
| Unaffected Trains | (13a), (13b) | Fix times of non-affected trains |
| Domains | (14a)-(14f) | Variable bounds and integrality |

This MILP model provides a complete, linear formulation that can be solved by standard solvers (e.g., CPLEX, Gurobi) to obtain an optimal conflict-free rescheduled timetable with corresponding feasible speed profiles under partial segment blockage disruptions.
