Based on the iterative development and feedback, here is the final, complete MILP model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockage disruptions:

---

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage: A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model

## 1. Problem Description

The TRSMP integrates train timetabling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with train speed management (running time/energy optimization) in the context of a partial segment blockage disruption. A set of segments on a bidirectional high-speed railway is blocked during a known time window. Affected trains may be rerouted to the opposite track, creating bidirectional track-sharing conflicts. The model simultaneously determines train times, orders, routes (normal vs. rerouted track), and speed profiles (via running times and energy) to minimize total operational cost while maintaining a conflict-free timetable.

## 2. Sets

| Set | Index | Description |
|-----|-------|-------------|
| $T$ | $t$ | Set of trains |
| $S$ | $s$ | Set of stations, indexed $s = 1, \ldots, |S|$ |
| $G$ | $g$ | Set of segments, where $g$ connects station $s_{\text{start}}(g)$ to station $s_{\text{end}}(g) = s_{\text{start}}(g)+1$ |
| $B \subseteq G$ | — | Set of blocked segments (disruption area) |
| $D = \{1, 2\}$ | — | Set of travel directions |
| $\mathcal{P}_t$ | — | Ordered sequence of stations in the path of train $t$ |
| $G_t \subseteq G$ | — | Set of segments traversed by train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | $k$ | Set of breakpoints of the energy function |
| $T_{\text{conf}}(g)$ | — | Set of pairs $\{(t,t')\}$ of trains that both traverse segment $g$ with $t \neq t'$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $d(t) \in D$ | Nominal (scheduled) direction of train $t$ |
| $t_{\text{start}}^{\text{dis}},\; t_{\text{end}}^{\text{dis}}$ | Start and end of the disruption time window |
| $A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $D^{\text{sched}}_{t,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $r^{\min}_{t,g},\; r^{\max}_{t,g}$ | Minimum/maximum feasible running time of train $t$ on segment $g$ |
| $w^{\min}_{t,s},\; w^{\max}_{t,s}$ | Minimum/maximum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau$ | Minimum headway (seconds) between consecutive trains on the same physical track segment |
| $T_{\max}$ | Planning horizon (maximum time) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M), $M \ge T_{\max}$ |
| $r_{t,g,k},\; e_{t,g,k}$ | Running-time and energy coordinates of the $k$-th breakpoint of train $t$'s energy curve on segment $g$, ordered so $r_{t,g,1} < r_{t,g,2} < \cdots < r_{t,g,|\mathcal{K}|}$ |
| $\lambda_{t,g,k}$ | Slope of the $k$-th linear piece: $\lambda_{t,g,k} = \dfrac{e_{t,g,k+1} - e_{t,g,k}}{r_{t,g,k+1} - r_{t,g,k}}$ |
| $E^{\max}_{t,g}$ | Upper bound on energy for train $t$ on segment $g$ (max of $e_{t,g,k}$ over $\mathcal{K}$) |
| $C_{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty cost for cancelling one train |
| $C_{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty cost per unit time of delay |
| $C_{\text{energy}}$ | Penalty cost per unit of energy consumed |
| $C_{\text{reroute}}$ | Penalty cost for rerouting a train on one segment |

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $A_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ |
| $r'_{t,g}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual running time of train $t$ on segment $g$ |
| $E_{t,g}$ | $\geq 0$ | Energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $g$ |
| $\Delta_{t,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $t$ at station $s$ relative to schedule |

### 4.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $c_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ is cancelled |
| $y_{t,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses its **normal** (direction-matched) track on segment $g$ |
| $z_{t,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ **reroutes** to the opposite track on segment $g$ |
| $b_{t,g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Disruption disjunction: 1 if train $t$ clears the blocked segment before $t_{\text{start}}^{\text{dis}}$; 0 if it enters after $t_{\text{end}}^{\text{dis}}$ |
| $\phi_{t,t',g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $t$ and $t'$ occupy the **same physical track** on segment $g$ |
| $o_{t,t',g}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $g$ (same physical track) |
| $u^i_{t,t',g}$ | $\{0,1\}$, $i=1,\ldots,4$ | Auxiliary AND variables for linearizing the physical-track conflict indicator |

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; C_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{t \in T} c_t \;+\; C_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{P}_t} \Delta_{t,s} \;+\; C_{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{g \in G_t} E_{t,g} \;+\; C_{\text{reroute}} \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{g \in G_t} z_{t,g}
$$

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Track Assignment

For every train $t \in T$ and every segment $g \in G_t$:

$$
y_{t,g} + z_{t,g} = 1 - c_t \tag{1}
$$

Rerouting is only permitted on blocked segments:

$$
z_{t,g} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\;\; g \in G_t \setminus B \tag{2}
$$

### 6.2 Time Consistency and Bounds

**Running time link** (for each train $t$ and segment $g \in G_t$ with $s_{\text{start}} = s_{\text{start}}(g)$, $s_{\text{end}} = s_{\text{end}}(g)$):

$$
r'_{t,g} = A_{t,\,s_{\text{end}}} - D_{t,\,s_{\text{start}}} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t \tag{3}
$$

**Running time bounds** (active trains only):

$$
r^{\min}_{t,g}(1 - c_t) \;\leq\; r'_{t,g} \;\leq\; r^{\max}_{t,g}(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t \tag{4}
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**

$$
D_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \;\geq\; w^{\min}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{5a}
$$

$$
D_{t,s} - A_{t,s} \;\leq\; w^{\max}_{t,s} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{5b}
$$

**Planning horizon and non-negativity:**

$$
0 \;\leq\; A_{t,s} \;\leq\; T_{\max} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{6a}
$$

$$
0 \;\leq\; D_{t,s} \;\leq\; T_{\max} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{6b}
$$

**Cancelled train deactivation:**

$$
A_{t,s} \;\leq\; M\,c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{7a}
$$

$$
D_{t,s} \;\leq\; M\,c_t \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{7b}
$$

> *Note:* When $c_t = 1$, constraints (7) force $A_{t,s} = D_{t,s} = 0$ (since they are non-negative and bounded above by $M \cdot 1 = M$, but combined with (6) bounded by $T_{\max}$; in practice, the objective will drive them to 0 as they contribute no benefit. For strict enforcement, one may add $A_{t,s} \leq T_{\max} c_t$ to ensure $A = 0$ when $c_t = 1$.)

### 6.3 Disruption (Blocked Segment) Constraints

For every train $t$ and every **blocked** segment $g \in G_t \cap B$:

If the train uses the **normal track** ($y_{t,g} = 1$), it must either exit before the disruption starts or enter after the disruption ends:

$$
A_{t,\,s_{\text{end}}(g)} \;\leq\; t_{\text{start}}^{\text{dis}} + M(1 - b_{t,g}) + M(1 - y_{t,g}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t \cap B \tag{8a}
$$

$$
D_{t,\,s_{\text{start}}(g)} \;\geq\; t_{\text{end}}^{\text{dis}} - M\,b_{t,g} - M(1 - y_{t,g}) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t \cap B \tag{8b}
$$

> *Logic:* If $y_{t,g} = 1$ (normal track on blocked segment), the $M(1-y)$ terms vanish, and the disjunction is enforced by $b_{t,g}$: either $b=1$ (exit before $t_{\text{start}}^{\text{dis}}$) or $b=0$ (enter after $t_{\text{end}}^{\text{dis}}$). If $y_{t,g} = 0$ (rerouted to opposite track, which is unblocked), the $M(1-y) = M$ terms dominate and the constraints are trivially satisfied.

### 6.4 Physical Track Conflict Indicator ($\phi$)

For each pair $(t, t') \in T_{\text{conf}}(g)$ with $t \neq t'$:

**Case A: Same direction ($d(t) = d(t')$)**

Trains share a physical track iff both use the normal track or both use the rerouted track:

$$
\phi_{t,t',g} = 1 \iff (y_{t,g}=1 \land y_{t',g}=1) \;\lor\; (z_{t,g}=1 \land z_{t',g}=1)
$$

Introduce AND variables $u^1_{t,t',g},\; u^2_{t,t',g}$:

$$
u^1_{t,t',g} \leq y_{t,g}, \quad u^1_{t,t',g} \leq y_{t',g}, \quad u^1_{t,t',g} \geq y_{t,g} + y_{t',g} - 1 \tag{9a}
$$

$$
u^2_{t,t',g} \leq z_{t,g}, \quad u^2_{t,t',g} \leq z_{t',g}, \quad u^2_{t,t',g} \geq z_{t,g} + z_{t',g} - 1 \tag{9b}
$$

OR-combination:

$$
\phi_{t,t',g} \geq u^1_{t,t',g}, \quad \phi_{t,t',g} \geq u^2_{t,t',g}, \quad \phi_{t,t',g} \leq u^1_{t,t',g} + u^2_{t,t',g} \tag{9c}
$$

**Case B: Opposite directions ($d(t) \neq d(t')$)**

Trains share a physical track iff one uses the normal track and the other uses the rerouted track (they meet on the "other" track):

$$
\phi_{t,t',g} = 1 \iff (y_{t,g}=1 \land z_{t',g}=1) \;\lor\; (z_{t,g}=1 \land y_{t',g}=1)
$$

Introduce AND variables $u^3_{t,t',g},\; u^4_{t,t',g}$:

$$
u^3_{t,t',g} \leq y_{t,g}, \quad u^3_{t,t',g} \leq z_{t',g}, \quad u^3_{t,t',g} \geq y_{t,g} + z_{t',g} - 1 \tag{10a}
$$

$$
u^4_{t,t',g} \leq z_{t,g}, \quad u^4_{t,t',g} \leq y_{t',g}, \quad u^4_{t,t',g} \geq z_{t,g} + y_{t',g} - 1 \tag{10b}
$$

OR-combination:

$$
\phi_{t,t',g} \geq u^3_{t,t',g}, \quad \phi_{t,t',g} \geq u^4_{t,t',g}, \quad \phi_{t,t',g} \leq u^3_{t,t',g} + u^4_{t,t',g} \tag{10c}
$$

### 6.5 Ordering and Headway Constraints

For every pair $(t, t') \in T_{\text{conf}}(g)$, $t \neq t'$, and segment $g$:

**Ordering completeness** (if same track, exactly one precedes):

$$
o_{t,t',g} + o_{t',t,g} = \phi_{t,t',g} \qquad \forall\, (t,t') \in T_{\text{conf}}(g),\; g \in G \tag{11}
$$

**Headway constraints** (if $t$ precedes $t'$, then $t'$ cannot enter the segment until $t$ has cleared it plus headway):

$$
D_{t',\,s_{\text{start}}(g)} \;\geq\; D_{t,\,s_{\text{start}}(g)} + r'_{t,g} + \tau \;-\; M\,(1 - o_{t,t',g}) \qquad \forall\, (t,t') \in T_{\text{conf}}(g),\; g \in G \tag{12a}
$$

$$
D_{t,\,s_{\text{start}}(g)} \;\geq\; D_{t',\,s_{\text{start}}(g)} + r'_{t',g} + \tau \;-\; M\,(1 - o_{t',t,g}) \qquad \forall\, (t,t') \in T_{\text{conf}}(g),\; g \in G \tag{12b}
$$

> *Note:* Since $o_{t,t',g} = 0$ when $\phi_{t,t',g} = 0$ (different tracks), the Big-M term relaxes the constraint, making it inactive.

### 6.6 Energy Consumption Model (Convex Piecewise Linear)

Assuming the energy function $e_{t,g}(r')$ is **convex** in running time $r'$, we use the tangent-line (epigraph) formulation. For all $t \in T$, $g \in G_t$, and each breakpoint $k \in \mathcal{K}$:

$$
E_{t,g} \;\geq\; e_{t,g,k} + \lambda_{t,g,k}\,\bigl(r'_{t,g} - r_{t,g,k}\bigr) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t,\; k \in \mathcal{K} \tag{13}
$$

Since the objective **minimizes** $E_{t,g}$, the solver will set $E_{t,g}$ to the tightest (maximum) of the tangent lines, which equals $e_{t,g}(r'_{t,g})$ for a convex piecewise-linear function.

**Energy–cancellation link:**

$$
E_{t,g} \;\leq\; E^{\max}_{t,g}\,(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; g \in G_t \tag{14}
$$

### 6.7 Delay Calculation

For every train $t$ and station $s$ in its path:

$$
\Delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; A_{t,s} - A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s} \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{15a}
$$

$$
\Delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in T,\; s \in \mathcal{P}_t \tag{15b}
$$

> Since the objective minimizes $\Delta_{t,s}$, at optimality $\Delta_{t,s} = \max(0,\; A_{t,s} - A^{\text{sched}}_{t,s})$.

### 6.8 Variable Domains and Integrality

$$
A_{t,s},\; D_{t,s},\; r'_{t,g},\; E_{t,g},\; \Delta_{t,s} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \text{(continuous)} \tag{16a}
$$

$$
c_t,\; y_{t,g},\; z_{t,g},\; b_{t,g},\; \phi_{t,t',g},\; o_{t,t',g},\; u^i_{t,t',g} \;\in\; \{0,1\} \quad \text{(binary)} \tag{16b}
$$

## 7. Modeling Assumptions

1. **Fixed paths:** Each train has a fixed sequence of stations. Rerouting is limited to track selection (normal vs. opposite) on blocked segments; no alternative routing through different stations is considered. *(Assumption – consistent with the partial blockage context.)*
2. **Double track per direction:** Each segment has two physical tracks (one per direction). Rerouting moves a train to the opposite direction's track. *(Standard for high-speed railways.)*
3. **Deterministic disruption:** The disruption time window $[t_{\text{start}}^{\text{dis}}, t_{\text{end}}^{\text{dis}}]$ is known and fixed.
4. **Convex energy function:** Energy consumption as a function of running time is convex (e.g., higher energy for both very fast and very slow running). This allows exact linearization without additional binary variables. If the energy function is non-convex, an alternative segment-selection formulation with additional binaries $\delta_{t,g,k}$ would be required.
5. **No overtaking on same track:** The ordering variables and headway constraints enforce a fixed sequence of trains on each physical track segment.
6. **Uniform headway:** A single minimum headway $\tau$ applies to all train pairs on the same track segment. (In practice, this could be pair-specific.)
7. **Big-M validity:** $M \geq T_{\max}$ ensures all Big-M constraints are valid (i.e., the relaxation is not infeasible).
8. **Dwell time flexibility:** Dwell times can vary within $[w^{\min}_{t,s}, w^{\max}_{t,s}]$, allowing the model to hold trains at stations to resolve conflicts.
9. **Single disruption event:** One disruption affecting segments in $B$ over a single time window. Multiple simultaneous disruptions would require additional sets and parameters.
10. **No capacity limits at stations:** Platform occupancy limits at stations are not modeled; only segment-level headway constraints enforce capacity. *(Assumption – could be extended with station capacity constraints.)*

---

This formulation is a complete, self-contained MILP. It simultaneously optimizes train times (retiming), train order (reordering via $o$ variables), track assignment (rerouting via $z$), train cancellations ($c$), and speed profiles (running times $r'$ with energy $E$), while enforcing conflict-free operation through headway constraints and respecting the disruption via the disjunctive blocked-segment logic.

Based on the iterative refinement, here is the final, complete MILP model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under a partial segment blockage disruption.

---

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model: TRSMP under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

**Context:** A high-speed railway corridor experiences a partial segment blockage. One track direction is blocked on a specific segment during a time window. The operator must reschedule train times, decide rerouting (using the opposite track), determine train orderings, and set running times (speed profiles) to minimize delay and energy while ensuring a conflict-free timetable.

**Key Assumptions:**
1.  **Single Corridor:** The line is a sequence of $N$ stations $s_1, \dots, s_N$ connected by segments $j=1, \dots, N-1$.
2.  **Two Directions:** Trains travel either East ($d=1$) or West ($d=-1$).
3.  **Single Disruption:** One segment $j_b$ in direction $d_{blocked}$ is blocked during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$.
4.  **Rerouting:** Affected trains in direction $d_{blocked}$ may use the opposite track on segment $j_b$ during the disruption window, incurring a time penalty $\Delta t_{reroute}$.
5.  **Speed Management:** Running times $RT(i,j)$ are decision variables within $[RT_{min}, RT_{max}]$. Energy is linearly approximated as increasing with speed (decreasing $RT$).
6.  **Fixed Stops:** Pass-through stations are handled by zero dwell time.
7.  **Conflict-Free:** Minimum headways are enforced for same-direction and (conditionally) opposite-direction trains.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $S = \{1, \dots, N\}$ | Set of stations in order along the corridor |
| $J = \{1, \dots, N-1\}$ | Set of segments (segment $j$ connects $s_j$ to $s_{j+1}$) |
| $I$ | Set of trains |
| $S(i)$ | Set of stations visited by train $i$ |
| $J(i)$ | Set of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $I_{blk}$ | Set of trains in direction $d_{blocked}$ that traverse segment $j_b$ |
| $I_{opp}$ | Set of trains in direction $-d_{blocked}$ that traverse segment $j_b$ |
| $P_{seg}(j)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{i, i'\}$ traveling same direction on segment $j$ |
| $P_{stn}(s)$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{i, i'\}$ stopping at station $s$ in same direction |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $A_{sched}(i,s)$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $D_{sched}(i,s)$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $RT_{min}(i,j)$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $RT_{max}(i,j)$ | Maximum running time of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $RT_{orig}(i,j)$ | Original scheduled running time (for reference) |
| $Dwell_{min}(i,s)$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ ($0$ if pass-through) |
| $Dwell_{max}(i,s)$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $T_{start}, T_{end}$ | Start and end of the disruption time window |
| $j_b, s_{b1}, s_{b2}$ | Disrupted segment and its origin/destination stations |
| $d_{blocked}$ | The blocked direction |
| $\Delta t_{reroute}$ | Additional time penalty for using the opposite track |
| $h_{min}(j)$ | Minimum headway for same-direction trains on segment $j$ |
| $h_{opp}$ | Minimum separation for opposite-direction trains on shared track |
| $w_i$ | Passenger/weight factor for train $i$ |
| $C_{delay}$ | Cost per unit time of delay |
| $C_{energy}$ | Cost per unit energy |
| $C_{reroute}$ | Fixed cost penalty for a rerouting decision |
| $a_E(i,j)$ | Energy sensitivity coefficient ($>0$) |
| $b_E(i,j)$ | Base energy offset ($\ge 0$) |
| $\Delta RT_{max}$ | Maximum allowed change in running time between consecutive segments |
| $T_H$ | Planning horizon (upper bound for all time variables) |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M) |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Continuous Variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $ARR(i,s)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $DEP(i,s)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $RT(i,j)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Actual running time of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $PT(i,j)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Midpoint passage time of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $DEL\_ARR(i,s)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $DEL\_DEP(i,s)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Departure delay of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $E(i,j)$ | $\mathbb{R}^+$ | Energy consumed by train $i$ on segment $j$ |

### Binary Variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $X(i)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i \in I_{blk}$ reroutes (uses opposite track on $j_b$) |
| $Y(i)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i \in I_{blk}$ passes segment $j_b$ before $T_{start}$ |
| $Z(i)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i \in I_{blk}$ passes segment $j_b$ after $T_{end}$ |
| $H(i,i',j)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ arrives at end of segment $j$ before train $i'$ (same direction) |
| $O(i,i',s)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ before train $i'$ arrives (platform order) |
| $B(i,i')$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if rerouted train $i$ passes segment $j_b$ midpoint before opposing train $i'$ |

*Note: $X(i), Y(i), Z(i)$ are only defined for $i \in I_{blk}$. For all other trains, they are fixed to 0.*

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay, energy consumption, and rerouting penalties:

$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S(i)} w_i \cdot C_{delay} \left[ DEL\_ARR(i,s) + DEL\_DEP(i,s) \right] + C_{energy} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J(i)} E(i,j) + C_{reroute} \sum_{i \in I_{blk}} X(i)
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

### A. Timing Consistency

**(1) Segment Timing Link**
For all $i \in I$, $j \in J(i)$, where segment $j$ connects $s_{origin}(j)$ to $s_{dest}(j)$:
$$
ARR(i, s_{dest}(j)) = DEP(i, s_{origin}(j)) + RT(i,j) \tag{1}
$$

**(2) Dwell Time Bounds**
For all $i \in I$, $s \in S(i)$ (intermediate stations and origin/destination as applicable):
$$
Dwell_{min}(i,s) \le DEP(i,s) - ARR(i,s) \le Dwell_{max}(i,s) \tag{2}
$$
*(For pass-through stations: $Dwell_{min} = Dwell_{max} = 0$, so $DEP(i,s) = ARR(i,s)$.)*

**(3) Running Time Bounds**
For all $i \in I$, $j \in J(i)$, $j \neq j_b$:
$$
RT_{min}(i,j) \le RT(i,j) \le RT_{max}(i,j) \tag{3a}
$$

For $i \in I_{blk}$, $j = j_b$ (with rerouting penalty):
$$
RT_{min}(i,j_b) + \Delta t_{reroute} \cdot X(i) \le RT(i,j_b) \le RT_{max}(i,j_b) + \Delta t_{reroute} \cdot X(i) \tag{3b}
$$

**(4) Speed Profile Smoothness**
For all $i \in I$, consecutive segments $j, j+1 \in J(i)$:
$$
RT(i,j+1) - RT(i,j) \le \Delta RT_{max} \tag{4a}
$$
$$
RT(i,j) - RT(i,j+1) \le \Delta RT_{max} \tag{4b}
$$

**(5) Midpoint Passage Time Definition**
For all $i \in I$, $j \in J(i)$:
$$
PT(i,j) = DEP(i, s_{origin}(j)) + \frac{1}{2} RT(i,j) \tag{5}
$$

### B. Disruption and Rerouting Logic

**(6) Three-Way Partition**
For all $i \in I_{blk}$:
$$
X(i) + Y(i) + Z(i) = 1 \tag{6}
$$

**(7) Pass Before Window ($Y=1$)**
$$
PT(i, j_b) \le T_{start} + M(1 - Y(i)) \tag{7}
$$

**(8) Pass After Window ($Z=1$)**
$$
PT(i, j_b) \ge T_{end} - M(1 - Z(i)) \tag{8}
$$

**(9) Reroute During Window ($X=1$)**
$$
PT(i, j_b) \ge T_{start} - M(1 - X(i)) \tag{9a}
$$
$$
PT(i, j_b) \le T_{end} + M(1 - X(i)) \tag{9b}
$$

### C. Delay Calculation

**(10) Arrival Delay**
For all $i \in I$, $s \in S(i)$:
$$
DEL\_ARR(i,s) \ge ARR(i,s) - A_{sched}(i,s) \tag{10a}
$$
$$
DEL\_ARR(i,s) \ge 0 \tag{10b}
$$

**(11) Departure Delay**
For all $i \in I$, $s \in S(i)$:
$$
DEL\_DEP(i,s) \ge DEP(i,s) - D_{sched}(i,s) \tag{11a}
$$
$$
DEL\_DEP(i,s) \ge 0 \tag{11b}
$$

### D. Energy Model

**(12) Linear Energy Approximation**
For all $i \in I$, $j \in J(i)$:
$$
E(i,j) = a_E(i,j) \cdot \left( RT_{max}(i,j) - RT(i,j) \right) + b_E(i,j) \tag{12}
$$
*(Shorter $RT$ = faster = higher energy.)*

### E. Conflict Resolution

**(13) Same-Direction Segment Headway**
For all $\{i, i'\} \in P_{seg}(j)$, where $s_{dest}(j)$ is the destination station of segment $j$:
$$
ARR(i, s_{dest}(j)) - ARR(i', s_{dest}(j)) \ge h_{min}(j) - M(1 - H(i,i',j)) \tag{13a}
$$
$$
ARR(i', s_{dest}(j)) - ARR(i, s_{dest}(j)) \ge h_{min}(j) - M \cdot H(i,i',j) \tag{13b}
$$

**(14) Station Platform Non-Overlap**
For all $\{i, i'\} \in P_{stn}(s)$ (same-direction trains stopping at station $s$):
$$
DEP(i,s) - ARR(i',s) \le M(1 - O(i,i',s)) \tag{14a}
$$
$$
DEP(i',s) - ARR(i,s) \le M \cdot O(i,i',s) \tag{14b}
$$

**(15) Bidirectional Conflict on Rerouted Segment**
For all $i \in I_{blk}$, $i' \in I_{opp}$ (trains sharing physical segment $j_b$ in opposite directions):
$$
PT(i, j_b) - PT(i', j_b) \ge h_{opp} - M(1 - B(i,i')) - M(1 - X(i)) \tag{15a}
$$
$$
PT(i', j_b) - PT(i, j_b) \ge h_{opp} - M \cdot B(i,i') - M(1 - X(i)) \tag{15b}
$$
*Explanation: If $X(i)=0$, both constraints are deactivated (RHS $\approx -M$). If $X(i)=1$, the binary $B$ enforces that the midpoint passage times are separated by at least $h_{opp}$.*

### F. Domain and Bounds

**(16) Time Bounds**
$$
0 \le ARR(i,s) \le T_H, \quad 0 \le DEP(i,s) \le T_H \quad \forall i, s \tag{16a}
$$
$$
0 \le RT(i,j) \le RT_{max}(i,j) + \Delta t_{reroute} \quad \forall i, j \tag{16b}
$$
$$
0 \le PT(i,j) \le T_H \quad \forall i, j \tag{16c}
$$
$$
0 \le DEL\_ARR(i,s), DEL\_DEP(i,s) \le T_H \quad \forall i, s \tag{16d}
$$
$$
0 \le E(i,j) \le a_E(i,j) \cdot RT_{max}(i,j) + b_E(i,j) \quad \forall i, j \tag{16e}
$$

**(17) Binary Domains**
$$
X(i), Y(i), Z(i), H(i,i',j), O(i,i',s), B(i,i') \in \{0,1\} \tag{17}
$$

---

## 7. Model Behavior Summary

1.  **Integrated Optimization:** The model simultaneously determines arrival/departure times, running times (speed profiles), rerouting decisions, and train orderings.
2.  **Disruption Handling:** The three-way partition $(X, Y, Z)$ ensures each affected train either reroutes through the disruption window (using the opposite track with a time penalty and bidirectional separation), or is rescheduled to pass before/after the window.
3.  **Energy-Delay Trade-off:** The objective balances delay costs (penalizing late arrivals/departures) against energy costs (penalizing fast running times). The smoothness constraint (4) prevents unrealistic speed profile changes.
4.  **Conflict-Free Guarantee:** Constraints (13)–(15) enforce minimum headways for same-direction trains on segments, platform non-overlap at stations, and bidirectional separation when trains share a track due to rerouting.
5.  **Linearity:** All constraints and the objective are linear, making the model solvable by standard MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP).

# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage
## Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Formulation

### 1. Problem Description
This model addresses the integrated optimization of train timetables and speed profiles following a **partial segment blockage** disruption. Specifically, segment $s^*$ in direction $d^*$ is blocked for a time window $[T_{dis\_start}, T_{dis\_end}]$. Trains in direction $d^*$ must reroute to the opposite track (direction $1-d^*$) during this window, sharing track resources with trains in the opposite direction. The model optimizes arrival/departure times, average speeds, and potential cancellations to minimize total passenger delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties, while ensuring conflict-free operation.

### 2. Assumptions
1.  **Network Structure**: The railway is a single corridor with $N$ stations and $N-1$ segments. Two directions of travel ($d \in \{1, 2\}$).
2.  **Discrete Speed Levels**: To maintain strict linearity in the MILP, average speeds are chosen from a finite set of discrete levels $\mathcal{V}_s$ for each segment $s$. This avoids the non-linearity of $V \cdot T = L$.
3.  **Ordering-Based Conflict Resolution**: Conflicts are resolved using binary ordering variables. If two trains share a segment, one must precede the other by a minimum headway.
4.  **Rerouting Logic**: During the disruption window on $s^*$, trains in direction $d^*$ share the track with trains in direction $1-d^*$. This is handled by applying headway constraints to all pairs of trains on $s^*$ during the disruption.
5.  **Cancellation Propagation**: If a train is cancelled at a station, it is cancelled for all subsequent stations.
6.  **Energy Model**: Energy is approximated as linear in average speed and deviation from nominal speed.
7.  **Big-M Constants**: $M_{time}$ is a sufficiently large constant (e.g., $T_{horizon}$) used for linearization.

---

### 3. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| $K$ | Set of trains, indexed by $k$. |
| $I$ | Set of stations, indexed by $i = 1, \dots, N$. |
| $S$ | Set of segments, indexed by $s = 1, \dots, N-1$. Segment $s$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$. |
| $I_k$ | Ordered set of stations visited by train $k$. |
| $S_k$ | Set of segments traversed by train $k$. |
| $\mathcal{V}_s$ | Set of discrete speed levels for segment $s$. |
| $K_{d^*}$ | Set of trains traveling in direction $d^*$. |
| $K_{1-d^*}$ | Set of trains traveling in direction $1-d^*$. |
| $K_{s^*}$ | Set of trains that traverse segment $s^*$. |
| $P_{k,k',s}$ | Set of pairs $(k, k')$ that share segment $s$ and require ordering. |

**Notation:**
*   $origin(k)$: First station in $I_k$.
*   $dest(k)$: Last station in $I_k$.
*   $next(i, k)$: Station immediately following $i$ in train $k$'s route.
*   $seg(i, k)$: Segment connecting $i$ and $next(i, k)$.

---

### 4. Parameters

**Time and Capacity:**
*   $T_{horizon}$: Planning horizon.
*   $M_{time}$: Big-M constant for time ($M_{time} = T_{horizon}$).
*   $t_{arr}^{nom}(k, i)$: Nominal arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$.
*   $t_{dep}^{nom}(k, i)$: Nominal departure time of train $k$ from station $i$.
*   $t_{stop}^{min}(k, i), t_{stop}^{max}(k, i)$: Min/max dwell time at station $i$ for train $k$.
*   $t_{sep}^{min}(k, k', s)$: Minimum headway between trains $k$ and $k'$ on segment $s$.

**Segment and Speed:**
*   $L_s$: Length of segment $s$.
*   $V_{min}(s), V_{max}(s)$: Min/max permissible speed on segment $s$.
*   $V_{nom}(k, s)$: Nominal average speed of train $k$ on segment $s$.
*   $V_{dis}(s^*)$: Reduced max speed on $s^*$ during disruption (if applicable).

**Disruption:**
*   $s^*$: Affected segment.
*   $d^*$: Affected direction.
*   $T_{dis\_start}, T_{dis\_end}$: Disruption time window.

**Energy Coefficients:**
*   $c_1$: Drag energy coefficient.
*   $c_2$: Deviation energy coefficient.

**Objective Weights:**
*   $\alpha = 1$: Weight for delay.
*   $\beta = 0.1$: Weight for energy.
*   $\gamma = 100$: Weight for cancellation.

---

### 5. Decision Variables

**Continuous Variables:**
*   $t_{arr}(k, i) \ge 0$: Arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$.
*   $t_{dep}(k, i) \ge 0$: Departure time of train $k$ from station $i$.
*   $T_{run}(k, s) \ge 0$: Running time of train $k$ on segment $s$.
*   $V_{avg}(k, s) \ge 0$: Average speed of train $k$ on segment $s$.
*   $Delay_k \ge 0$: Delay of train $k$ at its destination.
*   $Dev^+(k, s) \ge 0$: Positive deviation of $V_{avg}(k, s)$ from $V_{nom}(k, s)$.
*   $Dev^-(k, s) \ge 0$: Negative deviation of $V_{avg}(k, s)$ from $V_{nom}(k, s)$.

**Binary Variables:**
*   $x(k, i) \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ is cancelled at or before station $i$.
*   $u(k, s, v) \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses speed level $v \in \mathcal{V}_s$ on segment $s$.
*   $o(k, k', s) \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ precedes train $k'$ on segment $s$.

---

### 6. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of delay, energy, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min Z = \alpha \sum_{k \in K} Delay_k + \beta \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S_k} E(k, s) + \gamma \sum_{k \in K} x(k, dest(k))
$$

Where energy $E(k, s)$ is:
$$
E(k, s) = c_1 L_s V_{avg}(k, s) + c_2 L_s (Dev^+(k, s) + Dev^-(k, s))
$$

Substituting $E(k, s)$:
$$
\min Z = \alpha \sum_{k \in K} Delay_k + \beta \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{s \in S_k} \left[ c_1 L_s V_{avg}(k, s) + c_2 L_s (Dev^+(k, s) + Dev^-(k, s)) \right] + \gamma \sum_{k \in K} x(k, dest(k))
$$

---

### 7. Constraints

#### 7.1 Speed Selection and Running Time

**1. Speed Level Selection:**
$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_s} u(k, s, v) = 1 \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

**2. Average Speed Definition:**
$$
V_{avg}(k, s) = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_s} v \cdot u(k, s, v) \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

**3. Running Time Definition:**
$$
T_{run}(k, s) = \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_s} \frac{L_s}{v} \cdot u(k, s, v) \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

**4. Speed Bounds:**
$$
V_{min}(s) \le V_{avg}(k, s) \le V_{max}(s) \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

**5. Disruption Speed Restriction:**
For trains $k \in K_{d^*}$ traversing $s^*$ during $[T_{dis\_start}, T_{dis\_end}]$:
$$
V_{avg}(k, s^*) \le V_{dis}(s^*) \quad \forall k \in K_{d^*} \cap K_{s^*}
$$
*(If $V_{dis}(s^*) = 0$, this forces cancellation or rerouting.)*

#### 7.2 Timetable Consistency

**6. Time Propagation:**
$$
t_{arr}(k, next(i, k)) = t_{dep}(k, i) + T_{run}(k, seg(i, k)) \quad \forall k \in K, i \in I_k \setminus \{dest(k)\}
$$

**7. Dwell Time Constraints:**
$$
t_{dep}(k, i) - t_{arr}(k, i) \ge t_{stop}^{min}(k, i) \quad \forall k \in K, i \in I_k \setminus \{dest(k)\}
$$
$$
t_{dep}(k, i) - t_{arr}(k, i) \le t_{stop}^{max}(k, i) \quad \forall k \in K, i \in I_k \setminus \{dest(k)\}
$$

**8. Destination Arrival Horizon:**
$$
t_{arr}(k, dest(k)) \le T_{horizon} \quad \forall k \in K
$$

#### 7.3 Cancellation Logic

**9. Cancellation Propagation:**
$$
x(k, i') \ge x(k, i) \quad \forall k \in K, i, i' \in I_k, i' > i
$$

**10. Departure Constraint with Cancellation:**
$$
t_{dep}(k, i) \le M_{time} \cdot (1 - x(k, i)) \quad \forall k \in K, i \in I_k
$$

**11. Arrival Constraint with Cancellation:**
$$
t_{arr}(k, i') \le M_{time} \cdot (1 - x(k, i)) \quad \forall k \in K, i, i' \in I_k, i' > i
$$

**12. Speed Selection with Cancellation:**
If train $k$ is cancelled at or before the origin of segment $s$, it does not traverse $s$:
$$
\sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_s} u(k, s, v) \le 1 - x(k, origin(s)) \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

#### 7.4 Delay Calculation

**13. Delay Definition:**
$$
Delay_k \ge t_{arr}(k, dest(k)) - t_{arr}^{nom}(k, dest(k)) - M_{time} \cdot x(k, dest(k)) \quad \forall k \in K
$$
$$
Delay_k \ge 0 \quad \forall k \in K
$$
*(If cancelled, $x(k, dest(k))=1$, so the RHS is very negative, and $Delay_k=0$.)*

#### 7.5 Energy Deviation Variables

**14. Deviation Definition:**
$$
Dev^+(k, s) - Dev^-(k, s) = V_{avg}(k, s) - V_{nom}(k, s) \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$
$$
Dev^+(k, s) \ge 0, \quad Dev^-(k, s) \ge 0 \quad \forall k \in K, s \in S_k
$$

#### 7.6 Conflict-Free Operation (Ordering Constraints)

**15. Ordering Mutual Exclusivity:**
For any pair $(k, k') \in P_{k,k',s}$:
$$
o(k, k', s) + o(k', k, s) = 1 \quad \forall (k, k') \in P_{k,k',s}, s \in S
$$

**16. Headway Constraints (Same Direction):**
For trains $k, k'$ in the same direction on segment $s$:
$$
t_{dep}(k', origin(s)) - t_{dep}(k, origin(s)) \ge t_{sep}^{min}(k, k', s) - M_{time} \cdot (1 - o(k, k', s)) \quad \forall (k, k') \in P_{k,k',s}, s \in S
$$
$$
t_{dep}(k, origin(s)) - t_{dep}(k', origin(s)) \ge t_{sep}^{min}(k', k, s) - M_{time} \cdot (1 - o(k', k, s)) \quad \forall (k, k') \in P_{k,k',s}, s \in S
$$

**17. Headway Constraints (Opposite Direction on Disrupted Segment):**
For trains $k \in K_{d^*}$ and $k' \in K_{1-d^*}$ on segment $s^*$ during the disruption:
$$
t_{dep}(k', origin(s^*)) - t_{dep}(k, origin(s^*)) \ge t_{sep}^{min}(k, k', s^*) - M_{time} \cdot (1 - o(k, k', s^*)) \quad \forall k \in K_{d^*} \cap K_{s^*}, k' \in K_{1-d^*} \cap K_{s^*}
$$
$$
t_{dep}(k, origin(s^*)) - t_{dep}(k', origin(s^*)) \ge t_{sep}^{min}(k', k, s^*) - M_{time} \cdot (1 - o(k', k, s^*)) \quad \forall k \in K_{d^*} \cap K_{s^*}, k' \in K_{1-d^*} \cap K_{s^*}
$$

**18. Cancellation Relaxation for Ordering:**
If either train is cancelled, the headway constraint is relaxed:
$$
t_{dep}(k', origin(s)) - t_{dep}(k, origin(s)) \ge t_{sep}^{min}(k, k', s) - M_{time} \cdot (1 - o(k, k', s)) - M_{time} \cdot (x(k, origin(s)) + x(k', origin(s))) \quad \forall (k, k') \in P_{k,k',s}, s \in S
$$
*(Similar for the reverse ordering.)*

#### 7.7 Non-Negativity and Domain

**19. Variable Domains:**
$$
t_{arr}(k, i), t_{dep}(k, i), T_{run}(k, s), V_{avg}(k, s), Delay_k, Dev^+(k, s), Dev^-(k, s) \ge 0
$$
$$
x(k, i), u(k, s, v), o(k, k', s) \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

### 8. Implementation Notes

1.  **Discrete Speeds**: The set $\mathcal{V}_s$ should include enough levels to capture meaningful speed variations (e.g., 5-10 levels). This ensures the model remains a MILP.
2.  **Big-M Values**: $M_{time} = T_{horizon}$ is typically sufficient. Ensure $M_{time}$ is not too large to avoid numerical instability.
3.  **Ordering Variables**: The number of ordering variables can be large. Symmetry breaking can be applied by fixing $o(k, k', s) = 1$ for $k < k'$ if their nominal times do not overlap.
4.  **Disruption Handling**: The disruption is handled by restricting speed levels on $s^*$ for trains in direction $d^*$ and applying headway constraints between opposite-direction trains on $s^*$.
5.  **Solver**: This model can be solved using commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) or open-source solvers (CBC, SCIP).

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage Disruptions

## 1. Problem Context and Assumptions

This model addresses the integrated optimization of train timetables and speed profiles in a high-speed railway corridor following a partial segment blockage disruption. During the disruption, one direction of a track segment is blocked, forcing affected trains to reroute to the opposite track, creating bidirectional conflicts on shared track resources. The model simultaneously optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, potential cancellation, and speed profiles (via running time and energy consumption).

**Key Assumptions:**
1. The network is a linear corridor with stations in sequential order.
2. Energy consumption is linearly approximated as a decreasing function of running time (faster = more energy).
3. Headway requirements are fixed safety separation times.
4. All trains have identical speed capabilities (min/max running times are segment-dependent but train-independent for simplification).
5. The model horizon spans from just before the disruption to a recovery time after it ends.
6. Waiting due to conflicts is captured implicitly through extended dwell times at stations (bounded by max dwell).
7. The disruption blocks one direction of one specific segment during a fixed time window $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$.
8. Passenger delay is measured as the sum of positive deviations of rescheduled arrival times from scheduled arrival times at all served stations.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|-----|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of all trains, $I = \{1, 2, \dots, N\}$ |
| $I^+$ | Subset of trains traveling in the "up" (forward) direction |
| $I^-$ | Subset of trains traveling in the "down" (backward) direction |
| $S$ | Set of stations, $S = \{1, 2, \dots, N_S\}$, ordered sequentially |
| $E$ | Set of track segments (blocks), $E = \{e_1, e_2, \dots, e_{N_S-1}\}$, where $e_k$ connects station $k$ and station $k+1$ |
| $S_i$ | Set of stations served by train $i$ |
| $E_i$ | Set of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $e^*$ | The specific disrupted segment |
| $s_{start}^*$, $s_{end}^*$ | Start and end stations of segment $e^*$ ($e^*$ connects $s_{start}^*$ to $s_{end}^*$) |
| $I_{e^*}^+$ | Set of up-direction trains traversing segment $e^*$ |
| $I_{e^*}^-$ | Set of down-direction trains traversing segment $e^*$ |
| $P_s$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{i,j\}$ of distinct trains both serving station $s$ (same direction) |
| $Q_e$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{i,j\}$ of distinct trains both traversing segment $e$ in the same direction |
| $R_{e^*}$ | Set of ordered pairs $(i,j)$ with $i \in I_{e^*}^+$, $j \in I_{e^*}^-$ (bidirectional pairs in disrupted segment) |
| $K = \{N, R\}$ | Track options in the disruption area: $N$ = normal track, $R$ = rerouted (opposite) track |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s}^{sch}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}^{sch}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,e}^{min}$ | Minimum feasible running time for train $i$ on segment $e$ (max speed, max acceleration/braking) |
| $\tau_{i,e}^{max}$ | Maximum feasible running time for train $i$ on segment $e$ (min speed) |
| $w_{i,s}^{min}$ | Minimum dwell time for train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_{i,s}^{max}$ | Maximum dwell time for train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{same}$ | Minimum headway (time separation) between consecutive trains in the same direction on a segment |
| $h^{opp}$ | Minimum headway (time separation) between trains in opposite directions sharing a track (bidirectional conflict) |
| $T_{start}$, $T_{end}$ | Start and end times of the disruption window |
| $c_{delay}$ | Cost weight per unit time of passenger delay |
| $c_{energy}$ | Cost weight per unit of energy consumption |
| $c_{cancel}$ | Penalty cost for canceling a train |
| $c_{route}$ | Penalty cost for rerouting a train through the disruption area |
| $E_{max,i,e}$ | Energy consumption at minimum running time $\tau_{i,e}^{min}$ (maximum speed) |
| $\lambda_{i,e}$ | Linear energy reduction rate per unit time added to running time on segment $e$ ($>0$) |
| $\epsilon$ | Small positive separation constant (e.g., 1 second) to enforce strict ordering |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large constant (Big-M), set to the planning horizon length |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### 4.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,s} \geq 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Rescheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s} \geq 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Rescheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,e} \geq 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Rescheduled running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $del_{i,s} \geq 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Positive arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $En_{i,e} \geq 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Energy consumption cost for train $i$ on segment $e$ |

### 4.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $y_i \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is canceled, 0 otherwise |
| $x_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ before train $j$ (for $i,j$ same direction at $s$) |
| $u_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ enters segment $e$ before train $j$ (for $i,j$ same direction on $e$) |
| $z_{i,N} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the normal track in segment $e^*$ (applies to $I_{e^*}^+$) |
| $z_{i,R} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the rerouted (opposite) track in segment $e^*$ (applies to $I_{e^*}^+$) |
| $z_{j,N} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $j$ uses its normal track in segment $e^*$ (applies to $I_{e^*}^-$) |
| $z_{j,R} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $j$ uses the rerouted track in segment $e^*$ (applies to $I_{e^*}^-$) |
| $v_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if up-train $i$ exits the disrupted segment before down-train $j$ enters (bidirectional ordering) |
| $b_i \in \{0,1\}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if up-train $i$ passes segment $e^*$ entirely before $T_{start}$; 0 if entirely after $T_{end}$ (only relevant if $z_{i,N}=1$) |

**Note on track variables:** For up-trains $i \in I_{e^*}^+$, the normal track is Track 1 (up-direction track). The rerouted track is Track 2 (down-direction track). For down-trains $j \in I_{e^*}^-$, the normal track is Track 2. The rerouted track is Track 1.

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted cost:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{c_{delay} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S_i} del_{i,s}}_{\text{Passenger Delay Cost}} + \underbrace{c_{energy} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{e \in E_i} En_{i,e}}_{\text{Energy Consumption Cost}} + \underbrace{c_{cancel} \sum_{i \in I} y_i}_{\text{Cancellation Penalty}} + \underbrace{c_{route} \sum_{i \in I_{e^*}^+} z_{i,R} + c_{route} \sum_{j \in I_{e^*}^-} z_{j,R}}_{\text{Rerouting Penalty}}
$$

**Interpretation:**
- **Delay cost** penalizes deviation from the original timetable.
- **Energy cost** captures the trade-off: running faster (shorter $\tau$) saves delay but increases energy; running slower (longer $\tau$) saves energy but may increase delay.
- **Cancellation penalty** discourages service removal.
- **Rerouting penalty** reflects the operational complexity/cost of using the alternate track.

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1. Train Cancellation Logic

If train $i$ is canceled, its timing variables are deactivated.

$$
a_{i,s} \leq M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \leq M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

$$
\tau_{i,e} \leq M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

$$
del_{i,s} \leq M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

$$
En_{i,e} \leq M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

*(If $y_i = 1$, all associated variables are forced to 0, effectively removing the train from the timeline.)*

---

### 6.2. Running Time Bounds (Speed Feasibility)

The running time on each segment must lie within physically feasible limits determined by speed profiles (maximum speed, maximum acceleration, maximum braking):

$$
\tau_{i,e}^{min}\,(1 - y_i) \;\leq\; \tau_{i,e} \;\leq\; \tau_{i,e}^{max}\,(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

*(If $y_i=1$, both sides are 0, consistent with $\tau_{i,e}=0$.)*

---

### 6.3. Dwell Time Constraints

At each intermediate station, the dwell time must be within operational bounds:

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\geq\; w_{i,s}^{min}\,(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i \setminus \{s_{origin}^i, s_{dest}^i\}
$$

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\leq\; w_{i,s}^{max}\,(1 - y_i) + M \cdot y_i \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i \setminus \{s_{origin}^i, s_{dest}^i\}
$$

*(If $y_i=1$, both reduce to $0 \leq 0$, which is satisfied. The upper bound allows extended dwell for conflict-induced waiting, bounded by $w_{i,s}^{max}$.)*

**Extended dwell allowance for disruption:** To accommodate waiting due to bidirectional conflicts, we relax the upper bound at stations adjacent to the disrupted segment:

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \;\leq\; w_{i,s}^{max} + M \cdot \delta_{s,s^*} \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in \{s_{start}^*, s_{end}^*\}
$$

where $\delta_{s,s^*}=1$ if station $s$ is at the boundary of the disrupted segment, 0 otherwise. *(This allows extended waiting at the entry/exit of the disruption zone.)*

---

### 6.4. Flow Consistency (Time Linkage)

For each train $i$ and each segment $e$ in its route, the arrival at the next station equals the departure from the previous station plus the running time:

**For up-direction trains ($i \in I^+$), segment $e_k$ connecting station $k$ to station $k+1$:**

$$
a_{i,k+1} \;=\; d_{i,k} + \tau_{i,e_k} \quad \forall\, i \in I^+,\; e_k \in E_i
$$

**For down-direction trains ($i \in I^-$), segment $e_k$ connecting station $k+1$ to station $k$:**

$$
a_{i,k} \;=\; d_{i,k+1} + \tau_{i,e_k} \quad \forall\, i \in I^-,\; e_k \in E_i
$$

*(These hold when $y_i=0$; when $y_i=1$, all variables are 0 and $0=0+0$ is satisfied.)*

---

### 6.5. Origin/Destination Anchoring

Each train's departure from its origin station and arrival at its destination are anchored (with possible delay):

$$
d_{i,s_{origin}^i} \;\geq\; d_{i,s_{origin}^i}^{sch}\,(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

$$
a_{i,s_{dest}^i} \;\geq\; a_{i,s_{dest}^i}^{sch}\,(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i \in I
$$

*(Trains cannot depart their origin or arrive at their destination earlier than scheduled.)*

---

### 6.6. Passenger Delay Definition

The positive delay at each station is the excess of actual arrival over scheduled arrival:

$$
del_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{sch} \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

$$
del_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

*(In the optimal solution, $del_{i,s} = \max(0,\; a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{sch})$.)*

---

### 6.7. Energy Consumption Coupling

Energy consumption is linearly approximated as a decreasing function of running time (slower speed = less energy):

$$
En_{i,e} \;\geq\; E_{max,i,e} \;-\; \lambda_{i,e}\!\left(\tau_{i,e} - \tau_{i,e}^{min}\right) \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

$$
En_{i,e} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

$$
En_{i,e} \;\leq\; E_{max,i,e} \quad \forall\, i \in I,\; e \in E_i
$$

**Interpretation:**
- At $\tau_{i,e} = \tau_{i,e}^{min}$ (fastest), $En_{i,e} \geq E_{max,i,e}$ (maximum energy).
- At $\tau_{i,e} = \tau_{i,e}^{max}$ (slowest), $En_{i,e} \geq E_{max,i,e} - \lambda_{i,e}(\tau_{i,e}^{max} - \tau_{i,e}^{min})$ (minimum energy).
- Since the objective minimizes $En_{i,e}$ with a positive coefficient, the constraint is tight at the lower bound in the optimal solution.
- The coefficient $\lambda_{i,e} > 0$ represents the marginal energy saving per second of additional running time.

---

### 6.8. Passing Order at Stations (Reordering)

For each station $s$ and each pair of same-direction trains $\{i,j\} \in P_s$, one must depart before the other:

$$
d_{i,s} + \epsilon \;\leq\; d_{j,s} + M\!\left(1 - x_{i,j,s} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in P_s,\; s
$$

$$
d_{j,s} + \epsilon \;\leq\; d_{i,s} + M\!\left(x_{i,j,s} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in P_s,\; s
$$

$$
x_{i,j,s} + x_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in P_s,\; s
$$

**Interpretation:**
- If $x_{i,j,s}=1$ (i departs before j): the first constraint is tight ($d_{i,s} + \epsilon \leq d_{j,s}$), and the second is relaxed.
- If $x_{i,j,s}=0$ (j departs before i): the second constraint is tight, and the first is relaxed.
- The terms $y_i, y_j$ deactivate the constraints if either train is canceled.

---

### 6.9. Segment Occupancy / Headway Constraints (Same Direction)

For each segment $e$ and each pair of same-direction trains $\{i,j\} \in Q_e$, they cannot occupy the segment simultaneously:

$$
d_{i,s_{start}(e)} + \tau_{i,e} + h^{same} \;\leq\; d_{j,s_{start}(e)} + M\!\left(1 - u_{i,j,e} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in Q_e
$$

$$
d_{j,s_{start}(e)} + \tau_{j,e} + h^{same} \;\leq\; d_{i,s_{start}(e)} + M\!\left(u_{i,j,e} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in Q_e
$$

$$
u_{i,j,e} + u_{j,i,e} = 1 \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in Q_e
$$

**Interpretation:**
- Train $i$ must fully exit the segment (plus headway $h^{same}$) before train $j$ enters, or vice versa.
- The entry time to segment $e$ is the departure from $s_{start}(e)$; the exit time is $d_{i,s_{start}(e)} + \tau_{i,e}$.

**Consistency between station order and segment order:**
If train $i$ departs station $s_{start}(e)$ before train $j$, it must enter segment $e$ before $j$:

$$
x_{i,j,s_{start}(e)} \;\geq\; u_{i,j,e} \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in Q_e
$$

$$
x_{j,i,s_{start}(e)} \;\geq\; u_{j,i,e} \quad \forall\, \{i,j\} \in Q_e
$$

*(This prevents order reversals within a block.)*

---

### 6.10. Track Assignment in the Disrupted Segment

**For up-direction trains ($i \in I_{e^*}^+$):**

$$
z_{i,N} + z_{i,R} = 1 \quad \forall\, i \in I_{e^*}^+
$$

**For down-direction trains ($j \in I_{e^*}^-$):**

$$
z_{j,N} + z_{j,R} = 1 \quad \forall\, j \in I_{e^*}^-
$$

---

### 6.11. Blockage Constraint (Normal Track Unavailable for Blocked Direction)

Up-direction trains using the normal track ($z_{i,N}=1$) must pass segment $e^*$ entirely before $T_{start}$ or entirely after $T_{end}$ (they cannot be on the blocked track during the disruption window):

Introduce binary $b_i \in \{0,1\}$: $b_i = 1$ if train $i$ exits before $T_{start}$, $b_i = 0$ if train $i$ enters after $T_{end}$.

$$
d_{i,s_{start}^*} + \tau_{i,e^*} \;\leq\; T_{start} + M(1 - b_i) + M(1 - z_{i,N}) \quad \forall\, i \in I_{e^*}^+
$$

$$
d_{i,s_{start}^*} \;\geq\; T_{end} - M \cdot b_i - M(1 - z_{i,N}) \quad \forall\, i \in I_{e^*}^+
$$

**Interpretation:**
- If $z_{i,N} = 0$ (rerouted), the $M(1-z_{i,N}) = M$ term makes both constraints inactive (always satisfied).
- If $z_{i,N} = 1$ (normal track), then $M(1-z_{i,N}) = 0$, and the constraints force:
  - If $b_i=1$: exit before $T_{start}$.
  - If $b_i=0$: enter after $T_{end}$.
- If neither timing is feasible, the solver is forced to set $z_{i,N}=0$ (i.e., $z_{i,R}=1$, reroute).

**Forced rerouting for trains that cannot avoid the window:**
If the earliest possible exit and latest possible entry do not allow a valid "before" or "after" passage, the model naturally forces $z_{i,R}=1$.

---

### 6.12. Bidirectional Conflict Constraints on Shared Track (Core of Disruption Handling)

**Conflict Scenario:** An up-train $i$ rerouted to Track 2 ($z_{i,R}=1$) and a down-train $j$ staying on Track 2 ($z_{j,N}=1$) share the same physical track in segment $e^*$ and must not be on it simultaneously.

**Entry/Exit times:**
- Up-train $i$ enters $e^*$ at time $d_{i,s_{start}^*}$ and exits at $d_{i,s_{start}^*} + \tau_{i,e^*}$.
- Down-train $j$ enters $e^*$ (from the other end) at time $d_{j,s_{end}^*}$ and exits at $d_{j,s_{end}^*} + \tau_{j,e^*}$.

**Separation constraints** (active only if both are on Track 2, i.e., $z_{i,R}=1$ and $z_{j,N}=1$):

$$
d_{i,s_{start}^*} + \tau_{i,e^*} + h^{opp} \;\leq\; d_{j,s_{end}^*} + M\!\left(1 - v_{i,j} + 1 - z_{i,R} + 1 - z_{j,N} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, (i,j) \in R_{e^*}
$$

$$
d_{j,s_{end}^*} + \tau_{j,e^*} + h^{opp} \;\leq\; d_{i,s_{start}^*} + M\!\left(v_{i,j} + 1 - z_{i,R} + 1 - z_{j,N} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, (i,j) \in R_{e^*}
$$

**Interpretation:**
- If $z_{i,R}=1$ and $z_{j,N}=1$ (both on Track 2), the Big-M terms $M(1-z_{i,R}) + M(1-z_{j,N}) = 0$, and the constraints enforce strict temporal separation: either $i$ exits (plus $h^{opp}$) before $j$ enters, or $j$ exits (plus $h^{opp}$) before $i$ enters.
- If $z_{i,R}=0$ (up-train on Track 1) or $z_{j,N}=0$ (down-train on Track 1), the Big-M terms are large, deactivating the constraint (no conflict since they are on different tracks).
- The variable $v_{i,j}$ determines the passing order: $v_{i,j}=1$ means $i$ clears the segment before $j$ enters; $v_{i,j}=0$ means $j$ clears before $i$ enters.

**Symmetric conflict (both rerouted to Track 1):**
If a down-train $j$ reroutes to Track 1 ($z_{j,R}=1$) and an up-train $i$ stays on Track 1 ($z_{i,N}=1$), they share Track 1. The same structure applies:

$$
d_{i,s_{start}^*} + \tau_{i,e^*} + h^{opp} \;\leq\; d_{j,s_{end}^*} + M\!\left(1 - v_{j,i} + 1 - z_{i,N} + 1 - z_{j,R} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, (i,j) \in R_{e^*}
$$

$$
d_{j,s_{end}^*} + \tau_{j,e^*} + h^{opp} \;\leq\; d_{i,s_{start}^*} + M\!\left(v_{j,i} + 1 - z_{i,N} + 1 - z_{j,R} + y_i + y_j\right) \quad \forall\, (i,j) \in R_{e^*}
$$

---

### 6.3. Non-Anticipation / Horizon Bounds

All times must fall within the planning horizon $[0, T_{horizon}]$:

$$
a_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0, \quad d_{i,s} \;\geq\; 0 \quad \forall\, i, s
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_{horizon}(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i, s
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_{horizon}(1 - y_i) \quad \forall\, i, s
$$

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Variables | Constraints | Role |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|------|
| **Retiming** | $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ | Flow consistency, dwell time, origin/dest anchoring | Adjust train schedule |
| **Reordering** | $x_{i,j,s}$ | Passing order at stations | Modify passing sequence |
| **Speed Management** | $\tau_{i,e}, En_{i,e}$ | Running time bounds, energy coupling | Optimize speed profiles / energy |
| **Rerouting** | $z_{i,N}, z_{i,R}$ | Track assignment, blockage constraint | Choose track in disruption zone |
| **Cancellation** | $y_i$ | Deactivation constraints | Remove trains if necessary |
| **Bidirectional Conflict** | $v_{i,j}$, $b_i$ | Shared-track separation | Resolve conflicts on shared track |

**Objective:** Minimize total cost = delay + energy + cancellation + rerouting penalties.

**Key Feature:** The model integrates the train rescheduling problem (timetable, order, route, cancellation) with the train speed management problem (running times, energy consumption) in a single MILP. The bidirectional conflict constraints in the disruption area are the coupling mechanism that forces coordination between the two problem layers, ensuring the rescheduled timetable is feasible at the speed/control level while maintaining energy efficiency.

---

## 8. Computational Notes

- The model is NP-hard due to the combinatorial nature of ordering, rerouting, and cancellation decisions.
- The Big-M formulation can be tightened using problem-specific bounds to improve solver performance.
- For large-scale instances (hundreds of trains, dozens of stations), decomposition-based approaches (e.g., Benders decomposition or the train-plan decomposition described in the reference) can be employed to reduce computational complexity.
- The linear energy approximation maintains linearity; for higher accuracy, a piecewise-linear (SOS2) representation can replace the single-slope approximation at the cost of additional variables and constraints.

Text:
Here is the final, complete MILP model for the **Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under partial segment blockage disruptions.

---

# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) Model: TRSMP

## 1. Problem Context and Assumptions

A high-speed railway network experiences a **partial segment blockage**: one track ($k_{dis}$) on one segment ($s_{dis}$) is unavailable during a time window $[d_{start}, d_{end}]$. Affected trains must be rescheduled (retimed, reordered, rerouted to an alternative track, or cancelled) while simultaneously selecting **speed profiles** that minimize energy consumption. The model must ensure a **conflict-free** timetable, including resolution of **bidirectional conflicts** on shared tracks.

**Key Assumptions (marked where made):**

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| A1 | [ASSUMED] The railway line is linear with stations $i=1,\dots,N$ and $M$ parallel tracks per segment. |
| A2 | [ASSUMED] Each train $t$ has a **fixed route** (sequence of stations). Only track selection and timing vary. |
| A3 | [ASSUMED] Track switching is permitted at stations with no additional cost or time penalty. |
| A4 | [ASSUMED] Speed profiles are **pre-computed** discrete sets. Each profile $p$ for segment $s$, track $k$ has a known travel time $C_{s,k,p}$ and energy cost $E_{s,k,p}$. This linearizes the (otherwise nonlinear) physics. |
| A5 | [ASSUMED] The disruption completely prohibits use of track $k_{dis}$ on segment $s_{dis}$ during $[d_{start}, d_{end}]$. A train may still use that track if its traversal is entirely before $d_{start}$ or entirely after $d_{end}$. |
| A6 | [ASSUMED] Headway constraints are the primary conflict mechanism. For same-direction trains on the same track, a minimum time separation $H^{same}$ is required between the departure of the leading train from the segment origin and the departure of the following train. For opposite-direction trains on a single track, one must fully clear the segment before the other enters, requiring separation $H^{opp} \ge \max(T_{t_1,s}, T_{t_2,s}) + \varepsilon$. |
| A7 | [ASSUMED] Dwell times at each station have minimum and maximum bounds $[dmin_i, dmax_i]$. |
| A8 | [ASSUMED] A small subset of trains may be cancelled at a fixed penalty. |
| A9 | [ASSUMED] Passenger delay is measured at each station as the positive part of (actual arrival − scheduled arrival). |
| A10 | [ASSUMED] The planning horizon is $[0, T_{max}]$. All Big-M constants are set to tight bounds derived from $T_{max}$ and network characteristics. |

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, $t \in \mathcal{T}$ |
| $\mathcal{V}_t$ | Ordered set of stations visited by train $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of all (directed) segments; $s = (i, i')$ connects station $i$ to $i'$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_t$ | Ordered set of segments in train $t$'s route, $\mathcal{R}_t \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_s$ | Set of tracks available for segment $s$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_{s,k}$ | Set of pre-computed speed profiles for segment $s$, track $k$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_{s,k}$ | Set of unordered pairs $\{t_1, t_2\} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$, $t_1 \neq t_2$, such that $s \in \mathcal{R}_{t_1}$ and $s \in \mathcal{R}_{t_2}$ (potential conflict pairs) |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\tau^{sch}_{t,v}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $v$ |
| $C_{s,k,p}$ | Travel time (min) for segment $s$, track $k$, profile $p$ |
| $E_{s,k,p}$ | Energy cost (J) for segment $s$, track $k$, profile $p$ |
| $H^{same}$ | Minimum headway (min) for same-direction trains on the same track |
| $H^{opp}$ | Minimum separation (min) for opposite-direction trains on the same track |
| $dmin_v, dmax_v$ | Minimum / maximum dwell time (min) at station $v$ |
| $n^{pass}_t$ | Number of passengers on train $t$ |
| $s_{dis}, k_{dis}$ | Disrupted segment and track indices |
| $d_{start}, d_{end}$ | Disruption time window (min) |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | Objective weights for delay, energy, cancellation |
| $c^{cancel}$ | Fixed cancellation penalty per passenger |
| $T_{max}$ | Planning horizon (min) |
| $M$ | Big-M constant (set to $T_{max}$ or tighter bounds) |
| $\varepsilon$ | Small safety margin (min) |
| $dir(t, s) \in \{+1, -1\}$ | Direction of train $t$ on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Decision Variables

### Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $y_t$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if train $t$ is **cancelled** |
| $x_{t,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if active train $t$ uses **track $k$** on segment $s$ |
| $q_{t,s,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if train $t$ selects **speed profile $p$** on track $k$, segment $s$ |
| $z_{t_1,t_2,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $1$ if train $t_1$ **enters before** $t_2$ on track $k$, segment $s$ (defined for $t_1 < t_2$) |
| $w_{t,s_{dis}}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Disruption auxiliary: $1$ if train $t$ **exits** $s_{dis}$ before $d_{start}$; $0$ if it **enters** $s_{dis}$ after $d_{end}$ |

### Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|----------|--------|---------|
| $Arr_{t,v} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Actual **arrival** time of train $t$ at station $v$ |
| $Dep_{t,v} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Actual **departure** time of train $t$ from station $v$ |
| $Trv_{t,s} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | Actual **travel time** of train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $Del_{t,v} \ge 0$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | **Delay** of train $t$ at station $v$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\boxed{
\min \; Z \;=\;
\alpha \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} n^{pass}_t \sum_{v \in \mathcal{V}_t} Del_{t,v}
\;+\;
\beta \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_t} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_s} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{s,k}} E_{s,k,p} \, q_{t,s,k,p}
\;+\;
\gamma \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} c^{cancel} \, n^{pass}_t \, y_t
}
$$

| Term | Rationale |
|------|-----------|
| **Passenger-weighted delay** | Sum of positive delay at every station, weighted by onboard passengers |
| **Energy consumption** | Sum of energy of the selected speed profile on every traversed segment |
| **Cancellation penalty** | Fixed cost per cancelled train, scaled by passenger count |

---

## 6. Constraints

### Group A — Cancellation and Track Assignment

**A1. Inactivate cancelled trains:**
$$
x_{t,s,k} \le 1 - y_t \quad \forall\; t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t,\; k \in \mathcal{K}_s
$$

**A2. Exactly one track per segment (active trains):**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_s} x_{t,s,k} = 1 - y_t \quad \forall\; t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t
$$

**A3. Bounds on times for active trains:**
$$
Arr_{t,v} \le T_{max}(1 - y_t), \qquad Dep_{t,v} \le T_{max}(1 - y_t) \quad \forall\; t, v
$$

---

### Group B — Speed Profile Selection and Travel Time

**B1. Exactly one profile per used track:**
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{s,k}} q_{t,s,k,p} = x_{t,s,k} \quad \forall\; t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t,\; k \in \mathcal{K}_s
$$

**B2. Travel time equals selected profile's time:**
$$
Trv_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_s} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{s,k}} C_{s,k,p} \; q_{t,s,k,p} \quad \forall\; t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{R}_t
$$
*(This is linear because $C_{s,k,p}$ is a parameter.)*

---

### Group C — Time Propagation (Station-to-Station)

Let $v_{orig}(s)$ and $v_{dest}(s)$ denote the origin and destination stations of segment $s$. For train $t$ traversing $s \in \mathcal{R}_t$:

**C1. Arrival at destination = Departure from origin + Travel time:**
$$
Arr_{t,\,v_{dest}(s)} \;\ge\; Dep_{t,\,v_{orig}(s)} + Trv_{t,s} \;-\; M \, y_t
$$
$$
Arr_{t,\,v_{dest}(s)} \;\le\; Dep_{t,\,v_{orig}(s)} + Trv_{t,s} \;+\; M \, y_t
$$
*(For active trains, $y_t=0$, this is an **equality**.)*

**C2. Dwell time bounds at intermediate stations** $v \in \mathcal{V}_t \setminus \{v_{last}\}$:
$$
Dep_{t,v} - Arr_{t,v} \;\ge\; dmin_v \;-\; M\, y_t
$$
$$
Dep_{t,v} - Arr_{t,v} \;\le\; dmax_v \;+\; M\, y_t
$$

**C3. Initial departure (at the first station $v_{first}$ of train $t$):**
$$
Dep_{t,\,v_{first}} \;\ge\; \tau^{sch}_{t,\,v_{first}} \;-\; M\, y_t
$$
$$
Dep_{t,\,v_{first}} \;\le\; \tau^{sch}_{t,\,v_{first}} \;+\; M\, y_t
$$

---

### Group D — Delay Calculation

**D1. Delay is the positive part of (actual − scheduled):**
$$
Del_{t,v} \;\ge\; Arr_{t,v} - \tau^{sch}_{t,v} - M\, y_t \quad \forall\; t, v
$$
$$
Del_{t,v} \;\ge\; 0
$$
*(If $y_t = 1$, the first constraint becomes $Del \ge -M$, redundant. The objective drives $Del$ to 0.)*

---

### Group E — Conflict Resolution (Headway Constraints)

For each potential conflict pair $\{t_1, t_2\} \in \mathcal{C}_{s,k}$ ($t_1 < t_2$), segment $s$, track $k$:

**E1. Ordering linkage** — enforce exactly one ordering when both trains use track $k$:
$$
z_{t_1,t_2,s,k} + z_{t_2,t_1,s,k} \;\le\; x_{t_1,s,k} \tag{E1a}
$$
$$
z_{t_1,t_2,s,k} + z_{t_2,t_1,s,k} \;\le\; x_{t_2,s,k} \tag{E1b}
$$
$$
z_{t_1,t_2,s,k} + z_{t_2,t_1,s,k} \;\ge\; x_{t_1,s,k} + x_{t_2,s,k} - 1 \tag{E1c}
$$

> *Verification:* If both $x=1$: sum $=1$ (exactly one ordering). If one $x=0$: sum $=0$ (no ordering needed). If both $x=0$: sum $=0$.

**E2. Headway enforcement (same direction, $dir(t_1,s)=dir(t_2,s)$):**

If $z_{t_1,t_2,s,k}=1$ ($t_1$ goes first), $t_2$ must depart the segment origin at least $H^{same}$ after $t_1$:
$$
Dep_{t_2,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;-\; Dep_{t_1,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;\ge\; H^{same} \;-\; M(1 - z_{t_1,t_2,s,k}) \tag{E2a}
$$
$$
Dep_{t_1,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;-\; Dep_{t_2,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;\ge\; H^{same} \;-\; M(1 - z_{t_2,t_1,s,k}) \tag{E2b}
$$

**E3. Separation enforcement (opposite direction, $dir(t_1,s)\neq dir(t_2,s)$):**

If $t_1$ goes first, $t_2$ may only enter the segment **after** $t_1$ has **exited** (arrived at the far end). The required separation is $H^{opp} = C_{t_1}^{max} + \varepsilon$, where $C_{t_1}^{max} = \max_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{s,k}} C_{s,k,p}$ is the longest possible travel time of $t_1$ on $s$:

$$
Dep_{t_2,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;-\; Dep_{t_1,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;\ge\; H^{opp} \;-\; M(1 - z_{t_1,t_2,s,k}) \tag{E3a}
$$
$$
Dep_{t_1,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;-\; Dep_{t_2,\,v_{orig}(s)} \;\ge\; H^{opp} \;-\; M(1 - z_{t_2,t_1,s,k}) \tag{E3b}
$$

> *Note:* For opposite-direction trains, the "origin" of each train's segment differs ($v_{orig}$ for $t_1$ is $v_{dest}$ for $t_2$). The constraint is written in terms of each train's own departure from its own segment origin. The Big-M relaxation ensures inactivity when $z=0$.

---

### Group F — Disruption Constraint (Partial Segment Blockage)

For any train $t$ that may use track $k_{dis}$ on segment $s_{dis}$:

**F1. Disjunction via auxiliary binary $w_{t}$:**

If $x_{t, s_{dis}, k_{dis}} = 1$, the train's traversal of $s_{dis}$ must not overlap $[d_{start}, d_{end}]$. That is:
$$
\bigl(\text{Exit before } d_{start}\bigr) \;\;\text{OR}\;\; \bigl(\text{Enter after } d_{end}\bigr)
$$

Let $v_o = v_{orig}(s_{dis})$ and $v_d = v_{dest}(s_{dis})$ (relative to train $t$'s direction).

$$
Arr_{t, v_d} \;\le\; d_{start} \;+\; M(1 - w_t) \;+\; M(1 - x_{t, s_{dis}, k_{dis}}) \tag{F1a}
$$
$$
Dep_{t, v_o} \;\ge\; d_{end} \;-\; M \, w_t \;+\; M(1 - x_{t, s_{dis}, k_{dis}}) \tag{F1b}
$$

> *Logic:*
> - If $x = 0$: both constraints are fully relaxed ($+M$ terms). No restriction.
> - If $x = 1,\; w = 1$: (F1a) forces $Arr \le d_{start}$ (train exits before disruption); (F1b) is relaxed.
> - If $x = 1,\; w = 0$: (F1b) forces $Dep \ge d_{end}$ (train enters after disruption); (F1a) is relaxed.

---

## 7. Model Summary

| Component | Count (per instance) | Type |
|-----------|---------------------|------|
| Cancellation vars $y_t$ | $|\mathcal{T}|$ | Binary |
| Track assignment vars $x_{t,s,k}$ | $\sum_t \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_t} |\mathcal{K}_s|$ | Binary |
| Profile selection vars $q_{t,s,k,p}$ | $\sum_t \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_t} \sum_{k} |\mathcal{P}_{s,k}|$ | Binary |
| Ordering vars $z_{t_1,t_2,s,k}$ | $\sum_{s,k} |\mathcal{C}_{s,k}| \times 2$ | Binary |
| Disruption vars $w_t$ | $|\mathcal{T}|$ (trains on $s_{dis}$) | Binary |
| Time vars $Arr, Dep$ | $\sum_t |\mathcal{V}_t| \times 2$ | Continuous |
| Travel time vars $Trv$ | $\sum_t |\mathcal{R}_t|$ | Continuous |
| Delay vars $Del$ | $\sum_t |\mathcal{V}_t|$ | Continuous |

**Key structural features:**

1. **Integrated timetable + speed profiles:** The coupling between $q$ (profile) and $Trv$ (travel time) links the speed-management layer to the scheduling layer in a single MILP.
2. **Conflict-free guarantee:** The disjunctive headway constraints (Group E) with ordering variables $z$ ensure no two trains on the same track/segment violate the required time separation, for both same-direction and opposite-direction (bidirectional) conflicts.
3. **Disruption handling:** The auxiliary binary $w_t$ (Group F) allows trains to use the disrupted track if they can physically avoid the disruption window, maximizing flexibility.
4. **Energy-aware rescheduling:** By selecting among pre-computed profiles with different $(time, energy)$ trade-offs, the model captures the fundamental tension between arriving early (higher energy, possible extended dwell) and arriving late (lower energy, more delay).
5. **Linearity:** All constraints are linear. The nonlinear physics (speed → energy, acceleration/deceleration limits) are absorbed into the pre-computed discrete profile set, preserving MILP tractability.

**Implementation notes:**
- **Tight Big-M:** Set $M$ to the smallest valid bound (e.g., $T_{max} - \min$ time) to improve solver performance.
- **Profile pruning:** Remove dominated profiles (higher time AND higher energy than another profile for the same segment/track).
- **Symmetry breaking:** For ordering variables, one may add $z_{t_1,t_2,s,k} \ge z_{t_2,t_1,s,k}$ when $t_1$ has higher priority to reduce symmetry.
- **Lazy / cutting-plane approach:** For large instances, the headway constraints (Group E) can be generated on-demand when the LP relaxation produces infeasible train overlaps, significantly reducing the initial model size.
